It gives up after 0x20000 iterations with 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_TIMEOUT) and otherwise returns 0.

name: wait_port_1808_ticks
comment: Splits its argument into a tick count (bits 0-21) and a repeat count (bits 22 and above). Each pass reads the counter at I/O port 0x1808, masks it to 24 bits, adds the tick count, and then spins on 0x000002c0 until a full 32-bit read of the same port makes bit 23 of target minus current set. Because the repeat count is only tested after a pass has run, a repeat count of zero still waits once.

name: usec_to_port_1808_ticks
comment: Multiplies its argument by 0x369E99, divides by 1000000 with a 64x64-to-128 multiply by 0x431BDE82D7B634DB and an 18-bit shift, passes the quotient to 0x954 and returns its argument unchanged. The call sites in this module pass 0xF and 0x1388 (5000). The tick rate of the counter at I/O port 0x1808 is not established here, so the quotient is a raw count and not a measured time.

name: ec_write_reg_byte
comment: Writes one byte through three 0x000008F0 calls on the 0x62/0x66 port pair, carrying 0xA3 with 0x04, then 0xA2 with the register number, then 0xA5 with the value byte; under the 0xA3-high / 0xA2-low address scheme the first two select 0x0400 plus the register number, and that arithmetic is inferred from the same scheme elsewhere in this firmware, not EC-side confirmed. Returns early if either of the first two calls returns a negative value, and has no return value of its own.

name: wait_port_1808_ticks
comment: Splits its argument into a tick count in bits 0-21 and a repeat count in bits 22 and above. Each pass reads I/O port 0x1808, masks it to 24 bits, adds the tick count, and spins calling 0x000002c0 until a full 32-bit re-read makes bit 23 of target minus current set; because the repeat count is only tested after a pass has run, a repeat count of zero still waits once, and every pass after the first uses 0x400000 ticks. 0x1808 is not documented in this repository and its tick rate is not established here.

name: bounds_check_index_pair
comment: Calls the class helper 0x00001100 and the table selector 0x0000123c, which also writes an entry count (0x0f or 0x11) to the caller's stack slot, and rejects the first argument unless it is at least 0x400 when the class is 2 and at most (0x400 OR (count-1)), or at least 0x300 and at most (0x300 OR (count-1)) for any other class; the low byte of that argument must also be below the count. It then loads the 16-bit word at record*0x1e + 0x1c from the table 0x0000123c returned, for the record the low byte selects, and rejects the second argument unless it is no greater than ((word-1) >> 5). Returns 1 when every test passes and 0 otherwise; what the argument pair means is not decoded here.

name: copy_chain_to_new_buffer
comment: It asks 0x000008c0 for the chain's total length, requests exactly that many bytes from 0x00000894, copies the chain in with 0x00000b60, and returns the new buffer. Neither the status returned by 0x00000894 nor a NULL chain pointer is checked on this path.

name: ec_read_reg_byte
comment: Issues 0x000008F0 with 0xA3 0x04 and then 0x000008F0 with 0xA2 and the register number, then 0x0000078C with 0xA4, then polls bit 0 of port 0x66 (15-microsecond delays, at most 0x20000 iterations) and stores the byte it reads from port 0x62 through the third argument. The 0xA3/0xA2 pair selects 0x0400 plus the register number under the inferred address scheme. Returns 0, or 0x8000000000000007 if any stage fails or the poll count runs out.

name: usec_to_port_1808_ticks
comment: Multiplies its argument by 0x369e99, divides by 1000000 with a 64x64-to-128 multiply by 0x431bde82d7b634db and an 18-bit shift, passes the quotient to the tick wait at 0x000009a4, and returns its argument unchanged. The tick rate of the counter at I/O port 0x1808 is not established here, so the quotient is reported as a raw count.

name: wait_status_bit1_clear
comment: Polls the byte at port 0x64 or 0x66 (selected by whether its argument's low byte is 0x60) until bit 1 (0x02) is clear, delaying 15 units through 0xD04 on each iteration, and returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_TIMEOUT) after 0x20000 iterations. This is the same loop as 0x910 without the final write; 0x910 also returns 0 on the same condition.

name: write_port_register_byte
comment: Makes three exchanges through 0x0000094c, each with the port selector 0x62: first the pair 0xA3/0x07, then the register byte from the third argument, then the pair 0xA5 with the data byte from the fourth argument. The first two arguments are ignored, and the first negative status from any of the three exchanges is returned unchanged.

name: scale_argument_to_ticks_and_wait
comment: Multiplies its argument by 0x369e99, then divides by 1000000 using a 64x64-to-128 unsigned multiply by 0x431bde82d7b634db followed by a shift right of 0x12, so the quotient is the argument scaled by about 3.58. It passes that quotient to 0x000009c8 and returns its argument unchanged. The scale would imply a counter rate near 3.58 MHz at I/O port 0x1808, but no such clock is identified in this repository; the counts its callers pass are 15 and 5000 (0x1388).

name: memset_bytes
comment: Fills the count in the third argument (R8) bytes at the pointer in the first (RCX) with the byte in the second (DL): a byte-at-a-time loop up to the next 4-byte boundary, a 32-bit REP STOSD loop whose dword is built by duplicating the fill byte into AH and shifting AX left by 16, then a byte loop for the remainder. The alignment gap is computed as 4 - (dest & 3) through a NEG and an ADD. It returns the destination pointer unchanged; its one caller here fills 0x4C bytes at [RBP-0x12] with 0xFF.

name: read_table_field_via_mmio
comment: Calls the table selector 0x0000123c, computes the 0x1e-byte record at (low byte of the second argument) * 0x1e and loads a 16-bit field from it: offset 0x04 for selector 0, 0x0c for 1, 0x0a for 2, 0x10 for 3, 0x0e for 4, 0x14 for 5, 0x16 for 6 and 0x18 for 7, writing 0 to the out-pointer for any other selector and for a field that reads 0xffff. Otherwise it forms the address 0xfd000000 | (byte 0 of the record << 16) | ((field + element index * 4, or * 8 for selectors 6 and 7) truncated to 16 bits), reads the 32-bit word at that address and stores it through the out-pointer. Nothing in this listing establishes what the word at that address is.

name: lookup_entry_by_id_pair
comment: Returns the cached pointer at 0xdd0 if it is non-zero; otherwise clears it and walks the array at [saved_arg2+0x70] for the element count at [saved_arg2+0x68] in 0x18-byte steps, comparing each entry's first two qwords against the 16 bytes at 0xd10/0xd18. On a match it stores and returns that entry's third qword (offset +0x10); with no match it returns 0. Whether the 16 bytes at 0xd10 are a GUID is not established in this module.

name: read_port_register_byte
comment: Makes the same two 0x0000094c exchanges as 0x00000a14 (0xA3/0x07, then the register byte from the third argument), writes 0xA4 to the status port through 0x000007e8, then polls bit 0 of I/O port 0x66 until it is set - 15-unit delays through 0x00000bdc, bounded at 0x20000 iterations, 0x8000000000000007 on exhaustion - and stores the byte read from I/O port 0x62 through the pointer in the fourth argument. A negative status from either exchange, from 0x000007e8 or from the poll is returned without touching that pointer.

name: write_status_port_byte
comment: Takes a selector byte in CL and a value in DL. The port used is 0x64 when CL is 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise; the function reads it and, while bit 1 is set, delays 15 units through 0x10D0 and re-reads, giving up with 0x8000000000000007 once the counter reaches 0x20000. When bit 1 is clear it writes DL to the same port and returns 0.

name: find_cached_entry_by_tag
comment: Returns the cached qword at 0x00000DA0 when it is non-zero. Otherwise it walks the array at [0x00000D80+0x70] in 0x18-byte steps for the count at [0x00000D80+0x68], comparing the first two qwords of each entry against the values at 0x00000D00 and 0x00000D08, and on a match returns that entry's third qword (at +0x10) after caching it. A miss leaves 0x00000DA0 zero, so the search is repeated on the next call.

name: delay_poll_counter_port_1808
comment: Splits the 32-bit argument into a 22-bit amount (bits 0-21) and an iteration count (bits 22-31). Reads I/O port 0x1808, masks the value to 24 bits, adds the amount to form a target, then loops reading the port and calling the pause helper at 0x2c0 while bit 23 of (target - current) is clear, i.e. until the 24-bit counter has advanced by the amount or wrapped; the outer loop runs once per count plus one and sets the amount to 0x400000 after the first pass.

name: delay_by_counter_ticks
comment: Waits on the 24-bit counter at I/O port 0x1808: it adds the argument's low 22 bits to the counter's value masked to 24 bits, re-reads the port, and loops through 0x00000260 (PAUSE) until bit 23 of (target minus current) is set, i.e. until the counter has passed the target. The argument's bits 22-31 give the number of passes, so an argument below 0x400000 still waits once, and the 0x400000 immediate loaded into EDI is never used. The counter's identity is not decoded here.

name: find_config_table_entry_by_guid
comment: Cached lookup: when the global at 0x00000e10 is non-zero it is returned unchanged, otherwise it walks the array at offset 0x70 of the structure cached at 0x00000de8 in 0x18-byte steps, bounded by the count at offset 0x68, comparing the 16 bytes at each entry's offsets 0 and 8 against the bytes at 0x00000d80 and 0x00000d88 and caching the matching entry's qword at +0x10 in 0x00000e10. Returns 0 when the count is zero or nothing matches. Offsets 0x68 and 0x70 are where NumberOfTableEntries and ConfigurationTable sit in EFI_SYSTEM_TABLE, but nothing in this listing establishes that the cached structure is a system table.

name: find_config_table_by_module_guid
comment: Returns the pointer cached at 0xe78 if it is non-zero. Otherwise, if the count at system table +0x68 is non-zero, it walks the array of 0x18-byte entries at system table +0x70, comparing the two qwords of each entry's 16-byte leading field against the constants at 0xdc0 and 0xdc8, and caches and returns the third qword of the matching entry. The GUID those two constants form is not decoded in this repository.

name: delay_scaled_by_3579545
comment: Multiplies the argument by 0x369e99 (3579545) and then divides by 1000000, done as a 64x64 unsigned multiply by the constant 0x431bde82d7b634db followed by a shift of 18; over a wide range of inputs the result is floor(arg * 3579545 / 1000000). The quotient is passed to the port-0x1808 delay at 0xadc as a packed (iterations, amount) pair and the original argument is returned. The unit conversion this scaling implements is not established in this module; the only caller (0x944) passes the constant 15 and ignores the return.

name: write_reg_via_a2_a5_pair
comment: Ignores its first two arguments and always uses the 0x62 data port, sending the fixed pair (0xA3, 0x07) through 0xA74, then (0xA2, its third argument) and then (0xA5, its fourth argument). Each send is a selector byte followed by a data byte written to port 0x62, so the register picked by 0xA2 is immediately rewritten after 0xA5 selects it for writing. It stops at the first negative status from the three sends and returns 0 otherwise.

name: memmove_bytes
comment: A block move taking the destination in RCX, the source in RDX and the byte count in R8: when the source precedes the destination and the regions overlap, both pointers are biased by the count and the direction flag is set, which is why the flags are saved with pushf and restored with popf around the copy. It uses movsb.rep for the head, movsq.rep for the bulk and movsb.rep again for the tail when both the count and the pointer distance are at least 8, and a plain byte loop otherwise. It returns the original destination pointer, recovered by popping the value RCX held at entry.

name: wait_port_1808_ticks
comment: Splits its argument into a tick count (bits 0-21) and a repeat count (bits 22 and above). Each pass reads the counter at I/O port 0x1808, masks it to 24 bits, adds the tick count, and then spins on 0x000002c0 until a full 32-bit read of the same port makes bit 23 of target minus current set; because the pass counter is only tested after the first pass, a repeat count of zero still waits once.

name: init_oc_working_state
comment: Guarded by byte 0x3160: when it is non-zero the whole initialisation is skipped and only a SaSetup SetVariable runs. Otherwise the word at 0x315F becomes 0x100, 0x2681 becomes 1, and MSR 0xCE is read three times — byte 8 into 0x29C8 and 0x2901, byte 0x28 into 0x2A8F, byte 8 into 0x2A90 — then 0x2060 is called for thirteen out-parameters, two of the returned words are multiplied by 0x7D into 0x2912/0x2A95 and 0x2919/0x2A99, and 0x1F78 is called, its result replacing the default for 0x29C9 only when it is non-zero and no smaller than 0x2060's 4th out-parameter, which 0xB94 stores at 0x29CA; the default is 0x2060's 3rd out-parameter. The live globals 0x26CC and 0x26CE, the block 0x26D0..0x26E3, the block 0x2AB9..0x2ACC with 0x2B4E and 0x2B4F, the eight bytes 0x2B43..0x2B4A and the block 0x289A..0x28B0 are copied to 0x26CB, 0x26CD, 0x26E4..0x26F7, 0x2ACF..0x2AE4, 0x2B7D, 0x2B7E, 0x2B3B..0x2B42 and 0x289D..0x28C2 respectively, a 15-iteration word/byte array shift and a 5-iteration word shift run, MSR 0x620 is read and its bytes 0 and 8 masked with 0x7F into 0x2B0D and 0x2B0B, and CpuSetup, SaSetup and Setup are written back through runtime-services offset 0x58.

name: wait_status_port_bit1_clear
comment: Uses the same port choice as 0xA98 - 0x64 when CL is 0x60, 0x66 otherwise - but only waits: while bit 1 is set it delays 15 units through 0x10D0 and re-reads, returning 0x8000000000000007 after 0x20000 iterations and 0 once the bit clears. It reads no data port and writes nothing.

name: usec_to_port_1808_ticks
comment: Multiplies the microsecond argument by 0x369E99, divides by 1000000 with a 64x64-to-128 multiply by 0x431BDE82D7B634DB and an 18-bit shift, and passes the quotient to the tick wait at 0x00000b7c, returning its argument unchanged. The tick rate of the counter at I/O port 0x1808 is not established here, so the quotient is reported as a raw count.

name: write_two_bytes_to_port_pair
comment: Takes a selector in CL, a byte in DL and a third byte in R8. It calls 0xB98, then 0xB10, then 0xA98 with the selector and DL, then 0xB98 again, then - after its own wait loop on bit 1 of the 0x64/0x66 port - writes the third byte to port 0x60 or 0x62 (0x62 when the selector is not 0x60), and finally calls 0xB10 once more. The status from the first 0xB98 is returned. The 0xA3/0xA2/0xA4 bytes that 0xCC4 supplies in DL are what the first of those two writes sends; no further decoding of their meaning is done here.

name: scaled_delay_via_port_1808
comment: Computes its argument times 0x369e99, then divides by 1000000 using a 128-bit unsigned multiply by 0x431bde82d7b634db followed by a shift right of 0x12, so the quotient is the argument scaled by about 3.58. It passes that quotient to 0xba0 and returns the original argument unchanged. The scale factor implies a counter rate of roughly 3.58 MHz, but no clock is identified in this repository.

name: PadOwnership
comment: Reads a PCH GPIO pad's ownership bits: returns 0 and EFI_NOT_FOUND unless 0x1158 accepts the PID, then takes bits 1:0 of the pad's PCR word at PadCfgOffset + 8, which for GPP_B22 is PCR[0x6E][0x38] bits 25:24. 0 is PadOwn HOST here, and the GPP_B22 caller (0x5D8) treats anything else as a reason to leave the pad alone.

name: find_interface_by_16byte_id
comment: Returns the pointer cached at global 0xF70 when it is non-zero. Otherwise it takes the entry count from [0xF48 + 0x68] and the table base from [0xF48 + 0x70] and walks 24-byte entries, comparing each entry's first two qwords against the 16-byte constants at 0xEB0 and 0xEB8. A match stores the entry's third qword (offset 0x10) at 0xF70 and returns it; a miss, a zero count or a null table leaves 0xF70 at 0 and returns 0. What those 16-byte constants identify is not decoded here.

name: forward_to_variable_sync
comment: If 0x13D0 is null it caches the second argument there along with its +0x60 and +0x58 fields at 0x13C0 and 0x13C8, then calls 0xA08 unconditionally and returns 0 whatever that call did.

name: init_lang_variables_via_varstore
comment: Initialises four self-referential list heads (0x2b3a0/0x2b3a8, 0x2b380/0x2b388, 0x2b390/0x2b398, 0x2b370/0x2b378), stores the first argument in 0x29268 and, on first entry only, the second argument in 0x294a8 with [RDX+0x60] and [RDX+0x58] in 0x29498 and 0x294a0. It reads a variable through [0x29488+0x48] under the constants at 0x25c30 and 0x24198 with attributes 0 and the size written back through the fourth argument, calls 0x000008a4, reads the same name again through 0x0001f24c, and - if both the returned buffer and its size are non-zero - writes that buffer through [0x29488+0x58] under 0x25c60 and 0x234a0 with attributes 6. It next reads the name at 0x25c88 with 0x234a0 and, unless that call returns 0x8000000000000005, copies either the characters up to the first semicolon in the earlier buffer or the six-byte constant at 0x25c24 into a fresh pool allocation, writes the result through [0x29488+0x58] with attributes 7 and frees it. It then frees the first buffer and returns 0; the five-argument shape of the [0x29488] calls is that of a variable get/set pair, but the table itself is only identified by those offsets.

name: read_field_selector_6
comment: Passes the first two arguments to the bounds check 0x000009e4 and returns 0x8000000000000002 when it fails. Otherwise it calls 0x00000a68 with selector 6 (the 16-bit field at record offset 0x16), the first argument as the record index, the second as the element index and the third as the out-pointer, and returns 0 regardless of what that read leaves.

name: busy_wait_port_1808_ticks
comment: Splits its argument into a 22-bit tick count (bits 0 to 21) and a repeat count (bits 22 to 31), then busy-waits on I/O port 0x1808 until the counter's low 24 bits have advanced by the tick count, calling the PAUSE stub 0x260 between reads. The end test is bit 23 of the 24-bit subtraction (start + count) - current, so the wait survives a counter wrap, and the outer loop repeats the wait repeat + 1 times. Nothing is returned; the only effect is the passage of time measured in that counter's ticks.

name: read_field_selector_7
comment: Identical to 0x00000c8c except that it calls 0x00000a68 with selector 7, the 16-bit field at record offset 0x18. Returns 0x8000000000000002 when the bounds check 0x000009e4 rejects its first two arguments, and 0 after the read otherwise.

name: directional_mem_copy
comment: Arguments are destination, source and length. If source is below destination and destination is at or below source plus length it sets the direction flag, decrements both pointers and copies backwards; otherwise it copies forwards with the direction flag cleared. Once the length is at least 8 and the span at least 8 it aligns the two pointers with a byte move when they share the same low three address bits, then copies whole qwords with MOVSQ and finishes the remaining 0 to 7 bytes with MOVSB. It restores the saved flags and register and returns the original destination pointer.

name: delay_convert_arg_to_ticks
comment: Converts its argument into a tick count for the busy-wait at 0xCA4. The three-step arithmetic (imul by 0x369E99, mul by 0x431BDE82D7B634DB, shr 0x12) is the compiler's strength reduction of (argument * 0x369E99) / 1000000, not a second scaling, and the result lands in the 22-bit count field 0xCA4 splits out. It returns its argument unchanged, and the callers in this module pass 15 and 5000; the argument's time unit is not established here, though the conversion works out at about 3.574 ticks per unit and the 0x16B-tick wait in 0x32C is 363 ticks.

name: SbiClearLockTx
signature: static EFI_STATUS SbiClearLockTx (UINT32 PidPort, UINT32 Pad, UINT32 Bits)
comment: Clears P2SB sideband lock bits, after the same PID check 0x1158 performs (a failed check returns EFI_NOT_FOUND without touching the sideband). 0x119C calls it with (0x301, 0, 0x400000) and the mask reaches the sideband helper as ~0x400000, i.e. bit 22, GPP_B22's TX-lock, is cleared so the pad register can be changed. 0x119C puts it back through SbiSetLockTx afterwards.

name: write_byte_to_selected_port
comment: Selects 0x64 when the first argument is 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise, then reads that port in a loop until bit 1 is clear, delaying 15 units through 0x1120 between reads and counting the iterations; more than 0x1FFFF iterations returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_TIMEOUT). On success it writes the second argument's byte to that same port with out and returns 0. What the port pair is attached to is not shown by this listing.

name: alloc_via_table_offset_0x40
comment: Zeroes a local out-slot and calls the table pointer cached at 0x1360 at offset 0x40 with ECX=4, RDX=the size passed in RCX, R8=&out-slot, and a fourth value the caller left in the slot at [entry_RSP+0x10]. It returns the out-slot and discards the call's status, so a failed call is visible only as whatever the callee left in that slot. Which service sits at that table offset is not identified in this module.

name: SbiSetLockTx
signature: static EFI_STATUS SbiSetLockTx (UINT32 PidPort, UINT32 Pad, UINT32 Bits)
comment: Sets the same P2SB sideband lock bits 0xD2C clears, with the same PID check. 0x119C calls it with (0x301, 0, 0x400000) to restore GPP_B22's TX-lock after the pad register has been written.

name: alloc_and_zero_0x7d8_buffer
comment: Allocates 0x7D8 bytes with 0xD60 and, if the returned pointer is non-zero, calls the table cached at 0x1360 at offset 0x168 with (buffer, 0x7D8, 0), discarding that call's status. Returns the buffer pointer, or whatever 0xD60 returned if that was NULL.

name: drain_output_buffer_to_port_80
comment: Selects 0x64 as the status port when the first argument is 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise, and while bit 0 of it is set reads the data port (0x60 or 0x62), writes that byte to I/O port 0x80, waits 5000 units through 0x1120, and re-reads the status. More than 0x1FFFF iterations returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_TIMEOUT), and otherwise it returns 0. It writes nothing to the data port itself.

name: find_padded_key_in_table
comment: Builds a 4-byte key by loading 0x5F5F5F5F and copying the length of the third argument into it with 0x11C0, then linearly searches a table of 4-byte keys at the first argument for that key over the count in the second argument; a miss returns 0x800000000000000E. On a hit at address RDX it checks whether the preceding byte is 0x5C or 0x5E and whether the byte before that is 0x08; if so it fills the fifth argument with the tag byte, the two interior pointers, a zero qword and the constant 3, and returns 0. Otherwise it advances both the base and the count past the hit and searches again.

name: EcWritePortByte
signature: static EFI_STATUS EcWritePortByte (UINT8 Pair, UINT8 Value)
comment: Writes one byte to 0x66 (the EC command/status port) or to 0x64 (the KBC pair, selected by the port argument) after waiting for IBF=0. Part of the EC access sequence documented at 0xF38.

name: classify_mmio_word_e00f8002
comment: Returns immediately unless the cached byte at 0x13F0 is 0xFF. Otherwise it reads the 16-bit word at 0xE00F8002, masks off the low five bits, and stores 2 for a masked value of 0x280 or 0x9D80, 1 for 0x680 or 0xA300, and 0xFF for anything else into 0x13F0; the routine at 0x8C4 tests the result against 2. What that word is, and what the four constants identify, is not documented in this repository.

name: wait_port_bit1_clear
comment: Selects 0x64 when the first argument is 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise and loops reading that port while bit 1 is set, delaying 15 units through 0x1120 per iteration. It returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_TIMEOUT) at the 0x1FFFF iteration limit and 0 otherwise, and unlike 0xD2C it writes nothing.

name: EcDrainObf
comment: Drains OBF: while the status port's bit 0 is set, reads the data port (0x62, or 0x60 for the KBC pair) and writes each byte to 0x80, then gives the EC 5000 units of time before re-reading. Part of the EC access sequence documented at 0xF38.

name: write_two_bytes_to_port_pair
comment: Waits at 0xE2C, drains at 0xDA4, writes the second argument's byte with 0xD2C, waits at 0xE2C again, then repeats the bit-1 wait inline (15 units per poll, 0x1FFFF limit) and writes the third argument's byte to the data port, and drains once more at 0xDA4. The status port is 0x64 when the first argument equals the second argument and 0x66 otherwise, and the data port is 0x60 in that same case and 0x62 otherwise, so a caller that passes 0x62 as the first argument (both 0xF58 and 0xFB8 do) always gets the 0x66/0x62 pair. If the inline wait hits its limit the data byte is not written and the function returns the status of the first wait, which is normally 0.

name: store_value_by_width_code
comment: Calls 0xDC8 to locate a descriptor, then dispatches on the descriptor's first byte: 0 or 1 stores the low byte of the R9 value (and rejects values of 2 or more with 0x8000000000000002), 0x0A stores a byte, 0x0B a word, 0x0C a dword and 0x0E a qword, each immediately after the code byte. Any other code byte returns 0x8000000000000002; a negative status from 0xDC8 is returned unchanged.

name: dispatch_by_u16_key
comment: Dispatches on a 16-bit key taken from the low half of R8, in two passes, with 0x8000000000000003 as both the initial result value and the value returned if neither pass is entered. The first pass, entered only when the qword at 0x239a8 is non-zero, walks a table of 0x10-byte records based at 0x239a0: a record qualifies when the 16-bit value at record+4 equals the key or equals 0x1001, and its function pointer at record+8 is then called as ([0x24180], 1, 0, key), the walk stopping at the first null function pointer or the first call that does not return 0x8000000000000003. The second pass walks the circular list whose head is at 0x2b3a0 for a node whose 16-bit field at +0x10 equals the key and calls that node's +0x18 member. The table entries receive ([0x24180], 1, 0, key) and the list members receive a pointer to a 0x30-byte record this function assembles on the stack from its own six arguments - the third as 16 bits at +0x10, the fourth as a byte at +0x12, the fifth at +0x18 and the sixth at +0x20 - plus the qword at 0x24180 at +0x28, with the global 0x29270 holding that record pointer for the duration.

name: EcWaitIbfClear
comment: Waits for the status port's IBF (bit 1) to clear, with a short delay per poll, and returns EFI_TIMEOUT after 0x1FFFF polls. Part of the EC access sequence documented at 0xF38.

name: EcWriteCommandData
signature: static EFI_STATUS EcWriteCommandData (UINT8 Pair, UINT8 Command, UINT8 Data)
comment: EC access. ACPI EC ports: command/status 0x66, data 0x62 (the helpers take 'b' = 0x62; '`' = 0x60 would select the KBC pair 0x64/0x60). This one performs the whole write: wait for IBF=0 (0xED4), drain OBF (0xE4C), write the command byte to the command port (0xDD4), wait for IBF=0 again, optionally write the data byte to the data port, drain OBF again. Neither of the two sequences the hand-written reading calls EcRead0741 and EcWrite0741 is a single function: EcRead0741 is 0xA3 07, 0xA2 41, 0xA4, read 0x62, and EcWrite0741 is 0xA3 07, 0xA2 41, 0xA5 Data, and both are this function plus 0xDD4 and the data-port read. The vendor commands are 0xA3 <hi> and 0xA2 <lo> to set the EC RAM address, 0xA4 to read the byte at that address, and 0xA5 <val> to write it (all inferred). "Inferred" because the command semantics come from use, not from the EC side: OemUniWillVariableDxe (FUN_0000084c) uses the same 0xA3 07 / 0xA2 lo / 0xA4 sequence to fill UniWillVariable.ProjectID from lo = 0x40, i.e. EC 0x0740, which is the confirmed PROJECT_ID register (ec/annotations/registers.yaml).

name: wait_port_0x64_or_0x66_bit1_clear
comment: Chooses I/O port 0x64 when the low byte of the first argument is 0x60 and port 0x66 otherwise, then spins reading that port while bit 1 is set, calling 0x11E4 with the argument 0xF once per iteration and counting the iterations in RBX. It returns 0 once bit 1 is clear, or 0x8000000000000007 (the UEFI EFI_TIMEOUT status) if the count reaches 0x20000. What the polled port belongs to is not identified here.

name: write_register_a3_a2_a5
comment: Writes the three-byte sequence 0xA3 followed by the low byte of the first argument, 0xA2 followed by the low byte of the second argument, and 0xA5 followed by the low byte of the third, each through 0xE90 and always with the first argument 0x62 so the 0x66/0x62 port pair is used, stopping at the first call that returns non-zero. It returns 0 if all three calls succeed and the failing status otherwise. What 0xA3, 0xA2 and 0xA5 mean to the device on the other end is not shown by this listing.

name: read_register_a3_a2_a4
comment: Writes 0xA3 followed by the first argument's byte and 0xA2 followed by the second argument's byte through 0xE90, then 0xA4 through 0xD2C, all on the 0x62-selected 0x66/0x62 pair. It reads the status port 0x66 and, while bit 0 is clear, polls it with a 15-unit delay up to 0x1FFFF times, returning 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_TIMEOUT) at the limit; once bit 0 is set it reads the data port 0x62, stores that byte through the pointer in its third argument, and returns 0.

name: find_guid_in_saved_table
comment: Zeroes the out-pointer in the second argument, then reads a count from [0x1350]+0x68 and a table from [0x1350]+0x70 and walks it in 0x18-byte strides, comparing each entry's first two qwords against the 16 bytes at the first argument. On a match it writes the entry's third qword to the out-pointer and returns 0; with no match, or a zero count, it returns 0x800000000000000E.

name: parse_hex_chars_to_bytes
comment: Converts ASCII hex to bytes: source RCX, character count RDX, destination R8. It walks the source two bytes at a time, converting each character by subtracting 0x30 in the range 0x30-0x39, 0x37 in the range 0x41-0x46, and otherwise 0x57 with no range check - correct for lowercase a-f, wrapping for anything else - then shifts the first nibble left four, ORs in the second and stores one byte. When the index reaches count-1 the high nibble is forced to zero instead of being converted, so an odd character count emits a half byte. A count of zero returns without writing anything.

name: save_cpu_context_and_tail_jump
comment: Copies the live CPU state into the buffer at RCX: RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI and R12-R15 at offsets 0x00-0x40, RDX at 0x48, MXCSR at 0x50 (stmxcsr) and XMM6-XMM15 at 0x58-0xF7 (movdqu), with [RCX+0xF8] zeroed first. It reads the 32-bit global at 0x2090 and, only if that is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set, executes incsspq with a count of 1 followed by rdsspq and stores that result at [RCX+0xF8] instead of the zero. The prologue pushes RCX and pops RCX and RDX, so RDX becomes the caller's return address; RAX is cleared and the last instruction is an indirect jmp RDX.

name: save_cpu_context_to_frame
comment: Writes the current register state into the frame whose address is in RCX: RBX at +0x00, RSP at +0x08, RBP at +0x10, RDI at +0x18, RSI at +0x20, R12-R15 at +0x28 to +0x40, MXCSR at +0x50 and XMM6-XMM15 at +0x58 to +0xF7. It calls the stub at 0x14DC, then pops the pushed RCX back into RCX and the caller's return address into RDX, stores that at +0x48, zeroes RAX and jumps to RDX, so execution resumes just after the call in the entry function. If the flag at 0x2070 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set it first increments the shadow stack by one qword and stores the resulting SSP at +0xF8.

name: save_cpu_context_and_jump
comment: Called with RCX pointing at a 0x100-byte context buffer and RDX as the address to jump to: pops both, zeroes [RCX+0xF8], stores RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15 and RDX at [RCX+0x00..0x48], MXCSR at [RCX+0x50] and XMM6-XMM15 at [RCX+0x58..0xE8], then jumps to RDX with RAX zeroed. If the dword at 0x2060 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set it instead captures the shadow stack pointer with INCSspQ and RDSSpQ into [RCX+0xF8]. It calls the empty function at 0x139C first and only falls through to the end if a caller does return.

name: asm_context_save
comment: Saves the caller register state into the buffer pointed to by RCX: RBX at +0x00, RSP at +0x08, RBP at +0x10, RDI at +0x18, RSI at +0x20, R12-R15 at +0x28..+0x40, the continuation address popped off the stack into +0x48, MXCSR at +0x50 via stmxcsr, and XMM6-XMM15 at +0x58..+0xF7 via movdqu; those offsets match EDK2's EFI_CPU_CONTEXT. The qword at +0xF8 is first zeroed and is set to the current shadow-stack pointer (rdsspq after incsspq by 8) when the dword at 0x2020 is non-zero and bit 0x17 of CR4 is set; nothing in this listing writes 0x2020. It calls 0x1240 (a single ret) before the stores, then zeroes RAX and jumps to the continuation, so it does not return normally.

name: find_config_table_entry_by_guid
comment: Cached lookup: when the global at 0x000019b0 is non-zero it is returned unchanged, otherwise it walks the array at offset 0x70 of the structure cached in 0x00001990 in 0x18-byte steps, bounded by the count at offset 0x68, comparing the 16 bytes at each entry's offsets 0 and 8 against the qwords at 0x00001500 and 0x00001508, and caching the matching entry's qword at +0x10 in 0x000019b0. Returns 0 when the count is zero or when nothing matches. Offsets 0x68 and 0x70 are where NumberOfTableEntries and ConfigurationTable sit in EFI_SYSTEM_TABLE, but nothing in this listing establishes that the cached structure is a system table.

name: save_cpu_context_and_jump
comment: Writes the full x86-64 register file into the 0x100-byte structure at RCX: RBX at +0x00, RSP at +0x08, RBP +0x10, RDI +0x18, RSI +0x20, R12-R15 at +0x28..+0x40, the caller's RDX at +0x48, MXCSR at +0x50, and XMM6-XMM15 as sixteen-byte pairs from +0x58 to +0xF7. If the dword at 0xA2F0 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set, it executes INCSSPQ once, RDSSPQ, and stores the resulting SSP at +0xF8. It zeroes RAX and ends in a tail jump to RDX, so the call does not return here; the module entry at 0x12B0 calls it with RCX = 0xD820.

name: save_smm_cpu_context
comment: Called with RCX pointing at a context block. It first zeroes [RCX+0xF8]; if the module flag at 0x60A4 is non-zero and CR4 bit 23 is set, it runs incsspq followed by rdsspq and stores the resulting SSP at [RCX+0xF8]. It then stores RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15 and RDX at offsets 0x00 to 0x48, MXCSR at 0x50 and XMM6-XMM15 at 0x58 to 0xF7 with movdqu, zeroes RAX and returns by jumping to RDX, which is the return address its caller pushed.

name: lookup_cached_table_entry
comment: Returns the interface pointer cached at 0x1378, looking it up with 0xFE0 for the 16 bytes at 0x12C0 the first time (when 0x1378 is still zero) and reusing it on every later call. The lookup's status is not examined, so a failed first lookup leaves 0x1378 at whatever 0xFE0 wrote, which is zero.

name: find_record_by_id
comment: Returns the cached value at 0x13D8 if it is already non-null. Otherwise it takes the count at 0x13B0+0x68 and the array base at 0x13B0+0x70, walks the array in 24-byte steps comparing the 8-byte field at +0 with the value at 0x12E0 and the one at +8 with the value at 0x12E8, and on a match caches and returns the record's third 8-byte field at +0x10. With no match, or a zero count, it returns 0. What the two key values are is not shown by this listing.

name: wait_port_1808_ticks
comment: Splits its argument into a tick count (bits 0-21) and a repeat count (bits 22 and above). Each pass reads the counter at I/O port 0x1808, masks it to 24 bits, adds the tick count, and then spins on 0x000002c0 until a full 32-bit read of the same port makes bit 23 of target minus current set; because the pass counter is only tested after the first pass, a repeat count of zero still waits once. The 0x400000 written to EDI before the loop is never read.

name: delay_us_via_port_0x1808
comment: Takes a packed delay in ECX: bits 22 and above are a repeat count and bits 0-21 an amount in units of the 0x1808 counter. For each of count+1 passes it reads I/O port 0x1808, masks the low 24 bits, adds the amount, and spins calling 0x2E0 until bit 23 of (target - a fresh read of 0x1808) is set. Returns nothing.

name: restore_cpu_context_and_tail_jump
comment: The inverse of the save at 0x1000: reloads RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI and R12-R15 from offsets 0x00-0x40 of the buffer at RCX, executes ldmxcsr on [RCX+0x50] and loads XMM6-XMM15 from 0x58-0xE8, then sets RAX from RDX and tail-jumps to [RCX+0x48]. If the 32-bit global at 0x2090 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set it first computes ([RCX+0xF8] - the current SSP read by rdsspq) >> 3 and feeds that to incsspq, pushing and popping RDX around the sequence. No other memory is read or written.

name: convert_us_to_timer_units
comment: Multiplies the argument in RCX by 0x369E99, forms the 128-bit product with 0x431BDE82D7B634DB, takes the high half and shifts it right 18, then passes the result to 0x1070 as its packed (repeat | amount) delay. Returns its argument unchanged. The unit the multiplier pair converts to is not decoded here.

name: restore_cpu_context_from_frame
comment: Mirror of 0x1000: reloads RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI and R12-R15 from offsets +0x00 to +0x40 of the frame at RCX, executes LDMXCSR on +0x50 and MOVDQU on +0x58 to +0xF7 for XMM6-XMM15, then moves the RDX it was called with into RAX and tail-jumps through the qword at +0x48. When the flag at 0x2070 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set it subtracts the current SSP from the value at +0xF8, shifts the difference right by three and executes INCSSPQ, popping one qword off the shadow stack.

name: restore_cpu_context_and_jump
comment: Reloads RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15, MXCSR and XMM6-XMM15 from the buffer at RCX, copies RDX into RAX and jumps to the address stored at [RCX+0x48]. If the dword at 0x2060 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set it first moves the shadow stack pointer by the saved value minus the current SSP, shifted right by 3, using INCSspQ. It has no return path.

name: asm_context_restore
comment: Reloads the buffer at RCX into the registers it was saved from: RBX from +0x00, RSP from +0x08, RBP from +0x10, RDI and RSI from +0x18 and +0x20, R12-R15 from +0x28..+0x40, MXCSR via ldmxcsr from +0x50, and XMM6-XMM15 via movdqu from +0x58..+0xF7, then moves the second argument into RAX and jumps to the continuation at +0x48, so the caller is never resumed. When the dword at 0x2020 is non-zero and bit 0x17 of CR4 is set it first subtracts the current shadow-stack pointer (rdsspq) from the qword at +0xF8, shifts the difference right by three and applies it with incsspq, moving the shadow stack to the value stored in that slot. RDX is pushed and popped around that sequence so the second argument survives the reload.

name: restore_cpu_context_and_jump
comment: The inverse of the context save at 0x1000: it reloads RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15 from +0x00..+0x40, executes LDMXCSR from +0x50 and MOVdqu XMM6-XMM15 from +0x58..+0xF7. If the dword at 0xA2F0 is non-zero and CR4 bit 0x17 is set, it first computes ((SSP saved at +0xF8) - current SSP) >> 3 and pops that many qwords with INCSSPQ. It returns the incoming RDX unchanged in RAX and jumps to the function pointer at [RCX+0x48], the continuation the save routine recorded.

name: classify_device_id_word
comment: Returns the cached class byte at 0x00001540; when that byte is 0xff it reads the 16-bit word at MMIO 0xe00f8002, masks it with 0xffe0, and stores 2 for a masked value of 0x280 or 0x9d80, 1 for 0x680 or 0xa300, and 0xff for anything else, then returns the stored byte. What the 0xffe0 mask selects on is not determined by this function; the result is used only as a class, by 0x0000123c to choose between two tables.

name: restore_oc_working_state
comment: The unconditional inverse of 0xB94's copy phase: 0x2901, 0x2911 and 0x2909 are reloaded from 0x29C8, 0x2A93 and 0x2A92, the word at 0x315F is set to 0x100, 0x2710 to 0, 0x2711 to 0x2710 and 0x27F4 to 0, MSR 0xCE is read twice into 0x2A8F (byte 0x28) and 0x2A90 (byte 8). It then runs 0xB94's copy phase in reverse, moving 0x2B3B..0x2B42 into 0x2B43..0x2B4A, the twelve globals at 0x2ACF..0x2AE4 into 0x2AB9..0x2ACC, 0x2B7D and 0x2B7E into 0x2B4E and 0x2B4F, 0x289D..0x28C2 into 0x289A..0x28B0, 0x2B0B and 0x2B0D into 0x2B0A and 0x2B0C, 0x26E4..0x26F7 into 0x26D0..0x26E3, 0x26CB and 0x26CD into 0x26CC and 0x26CE, and 0x29C9..0x29D0 into 0x29D1..0x29D8. Two array shifts run in the opposite direction to 0xB94's: 15 iterations copying words from +0x2F and bytes from +0x2F into 0x2B50 and 0x2B6E, then 5 iterations copying words from +0xA2 into 0x2A5B. It finishes by writing SaSetup, CpuSetup and Setup back through runtime-services offset 0x58, in that order.

name: find_config_table_by_first_two_qwords
comment: Returns the value cached at 0x1508 if it is non-zero; otherwise it walks the array at [0x14E0]+0x70 in 0x18-byte steps for at most the count at [0x14E0]+0x68 entries, comparing the first two qwords of each entry with the 16 bytes at 0x13B0/0x13B8. On a match it returns and caches a pointer to the entry's third qword (entry+0x10) rather than to the entry or to the table its first qword points at, and with no match it returns 0.

name: delay_by_counter_ticks
comment: Multiplies the first argument by 0x369E99, divides by 1000000 through a 128-bit multiply by 0x431BDE82D7B634DB and a shift of 18, passes the 32-bit quotient to 0x10C0, and returns its argument unchanged. The quotient works out at about 3.58 port-0x1808 ticks per argument unit (15 gives 53, 5000 gives 17897); the time unit the callers are expressing is not established by this listing.

name: restore_smm_cpu_context
comment: The mirror image of the save at 0x1000. If the flag at 0x60A4 is non-zero and CR4 bit 23 is set, it loads the saved SSP from [RCX+0xF8], subtracts the current SSP, shifts the difference right by 3 and runs incsspq to unwind the shadow stack. It then reloads RBX, RSP, RBP, RDI, RSI, R12-R15, MXCSR and XMM6-XMM15 from offsets 0x00 to 0xF7, copies the incoming RDX into RAX and jumps to the return address stored at [RCX+0x48].

name: IsPchLp
comment: Transcribed name, and it does not describe the return value: the decompile returns 1 when the 00:1F.0 device-ID class from 0x1100 is NOT -LP and the chosen table's PadPerGroup is > 22, and 0 otherwise. The name records the question being asked; the call site at 0x5D8 proceeds only on a non-zero return, which is what makes the early return in the hand-written reading of 0x5D8 ("if IsPchLp or PadPerGroup <= 22, return") come out right. Left as transcribed rather than renamed, with the discrepancy stated here rather than quietly fixed (CLAUDE.md). A device ID 0x1100 does not recognise becomes class 0xFF, takes the 17-entry H table, and so passes this check with PadPerGroup > 22: an unknown ID uses the H table.

name: module_entry
comment: The module's own entry point, the one Ghidra calls `entry`: it stores its second argument at 0x2050 and the qword at [second argument + 0x60] at 0x2058, zeroes the stack slot at RSP+0x30, and calls [+0x140] of that table with RCX = 0x2010, RDX = 0 and R8 = &the slot; the pointer left in the slot then becomes RCX for a second call, this time to [+0x8] with RDX = 0x2060 and R8 still pointing at the same slot. 0x2060 is used as a function-pointer table at +0xD0 below, but no store to it appears in this listing, and the contents of 0x2010 and 0x2060 are not in the listing either, so neither service is identifiable here. It sets 0x2170 to 0x8000000000000001 and calls 0x1000 with RCX = 0x2070, the 0x100-byte buffer the save and restore pair use, which continues at 0x11E0; there it calls [+0xD0] of the 0x2060 table with RCX = 0x2000, RDX = 0 and R8 = &the slot, skipping the next call when that returns negative. On the success path it calls the pointer in the slot with (slot, 0x1240, RSP+0x38), clears 0x2170 and calls 0x10D0 with RCX = 0x2070 and RDX = -1, which resumes at 0x11E0 with RAX = -1, takes the jnz to 0x1233 and returns the now-zero 0x2170.

name: mem_move_bytes
comment: memmove with dst in RCX, src in RDX and length in R8. It computes R9 = src+len-1 and, if src < dst and dst <= R9, copies backwards with DF set (std) using rep movsb from the two ends; otherwise it copies len>>3 qwords with rep movsq and then the len&7 remaining bytes with rep movsb. Restores DF with cld and returns the original dst in RAX.

name: memmove
comment: Copies R8 bytes from RDX to RCX. It compares the source with the destination and with the last source byte: when the source lies inside the destination range it sets the direction flag and copies backwards from the last byte, otherwise it copies forwards with MOVSQ.REP followed by MOVSB.REP for the sub-qword remainder, and clears the direction flag either way. RAX is loaded with the destination before the copy, so the destination address is returned.

name: module_entry_locate_and_dispatch
comment: Caches the table pointer at [arg2+0x60] in the globals 0x20B0 and 0x20B8, calls its entry at +0x140 with (16 bytes at 0x2040, 0, &interface), then calls vtable +0x08 of the returned interface with the address 0x20C0 and keeps that result in the global 0x20C0. Initialises the status global 0x21D0 to 0x8000000000000001, saves the CPU context with 0x1000, calls 0x12C0, and overwrites 0x21D0 with the RAX that call left behind only when that value is negative and the previous status was negative too. It then calls 0x10D0 with RDX = -1 to restore the saved context and jump to the recorded return address, so the normal path leaves through the restore; the ret at the end is reached only when 0x1000 comes back with RAX non-zero.

name: memcpy_forward_or_reverse
comment: memcpy(dest = RCX, src = RDX, len = R8). Copies R8>>3 qwords with REP MOVSQ and then the R8&7 trailing bytes with REP MOVSB. When the ranges overlap with the destination above the source (src < dest <= src+len-1) it sets the direction flag with STD, points both cursors at the last byte and walks them backwards with REP MOVSB, then restores DF with CLD; it returns nothing in particular.

name: wait_port_0x1808_ticks
comment: Takes a packed count in ECX: the low 22 bits are added to the 24-bit value read from I/O port 0x1808 and the top 10 bits are the number of passes. Each pass spins on 0x300 (PAUSE) until bit 23 of (target - current) is set, that is until that counter has advanced past the target, and the outer loop runs param>>22 times when that is non-zero and once when it is zero.

name: MemOcSetGppB22Tx
signature: static VOID MemOcSetGppB22Tx (UINT16 Pid, UINT8 Pad, UINT64 Group, UINT32 TableSel)
comment: The routine the hand-written annotation labelled "/* 0x119C */" without naming; the name here is new. It is what 0x5D8 calls once the table and ownership checks have passed: read the pad's lock bits, if bit 22 (GPP_B22 TX-lock) is set clear it through SbiClearLockTx (0xD2C), then set PCR[0x6E][0x790 + 22*0x10] bit 0 (GPP_B22 DW0 GPIOTXState = 1) directly, then restore the lock through SbiSetLockTx (0xD80) if it had been set.

name: cpu_pause
comment: A single PAUSE instruction followed by ret; nothing is read or written. Its one call site is inside the I/O port 0x1808 poll at 0x13DE, where it is executed on every pass of the loop.

name: memcpy_forward_or_reverse
comment: Copies R8 bytes from the source in RDX to the destination in RCX. If the source lies below the destination and the ranges can overlap it sets the direction flag and copies backwards instead, backing both pointers up first. The body then, when the two pointers share the same nonzero 8-byte offset, copies that many bytes to align them, moves whole qwords with a repeated 8-byte move, and finishes the remainder byte by byte. Returns the original destination.

name: cpu_pause
comment: A single PAUSE instruction followed by RET: no memory is read or written and no register other than the return address is touched. The polling loop at 0x141E in this module calls it between the two port reads.

name: memset_zero
comment: memset(dest = RCX, 0, len = RDX). RAX is zeroed, RDI is loaded with the destination, and len>>3 qwords are written with REP STOSQ followed by the len&7 remaining bytes with REP STOSB. The trailing POP RAX reloads the destination pointer that was pushed on entry, so the function returns the destination in RAX.

name: read_timestamp_counter
comment: Executes rdtsc, shifts EDX left by 0x20 and ORs it into RAX, so the 64-bit return value is the TSC high and low halves concatenated. No memory is touched, and both call sites in this module (0x13D7 and 0x13F7) discard the result.

name: read_tsc_64bit
comment: Executes RDTSC, shifts the EDX half left by 32 and ORs it into EAX, returning the full 64-bit timestamp counter in RAX. Two instructions precede the return; nothing else is read or written.

name: enable_interrupts
comment: Executes sti and returns, enabling maskable interrupts. It is the restore half of the pair with the cli at 0x11F0: the caller at 0x1400 picks between them on the IF bit it captured from RFLAGS before the poll below 0x12A4.

name: enable_interrupts
comment: STI followed by RET. The only effect is setting the interrupt-enable flag; no memory is touched.

name: memset_byte
comment: memset(dest = RCX, byte = R8, len = RDX). RDI takes the destination and XCHG RDX,RCX puts the count in RCX and the destination in RDX, then REP STOSB writes it. RAX ends up holding the destination (moved out of RDX), which is what the function returns.

name: disable_interrupts
comment: Executes cli and returns, disabling maskable interrupts. Called at 0x13BE before the I/O port 0x1808 poll, and again at 0x1407 when the RFLAGS read at 0x13B6 had IF clear.

name: disable_interrupts
comment: CLI followed by RET. The only effect is clearing the interrupt-enable flag; no memory is touched.

name: read_rflags
comment: Pushes the flags, pops them into RAX and returns, so the return value is RFLAGS zero-extended to 64 bits. Its single caller at 0x13B6 keeps only bit 9 to decide whether to re-enable interrupts at the end of the function.

name: read_rflags
comment: Pushes RFLAGS onto the stack and immediately pops it into RAX, so the current RFLAGS is returned in RAX. The caller at 0x13F6 uses bit 9, the interrupt-enable flag, of the returned value to decide whether to re-enable interrupts after its polling loop.

name: memcmp_bytes
comment: memcmp(a = RCX, b = RDX, len = R8). R8 is moved into RCX and REP CMPSB walks the two strings, then the last byte read from each ([RSI-1] and [RDI-1]) is zero-extended and subtracted, so the result is a[k] - b[k] at the first difference and 0 when the compared prefixes match. The byte difference is not normalised to -1/0/1; callers here only test it against zero.

name: smm_handler_entry
comment: The module entry. It calls the init at 0x12A4, stores the constant 0x8000000000000000 into the status global at 0x2200 (every test of it in this function is on bit 63), then calls 0x1000 with RCX = 0x2100 so the whole CPU context is saved into that static block and control lands back here. Next it calls 0x14DC and keeps the returned status in 0x2200 unless the call was negative and the stored value was not already an error, then calls 0x10D0 with RDX = -1 to restore the context. It returns that status in RAX, and if it has bit 63 set it first calls the dispatch at 0x1648.

name: smm_entry_save_context_and_register_handler
comment: Module entry point: calls the module body 0x12E4 with the two arguments it received, stores 0x8000000000000000 into the global at 0x21E0, and calls the context-save routine 0x1000 on the frame at 0x20E0. If control returns with RAX non-zero, which is the resume path taken through 0x10D0, the registration block is skipped; otherwise it calls the function at offset 0x140 of the table at 0x20A8 with (0x2000, 0, &local), copies 8 bytes of the returned interface pointer into 0x21F8 with 0x14E0, calls the function at offset 0xA8 of the table at 0x20B0 with (&local, 0x2040, 0, 0x21F8), clears 0x21E0, and calls 0x10D0 on the frame at 0x20E0 with RDX set to -1. It finally returns the value at 0x21E0, calling 0x1578 first if that value is negative.

name: select_table_by_class
comment: Calls the class helper 0x00001100 and, when it returns 2, writes 0x0f to the caller's out-parameter and returns the table base 0x00001750; for any other class it writes 0x11 and returns 0x00001550. The tables are read elsewhere in this module as 0x1e-byte records indexed by a record number, but their contents are static data and are not decoded here.

name: empty_ret_stub
comment: The entire body is `c2 00 00`, a `ret 0`: no register, memory or port access, and no effect on the flags. Nothing in the listing says what the function is meant to do, so its role is left unresolved.

name: cpu_pause
comment: One pause instruction and a return. 0x5960 calls it once per turn of its polling loop, which is the only use of it in this module; what the loop is waiting for is not decoded here.

name: read_tsc
comment: Executes rdtsc, shifts RDX left by 32 and ORs it into RAX, so the return value is the 64-bit time-stamp counter assembled from EDX and EAX. 0x5960 calls it on both sides of its delay loop; the decompiled C reading discards both results.

name: cpu_relax_pause
comment: A single PAUSE instruction followed by RET. The listing contains nothing else, so what this function is for is entirely a property of its callers.

name: enable_interrupts
comment: A single sti and a return, which sets IF in RFLAGS and enables maskable interrupts. 0x5960 takes this branch when the flags it read through 0x1280 have IF set.

name: alloc_and_parse_hex_from_utf16
comment: Counts the UTF-16 hex characters starting at RCX+0xa, using the same in-range test as 0x00001074, then allocates count>>1 bytes through [0x29478+0x40] with pool type 4 into the pointer-to-pointer in RDX and, on success, calls 0x00000ff4 with (RCX+0xa, the character count, the allocated buffer) and writes count>>1 through the third argument. The count is a character count rather than a byte count, so an odd number of characters leaves the final nibble zero, and the allocated size does not include a terminator.

name: read_timestamp_counter
comment: Executes RDTSC and returns the 64-bit counter in RAX, assembled from the instruction's EDX:EAX output with SHL RDX,0x20 and OR RAX,RDX. No serialising instruction is issued around it.

name: disable_interrupts
comment: A single cli and a return, which clears IF in RFLAGS. 0x5960 calls it to mask interrupts around its polling loop, and again on the branch taken when the flags it read through 0x1280 have IF clear.

name: enable_interrupts
comment: Executes STI and returns. STI takes effect only after the following instruction, so control reaches the caller before interrupts are re-enabled; nothing here records that it ran.

name: read_eflags
comment: pushfq, pop RAX, ret: returns the current RFLAGS as a 64-bit value. 0x5960 tests bit 9 of the result to choose between the 0x1270 and 0x1260 paths, which the decompiled C spells as the IF bit.

name: disable_interrupts
comment: Executes CLI and returns to the caller with interrupts masked. Nothing in this listing re-enables them; that has to be the caller's business.

name: smi_handler_entry
comment: The module entry point. It spills its two arguments, calls 0x12E0 with them, then calls 0x1420 with the same two and keeps the 64-bit result in RSI; if that result is negative it calls 0x13B0 with the original arguments. It restores its saved registers and returns the value from 0x1420 in RAX.

name: read_flags_register
comment: PUSHFQ followed by POP RAX: returns the current RFLAGS in RAX, with bit 9 carrying the interrupt-enable state. No field of RFLAGS is inspected or altered here.

name: locate_three_protocols_and_invoke
comment: Calls the +0xD0 entry of the interface cached at 0x20C0 with the (GUID, 0, &interface) argument shape for the 16 bytes at 0x2030, 0x2050 and 0x2000 in turn, skipping any call that returns negative. On the first it calls vtable +0x00 of the new interface with the 16-byte constant at 0x1594 and two stack out-pointers; on the third it calls vtable +0x00 with the address 0x1220 and one out-pointer. On the second it calls vtable +0x00 with the address 0x159C in a loop over a 32-bit counter that starts at 3, is passed by pointer and is incremented after each call until it reaches 6, so the callback is entered with 4 and then 5. The contents of the constants at 0x2030, 0x2050, 0x2000 and 0x1594, the behaviour of the code at 0x1220, and the return values of all three calls are not decoded by this listing.

name: init_module_globals
comment: Calls nine routines in a fixed order, each with the same two arguments and each return value dropped into the same stack slot at [RSP+0x20]: 0x5684, 0x569C, 0x56AC, 0x57A0, 0x58E0, 0x5950, 0x5960, 0x5A14 and 0x5A48. It reloads RCX and RDX from the stack before every call rather than holding them in registers across the sequence.

name: scan_for_marker_then_connect
comment: Scans the UTF-16 string in RCX for a 0x26 ('&') followed by 10 bytes equal to the constant at 0x25e68, compared with 0x000002c0 and short-circuited when the candidate address is 0x25e68 itself; reaching the NUL first returns 0x800000000000000e. After a match it calls 0x00001268 on the text beyond it, which allocates a buffer and hex-decodes it, then requires the buffer to be non-null, the decoded length at [RSP+0x60] to be at least 4, the 16-bit value at buffer+2 to be no larger than that length, and the first byte to be either 1 to 5 or 0x7f - otherwise the same 0x800000000000000e is returned. On success it calls [0x29478+0xb8] with (0x23690, the buffer, the second argument), frees the buffer through [0x29478+0x48] and returns that call's status. What 0x23690 and the decoded bytes represent is not decoded here.

name: nop_stub_return
comment: Contains a single RET and no other instruction. It is called from 0x1000 before that function fills the context buffer, but why the module needs an empty callee there is not determinable from this listing.

name: find_table_entry_by_16_byte_id
comment: Takes the entry count from [0x20C0+0x98] and the table pointer from [0x20C0+0xA0] and walks the table in 0x18-byte strides, comparing the first 0x10 bytes of each entry against the 16 bytes at 0x2020, qword-at-a-time while both pointers are 8-byte aligned and byte-at-a-time for the tail. On the first match it stores the qword at entry+0x10 through the caller out-pointer and returns 0; with no match, or with a zero count, it returns 0x800000000000000E. The 16 bytes at 0x2020 and the table entries are not decoded by this listing.

name: forward_to_00005820
comment: Spills its two arguments, calls 0x5820 with them and drops the result into the unused slot at [RSP+0x20] before returning. That single call is all this listing contains, so what 0x5820 does is not decoded here.

name: record_status_and_restore_context
comment: If the status in RCX is negative and the qword at 0x6240 is also negative, it overwrites 0x6240 with the incoming status; otherwise 0x6240 is left as it is. It then loads RDX with -1 and RCX with the address 0x6140 and calls 0x5788, which is a one-instruction jump to 0x1130. The result of 0x5788 is not returned from here.

name: run_smm_handler_body
comment: Stores 0x8000000000000001 to the status word at 0x6240, loads RCX with the address 0x6140 and calls 0x1000, the context-save routine. If that comes back with RAX non-zero it skips to the return; otherwise it reloads its own two arguments, calls 0x55E0 and passes the 64-bit result to 0x13E0 in RCX. It returns the qword at 0x6240.

name: test_cpuid6_and_msr_1a0
comment: Reads MSR 0x1A0 through 0x5790 and issues CPUID leaf 6 through 0x10D0 into four stack dwords. It returns 1 if bit 1 of the CPUID EAX result is set, and if that bit is clear returns 1 only when bit 38 of the MSR value is set, under the mask 0x4000000000; otherwise it returns 0. The listing does not say what either bit means to this module.

name: protocol_vtbl0_call_with_5_args
comment: Builds the 16-byte value 55cfba41-b834-4f3c-be0f-ae034e134975 on the stack, calls the +0xD0 entry of the interface cached at 0x20C0 with (16 bytes at 0x2010, 0, &interface) and, if that does not return negative, calls vtable +0x00 of the returned interface with five arguments: the address 0x2068, the stack copy of the 16-byte value, a pointer to an uninitialised stack slot, a pointer to the value 10, and the caller out-pointer. The relationship between the constant at 0x2010 and the stack value, the contents at 0x2068, and the meaning of the 10 are not decoded by this listing.

name: register_callback_and_copy_buffer
comment: Calls the locator at [0x20C8+0x140] with the GUID at 0x2040, then the method at [0x20D0+0xD0] with the GUID at 0x2070, then the first member of the interface returned by that, passing the in-module address 0x149C, a pointer to a qword pre-set to -1, and a second out-pointer. On success it writes the low byte of the -1 qword to offset 4 of the buffer named by a third out-pointer and copies 8 bytes from that buffer to 0x2220 through the helper at 0x15B0, then calls [0x20D0+0xA8] with a stack address, the constant 0x2000, 0 and 0x2220. It returns 0 on success, or the negative status of whichever call failed first, carried back in RBX. Which protocol sits behind the pointer at 0x20D0 is not resolved here.

name: ret_stub
comment: The listing is a single RET 0: the return address is popped and 0 is added to RSP, so this is a plain return that reads no memory and changes no register. 0x1000 calls it before touching the frame it was handed; nothing in this listing shows why the call is made, so the role is not decoded.

name: copy_to_global_0x21f8
comment: Copies RDX bytes from RCX into the fixed module global at 0x21F8 by calling 0x1180, and returns immediately if RCX already points at 0x21F8. The 0x28 bytes of stack it reserves are never used by the body.

name: test_msr_ce_bit29
comment: Reads MSR 0xCE through 0x5790 and returns 1 if bit 29 of the 64-bit result is set, under the mask 0x20000000, and 0 otherwise. The bit's meaning to this module is not shown by the listing.

name: protocol_vtbl10_call_with_null_args
comment: Builds the same 16-byte value 55cfba41-b834-4f3c-be0f-ae034e134975 on the stack, locates an interface through the +0xD0 entry of the interface cached at 0x20C0 with (16 bytes at 0x2010, 0, &interface) and, if that does not return negative, calls vtable +0x10 of the result with the address 0x2068, the stack constant and three NULL arguments. It uses the same 0x2068 and the same 16-byte value as 0x14B0 but reaches vtable +0x10 instead of vtable +0x00 and passes neither buffer nor count. What the call does is not decoded by this listing.

name: append_text_record_to_output
comment: Appends one delimited record to the output structure at RCX: byte 0x02, then the NUL-terminated string in RDX copied in with the memcpy at 0x1180, then byte 0x03. When the dword at [RCX+0x20] is non-zero and bit 1 of [RCX+0x14] is set, it first writes a 0x0A newline at RCX + [RCX+0x20] + 0x24 and starts the new record one byte after it. It then ORs 2 into [RCX+0x14] and stores (end of the new record) - RCX - 0x23 into [RCX+0x20], so the buffer is a newline-separated list of 0x02/0x03-wrapped text records.

name: query_interface_via_offset_0x50
comment: Calls the function at offset 0x50 of the structure pointed to by 0x20B0 with (6, the caller's second argument, &out) and returns the pointer written to out, or 0 when the returned status has its sign bit set. What the constant 6 and the pass-through second argument stand for is not decoded by this listing.

name: test_msr_ce_bit28
comment: Reads MSR 0xCE through 0x5790 and returns 1 if bit 28 of the 64-bit result is set, under the mask 0x10000000, and 0 otherwise. Same read and same shape as 0x1520, one bit lower.

name: forward_by_range_test
comment: Calls 0x1504 with the pointer at 0x21F0 and, if it returns non-zero, tail-jumps to the function at offset 0x58 of the table at 0x20B0; otherwise it tail-jumps to the function at offset 0x48 of the table at 0x20A8. Both tails are entered with RCX still holding the pointer read from 0x21F0. Its only call site in this module is 0x1230, which invokes it when the global at 0x21E0 holds a negative value.

name: branch_on_value_4_or_5
comment: Reads the 32-bit value at [RDX], subtracts 4 and takes the direct path only when the result is 0 or 1, that is when the value is 4 or 5. On that path it calls 0x14B0 into a 10-byte stack buffer, returns immediately if the call returned negative, and if the first byte of the buffer is 1 calls 0x152C and returns. Every other case, including a first byte other than 1, calls 0x15D4.

name: empty_return_stub
comment: A single ret with an immediate operand of 0: it only pops the return address and does nothing else. Its one call site is the prologue of the context save at 0x1000, where the call site balances its own push/sub, so the hook is a no-op in this build. What it is meant to do is not decoded from the bytes.

name: copy_bytes_to_static_buffer
comment: Compares the source pointer RCX against 0x2220 and returns immediately if they are equal; otherwise it calls the memmove at 0x1180 with dst = 0x2220, src = RCX and length = RDX, so the destination is always the same static buffer and a self-copy is a no-op. The only call site passes a length of 8 (0x1572).

name: find_cached_entry_by_16_byte_key
comment: Returns the pointer cached at 0x20C8; when that is zero it walks the table at offset 0x70 of the structure saved at 0x20A0, bounded by the count at offset 0x68, in 0x18-byte entries, comparing the first 16 bytes of each entry against the pair stored at 0x2020/0x2028. On a match it stores that entry's third qword into 0x20C8 and returns it, so later calls return the cached value without searching. The offsets 0x68/0x70 and the 0x18-byte entries holding a 16-byte key followed by a pointer match the layout of the configuration table EFI_SYSTEM_TABLE carries, but the key at 0x2020 is module data and is not decoded here.

name: expand_runs_into_table_60f0
comment: Expands a run-length description into the byte table at 0x60F0. The first loop writes value 0 into the table count[0] times, and each later loop writes value n into the next count[n] minus count[n-1] bytes, appending at a running index held in [RSP+0x1]; CL, DL, R8B and R9B supply the first four values and the rest come from the stack. The word at 0x60FC is not written here, so this function does not set the table's length.

name: output_contains_record_named
comment: Walks the record buffer at [RCX+0x24] for the [RCX+0x20] bytes it holds, looking for a byte 0x02 record whose payload up to the closing 0x03 is the same length as the string in RDX and compares equal through 0x7E98. Returns 1 in AL on a match and 0 otherwise, stopping early after three 0x0A newlines or at the end of the buffer. The result is a boolean, not an index: nothing here says where the match was.

name: save_or_restore_oc_state
comment: Selected by CL: CL == 1 copies the module's live globals into the save block starting at 0x2BE1 — the word at 0x26C3, the bytes and words at 0x26CC..0x26E3, dword 0x2711, the block 0x289A..0x28C4, 0x2901..0x292B, 0x29D1..0x29DA, the words and bytes at 0x2AB2..0x2ACC, the byte at 0x2B0C, the eight bytes 0x2B43..0x2B4A, the dwords 0x2A95 and 0x2A99, the qword at 0x2A5B and the byte at 0x315F — and any other value runs the mirror copy at 0x19F4, which writes the live globals from 0x2BE1 instead. There is no I/O port and no MSR access in either direction: this is a pure block copy, and 0x400, its only caller in this module, does the variable writes around it. The restore path additionally loads 0x2710 from 0x2BF4, a byte the save path in this listing never writes.

name: range_table_contains_addr
comment: Returns 1 in AL if the argument RCX falls inside one of the ranges described by the table at the base held in the global 0x2210, and 0 otherwise. The number of ranges is the global at 0x2208; the walk starts at base+8 and steps 0x20 bytes per entry, reading the first qword of an entry as a start and the next as a length and testing start <= arg < start+length. Nothing is written, and the return is only the AL byte.

name: out_port_80_then_call_vtbl_68
comment: Writes 0x77, 0x78, 0x79 and 0x88 to I/O port 0x80 at four points, computing DX as value+9, value+8, value+7 and value-8 respectively: before the first protocol call, on its negative return, on a negative return from 0x13A0, and after the dispatch loop. It calls 0x14B0 into a 10-byte buffer, treats the second byte of that buffer as a count and, when the count is non-zero, walks the data pointed to by the buffer last 8 bytes in 0xE-byte strides, copying each entry first dword into the object returned by 0x13A0. Each iteration calls vtable +0x68 of that object with (object, descriptor, entry[8], entry[9], entry[0xA]), where descriptor is a 0x31-byte buffer filled with zero by 0x1730 whose byte at offset 0x17 is set to 0xE0 immediately before the call. It then calls 0x152C, writes 0x88 to port 0x80 and returns the last vtable return value; what the port 0x80 index values and the object vtable +0x68 entry mean is not decoded by this listing.

name: query_protocol_value_arg6
comment: Calls the function pointer at [0x20D0+0x50] with RCX = 6, the caller's second argument in RDX and a pointer to a stack slot in R8, then returns that stack slot's contents when the call returned non-negative and 0 when it returned an error (cmovs). The interface at 0x20D0 and the meaning of the constant 6 are not resolved here; the only caller passes it the size it just read from [interface+0x18].

name: dispatch_to_base_table_method
comment: Passes the address in the global 0x2210 to the range-table test at 0x15D4 and tail-jumps to the method at offset 0x58 of the interface in 0x20D0 when that test returns non-zero, otherwise tail-jumps to the method at offset 0x48 of the table in 0x20C8. Both are indirect jumps through a function pointer, so the destination of each is not decodable from this module.

name: lookup_guid_in_entry_table
comment: Returns the cached pointer in the global 0x20E8 if it is non-zero. Otherwise it takes the entry's saved second argument from 0x20C0, reads the entry count at [ptr+0x68] and the table base at [ptr+0x70], and walks 0x18-byte entries comparing the 16 bytes at 0x2030/0x2038 against the first two qwords of each; on a match it caches the entry's third qword (base+0x10+index*0x18) into 0x20E8 and returns it, or returns 0 if the count is zero or no entry matches. The structure that owns that table is not identified further than being the entry's second argument.

name: get_argument_string_for_record
comment: Repeats the record walk of 0x15C4, but when the named record matches and the record immediately after it also begins with 0x02, it allocates payload-length+1 bytes through the interface at 0xD7A0 (its vtable entry +0x50, called with pool type 6), zeroes them with 0x11C0, copies the following record's payload in with 0x1180 and returns the buffer. Returns NULL when nothing matches, when the pool call returns an error, or when the record after the match is not 0x02 - so the caller gets a private copy it is expected to free with the same interface's +0x58 entry.

name: memset_u8
comment: Fills the R8 bytes at the destination in RCX with the byte value in DL and returns the original destination pointer. It expands the byte into a dword-wide pattern in EAX, writes single bytes until the destination is 4-byte aligned, then uses REP STOSD for the whole-dword remainder and finishes with a byte tail for count mod 4. No other side effects are visible in the listing.

name: get_trailing_value_for_named_record
comment: Walks the record buffer at [RCX+0x24] a byte at a time counting 0x0A newlines, and once three have been seen it compares the name delimited by the surrounding 0x02/0x03 bytes against the NUL-terminated constant at 0xA690 through 0x7E98 - the contents of that constant are not in this listing and are not decoded here. On a match it stores (buffer length - position) through the pointer in RDX, allocates that many bytes from the interface at 0xD7A0 vtable +0x50 with pool type 6, zeroes them and copies the remainder of the buffer from the current position into them, and returns the new buffer. Returns NULL when there is no match or the remaining length is zero.

name: encode_runs_from_byte_table
comment: Reads the byte table at 0x60F0 for the length held in the word at 0x60FC and run-length encodes it into two 8-byte stack arrays, seeding the first run from table[0] with a count of 1. Where a byte equals its predecessor the current run's count is incremented in place; where it is lower than its predecessor a new run is opened whose count is the previous run's count plus one, so the walk assumes the table is already in ascending order. It then writes the eight value bytes out through the first eight stack pointers at [RSP+0x30] to [RSP+0x68] and the eight counts through the next eight at [RSP+0x70] to [RSP+0xA8].

name: parse_number_string_auto_base
comment: Skips leading spaces (0x20) and then leading '0' characters in the string at RCX, then inspects the first byte left: if subtracting 0x58 and masking with 0xDF yields zero the byte is 'X' or 'x' and the string is parsed as hexadecimal by 0x7F98, otherwise as decimal by 0x7EF4. Both parsers are called with RCX = the original string, RDX = the end-pointer out-parameter (which this listing never initialises) and R8 = the out-parameter at [RSP+0x30], whose first qword is returned in RAX. Overflow and error reporting are whatever 0x7EF4 and 0x7F98 do; neither is in this listing.

name: clear_output_buffer
comment: Zeroes [RCX+0x24] for the number of bytes held in the dword at [RCX+0x20] using the memset at 0x11C0, then stores 0 into that length dword. The flag dword at [RCX+0x14] and everything past the old length are left untouched.

name: register_callback_for_key
comment: Appends a callback to the list headed at 0x2b3a0/0x2b3a8. A NULL second argument returns 0x8000000000000002, and before allocating it walks the list and returns 0x8000000000000003 if any node's 16-bit field at +0x10 already equals the key. Otherwise it allocates 0x20 bytes through [0x29478+0x40] with pool type 4, stores the key as a 16-bit value at node+0x10 and the callback at node+0x18, sets node+0 to the sentinel 0x2b3a0 and node+8 to the current tail in 0x2b3a8, then relinks the old tail and 0x2b3a8 to the new node. The allocated pointer is also written into the caller's fifth argument slot, which the callers do not use, and the return value is the allocator's status - zero on success.

name: dispatch_command_by_table_id
comment: Reads the context pointer at 0xD770 and the dword at [context + 0x10]. If that dword is 1, it reads the bytes at [context+0x24] and [context+0x25] as a big-endian 16-bit version: 1 or more clears [context+0x18] and [context+0x14] and calls the table serialiser 0x1B2C, while 0 clears the buffer with 0x11C0, sets [context+0x14] to 2 and [context+0x18] to 0x8000000000000003, and appends the constant at 0xA6B8, which the decompiler names 'Unsupported tool version'. Any other value is looked up by scanning 0x16 (22) entries at 0x24 stride from 0x90F8 for one whose leading dword equals it, and the matching function pointer from the parallel table at 0x90FC is called with the context as its only argument. Returns 0 on every path, including the not-found case.

name: register_sw_dispatch_handler
comment: Registers the module's handler address 0x1C4C with an SMM dispatch protocol. It caches the second argument's +0x60 and +0x58 members at 0xD798 and 0xD7D0 on first use, locates the protocol whose GUID constant is at 0x9E18 through the boot-services pointer at 0xD798, calls the located object's vtable 0 with an out-byte to test whether a registration already exists and its vtable 1 to cache an interface at 0xD7A0, and if that interface is present calls 0x84FC, 0x8390 and 0x8418 while setting the bytes at 0xD7A8 and 0xD7B8. It then locates two further GUIDs (0x9020 into the global 0xD778, 0x9060 into a stack slot), calls [0xD7A0 + 0xD0] with the GUID at 0x90A0, and invokes the returned object's vtable 0 with (this, 0x1C4C, &status, &context) - the SMM software-dispatch registration shape, though the GUID bytes are not in this listing. It stores the status byte and context pointer at 0x90C0/0x90C8, rewrites every entry of the 0x16-entry table at 0x90F8 whose leading dword is 0xFFFF as (index + 1) | 0x80000000, and finally calls [0xD7A0 + 0xA8] with the GUID at 0x9000 and the saved pair.

name: find_config_table_entry
comment: Configuration-table lookup on the system table cached at 0x2688: NumberOfTableEntries is at +0x68, the array at +0x70, and the stride 0x18 is the size of one EFI_CONFIGURATION_TABLE, so each entry is a 16-byte vendor GUID followed by a Data pointer. Each entry's GUID is compared against the 8 bytes at 0x2580 and 0x2588, and a match caches and returns the entry's Data pointer ([entry+0x10], held in 0x26A0). A non-zero cache short-circuits the search, and the return is 0 when there is no table, no count or no match.

name: read_cpuid1_stepping
comment: The same leaf-1 call through 0x310, returning EAX & 0xF, the low four bits of the version word. As at 0x1E14 only the EAX output is read.

name: scan_config_data_for_guid
comment: Walks the pointer 0x1E28 returns as a variable-length record chain: a 16-bit type at +0, a 16-bit length at +2, advancing by that length. A type of 0xFFFF ends the walk and clears RAX to 0, a type of 4 goes straight to the test, and any record that survives has its qwords at +8 and +0x10 compared against the 16 bytes at 0x25C0 and 0x25C8. It returns no value of its own: RAX is left holding the matching record pointer, or 0 if the terminator was reached, and 0x364 tests RAX after the call and skips its port-0x1808 delay when it is non-zero.

name: delay_via_port_1808
comment: A polling delay on 16-bit I/O port 0x1808, run (ECX >> 0x16) + 1 times. The first pass adds ECX & 0x3FFFFF to the sampled value and every later pass adds the constant 0x400000, written into EDI just before the first inner loop; each pass compares the running total with a fresh sample, tests bit 0x17 of (total - sample) with bt and calls the pause at 0x320 while that bit is clear, so it spins until bit 0x17 of that difference comes set. Its only caller here is 0x1F44, which returns its own argument unchanged and discards this function's result.

name: locate_protocols_and_register_dispatch
comment: Caches the second argument at 0xD7E8 and its +0x60 and +0x58 members at 0xD798 and 0xD7D0 if they are not already set, then locates the protocol whose GUID constant is at 0x9E18 through the boot-services pointer at +0x140 of 0xD798 (the LocateProtocol shape; the GUID bytes are not in this listing). It calls the located object's vtable 0 with a stack byte and gives up if that byte is zero; on a non-zero byte it fetches the object's interface with vtable 1 into 0xD7A0, runs 0x84FC, 0x8390 and 0x8418 with the bytes at 0xD7A8 and 0xD7B8 flipped around them, and calls the registration routine at 0x1CFC.
