The status of the first failing step is what the function returns.

name: find_table_node_by_id
comment: Takes the table pointer from 0x1EB0 and walks it as a sequence of nodes with a 16-bit tag at offset 0 and a 16-bit total length at offset 2, following that length to the next node. A node is accepted only if its tag is 0xFFFF or 4 and the qwords at offsets 8 and 0x10 match the constants at 0x2278 and 0x2280; on a mismatch the walk continues from that node's length, so 0xFFFF is not an unconditional stop. It returns the matching node's pointer, which the entry point tests and skips its port delay over when non-zero. The first node's tag is read before any test of the pointer, so a zero returned by 0x1EB0 is dereferenced at 0x1F48 before the zero check at 0x1F53 can run; the tag values and the 16-byte constant are not decoded further.

name: scale_and_delay
comment: Multiplies RCX by 0x369E99, does one unsigned multiply-high against 0x431BDE82D7B634DB and shifts the high half right by 0x12, then passes the result in ECX to the port-0x1808 delay at 0x1EE4. Measured on the only two inputs its callers pass — 1 from 0x2484 and 10 from 0x1F78 — the result is 3 and 35, so the net effect is a multiply by about 3.58; this listing does not say what unit that is. It returns its original argument in RAX, not the quotient.

name: probe_msr_150
comment: Polls MSR 0x150 through 0x2484, writes it with wrmsr 0x150 as low dword 0 and high dword 7, with byte 7 of that dword then overwritten by the 0x80 stored at offset 7 of the 8-byte value, i.e. 0x80000007, polls again, then reads MSR 0x150 twice with a delay of 10 units (0x1F44) between the two reads; call them r1 and r2. It returns the low byte of r1's low dword only if (r1's high dword equals r2's, or r1's low dword equals r2's) and byte 4 of r1 — the low byte of its high dword — is zero; every other path, including a failed poll, returns 0. Nothing in the listing says which CPU feature MSR 0x150 corresponds to.

name: handle_gpu_clock_command
comment: Handles one of four sub-commands selected by EDX. EDX 0 reads the word at I/O port 0xFF43000B and EDX 1 the word at 0xFF43000D, replacing a value above 0x4B0 (1200) or 0x3E8 (1000) respectively with zero, then formatting it through 0x8B40 against the constants at 0xA6FC and 0xA700. EDX 2 (constant at 0xA6EC) and EDX 3 (0xA6F4) fetch the argument string with 0x16BC, validate it as decimal with 0x192C and convert it with 0x19A8, and a value over the same limit is refused by appending the messages at 0xA708/0xA730 or 0xA7C0/0xA7E8; otherwise the 16-bit value is placed at the head of 11 or 13 bytes and handed to 0x2648. The decompiler's symbol names for these constants read 'SetGC' and 'SetMC' and name the refusal and help lines 'GPU OverClocking' and 'VRAM OverClocking' - that is the module's own labelling of the ports, and nothing in this repository decodes what 0xFF43000x is.

name: read_msrs_610_606_1ad
comment: Fills 13 out-pointers from three MSR reads: MSR 0x610 bits 14:0 into the word at the 11th slot and bits 46:32 into the 12th, a word quotient of (MSR 0x610 & 0x7FFF) / (1 << ((MSR 0x606 & 0xF) - 1)) into the 1st, a zero word into the 2nd, and the eight bytes of MSR 0x1AD at shifts 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 and 56 into slots 3 to 10. It then walks the table at 0x2620, comparing (MSR 0x610 >> 17) & 0x7F against the odd byte of each pair and taking the even byte of the matching pair as the 13th output, defaulting to 1 when it reaches a pair whose even byte is 0xFF. What the table's entries mean is not decoded here.

name: submit_oc_descriptor
comment: Given a 0x30-byte buffer in RCX and an interface pointer in RDX, it calls the interface at offset 0x40 into a dword that must come back 0 and the one at 0x38 into a byte whose low nibble must be 0, returning -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFD or -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFA on those two failures. It then copies the 0x30 buffer to a local with 0x2C0 unless it is already there, sets the five-dword descriptor {0x50000, 0x1B, 0, 0x1C, 0} and calls vtable entry 0 with (0, &descriptor, 0x30, &out-size 0x30, 0, 8). If the descriptor's third dword is non-zero afterwards the call's success is replaced by -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFF9.

name: append_clock_help_text
comment: Writes the module's fixed help text for the clock commands into the output structure at RCX: it stores 2 to the flag dword at [RCX+0x14], clears the buffer through 0x19FC, and appends five NUL-terminated constants in order from 0xA878, 0xA898, 0xA8D0, 0xA910 and 0xA938, the last by a tail jump to the record writer at 0x1530. The decompiler names them 'Help: Display OC command' followed by the GetGC, GetMC, SetGC and SetMC help lines, so the text is a usage screen for the same four sub-commands 0x2028 handles. No port is touched here.

name: dispatch_clock_command
comment: Tests the output buffer against a fixed list of NUL-terminated constants in order - 0xA6DC, 0xA6E4, 0xA6EC, 0xA6F4 and 0xA6D4 - with the membership test at 0x15C4, and on the first four matches clears the qword at [RCX+0x18] and calls the sub-command handler 0x2028 with EDX 0, 1, 2 or 3 respectively. If none of the first four matches, it still clears [RCX+0x18], runs the same test against 0xA6D4 and calls the help writer 0x225C whatever the answer. The decompiler's symbol names for the five constants are '_GetGC_', '_GetMC_', '_SetGC_', '_SetMC_' and '_Help_'. Always returns 0.

name: locate_protocol_25b0_with_fallback
comment: Locates the protocol at GUID 0x25B0 and returns 1 if that succeeds. Otherwise it locates GUID 0x2520, calls its offset 0x40 into a dword that must be 0, and calls vtable entry 0 with (0, &{0x1DFF}, 4, &out {8}, 0, 7); it returns 0 unless that call succeeds, its status dword reads 0, and the preceding 0x40 check passed. If all of that holds it locates 0x25B0 once more and, only when that lookup returns exactly -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFF2, calls the boot-services entry at offset 0x80 with (0, 0x25B0, 0, 0) before returning 1.

name: wait_for_msr150_bit56
comment: Polls MSR 0x150 up to 1000 times: reads the 64-bit value, copies it to a scratch slot with 0x2C0, takes bit 7 of its top byte — bit 56 of the value — and calls the delay at 0x1F44(1) between samples. It returns 0 as soon as that bit reads 1, and -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFEE after 1000 consecutive samples with it clear, counted in a 16-bit accumulator against 0x3E8. 0x1F78 is its only caller in this module.

name: append_board_id_help_text
comment: Writes the module's board-ID help text into the output structure at RCX: stores 2 to [RCX+0x14], clears the buffer through 0x19FC, and appends the constants at 0xAA18, 0xAA48, 0xAA80, 0xAAA8, 0xAAD0, 0xAAF8, 0xAAD0, 0xAB20, 0xAB48 and 0xAAD0 again, the last by a tail jump to 0x1530. The decompiler's symbol names make the last two descriptive lines 'BIT0: LCD_Q_key' and 'BIT1: EC_Battery_Boost', and the neighbouring constant a 'SW_Board_ID table' heading. Those labels are the module's own strings: no port or register for either bit appears in this function, and none is decoded elsewhere in this repository.

name: read_modify_write_fixed_port_page
comment: Writes len = RDX bytes from the buffer at RCX into the 0x1000-byte page at 0xFF430000 + (offset & 0xFFF) with offset = R8, through the protocol interface cached at 0xD778. It returns 0x8000000000000001 if that interface is NULL and 0x8000000000000004 if len + offset exceeds 0x22000; otherwise it calls the interface's vtable entry +0x20, and for each page involved calls its Read at +0x00, patches the payload into the page buffer with the memcpy at 0x1180, then Write at +0x08 and a second Read at +0x10, finishing with vtable entry +0x28 and a return of 0. Any failing page returns 0x8000000000000007. The read-modify-write shape is what lets a caller change a few bytes of a fixed port block without knowing the rest of the page; what the ports themselves decode to is not established in this repository.

name: call_protocol_10_and_widen_result
comment: Builds a 0x30-byte structure on the stack with 0x00023370, then calls the method at offset 0x10 of the caller's third argument with (a second 0x30-byte stack buffer, 0x30, the low byte of the caller's second argument) and keeps the returned status byte in BL. If that byte is not 0xff it calls 0x0001daf4 with the first buffer, the constant at 0x25f50 and the second buffer - the listing sets only three of that callee's four arguments. It then widens the bytes of the first buffer into the caller's UTF-16 destination one byte per 16-bit word, stopping at the first NUL, terminates the destination with a zero word and returns the status byte in AL. What the 0x30-byte structure, the constant at 0x25f50 or the method at offset 0x10 encode is not decoded here.

name: set_oem_var_byte_in_0xb4_block
comment: Resolves a protocol through the pointer at 0xD790 (member +0xD0) with the GUID at 0x9040, then calls its first member with the variable GUID at 0xAB80, an attribute word of 7 at [RBP+0x6F], a size of 0xB4 at [RBP+0x77] and a data buffer at RBP-0x69 passed on the stack. If that read succeeds it stores the byte in CL at offset 14 of that buffer and calls member +0x10 with the same five arguments to write the block back; either status being negative returns with nothing stored or written. What the byte at offset 14 of the 0xB4 structure is, is not decoded here.

name: handle_set_tdr
comment: EDX selects the direction. With 0 it finds the argument after the keyword string at 0xAB70 (0x16BC, 0x192C, 0x19A8), writes the parsed byte to offset 0x12 of the 0xFF430000 block through 0x2648, appends it formatted with the template at 0xABA8, and calls 0x2804 to place the same byte at offset 14 of the 0xB4 variable block. With 1 it reads the byte at 0xFF430012 directly and appends it with the template at 0xABA0; any other value of EDX returns immediately. A missing or non-numeric argument is freed through member +0x58 of the object at 0xD7A0 and the string at 0xABC0 is appended instead. What the byte at offset 0x12 controls is not decoded here.

name: append_settdr_help
comment: Sets the 32-bit field at [RCX+0x14] to 2, clears the pending-text buffer with the call at 0x19FC and appends the three fixed strings at 0xABF0, 0xAC18 and 0xAC40 through 0x1530, the last by tail call. It reads and writes nothing else.

name: append_notebook_type_help
comment: Clears the text buffer with 0x19FC and appends the three strings at 0xAD50, 0xAD80 and 0xADB0, then formats and appends two entries from the 12-byte-stride record array at 0x9518 (the dword at the record and the qword at record-8, template 0xADE0), four from 0x9538 (template 0xAE20) and four more from 0x9658 (template 0xAE68), each through 0x8B40 into a buffer whose size 0x100 is passed in EDX. The second loop counts in EBP and the third reuses ESI, which the second loop never decrements, which is why all three loops terminate. What the records name is not decoded here.

name: set_notebook_type
comment: Finds the argument after the keyword at 0xAD34, tests it with 0x192C and parses it with 0x19A8, then frees it through member +0x58 of the object at 0xD7A0, and scans the two 12-byte records at 0x9518 for a dword match. On a hit it writes the parsed byte to offset 0x34 of the 0xFF430000 block through the writer pointer at 0x90D0 and appends the record's name (the qword at record-8) formatted with 0xAEF0, with a fifth format argument chosen between the strings at 0xAEE0 and 0xAEE9 according to the writer's status. A missing or non-numeric argument, a value of 2 or above, or a value matching no record instead stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at [RCX+0x18], appends 0xAF08, and then formats and appends both records at 0x9518 with the template 0xADE0. What the records name is not decoded here.

name: format_three_fields_into_string_ids
comment: Divides the 32-bit field at +0x20 of the structure in the first argument by 1000000 (magic multiply 0x431BDE83, shift 18) and formats the quotient through 0x680 into string id 0x17D8 of the object at 0x2B360, with the format string the decompiler labels a %2d.%2d MHz format at 0x25FD0. It likewise divides the byte at +0x2A by 100 (magic 0x51EB851F, shift 5) and formats that quotient with the %2d % format at 0x26000 into id 0x17DA. It then picks id 0x17E7 or 0x17E8 depending on whether the byte at +0x28 is zero, resolves it with 0x2CD4, formats the result into id 0x17DC, and tail-calls the method at +0x48 of the table at 0x29478 on the resolved string.

name: set_notebook_mode
comment: Identical in shape to 0x2D5C but keyed on the string at 0xAD3C and scanning the four 12-byte records at 0x9538: the argument is found with 0x16BC, tested with 0x192C, parsed with 0x19A8 and freed through member +0x58 of the object at 0xD7A0. A hit writes the parsed byte to offset 0x34 through the writer pointer at 0x90D0 and appends the record's name (qword at record-8) with the template 0xAF30, again with a fifth argument chosen between 0xAEE0 and 0xAEE9 by the writer's status. A missing or non-numeric argument, a value of 2 or above, or no match stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at [RCX+0x18], appends 0xAF08, and lists the four records with the template 0xAE20. What the records name is not decoded here.

name: update_setup_struct_and_watchdog_var
comment: Locates the interface for the GUID at 0x234B0 through [0x29478+0x140], calls its methods +0x40 and +0x38 for a 32-bit value and a byte, and only continues when the first is zero and the low nibble of the second is zero. It copies 0x30 bytes from the caller's structure into a stack copy when the addresses differ, fills that copy with the dwords 0x50000, 0x1B, 0, 0 and 0x1C, and passes it to the interface's method 0 with a size of 0x30. It then reads the variable whose name is at 0x26070 (decompiler label SaSetup) with GUID 0x238F0, stores [param+0x1C]/10000 (magic 0xD1B71759, shift 13) to 0x29581, writes the variable back, copies 0x30 bytes from 0x29780 into the stack structure, and if the 32-bit field at +0x18 or the bytes at +0x28 and +0x29 of the caller's structure differ from that copy writes a one-byte value of 1 to the variable at 0x26048 (decompiler label WdtPersistentData).

name: set_notebook_mode_table
comment: Parses the argument after the keyword at 0xAD44 and scans the four 12-byte records at 0x9658 for a dword match. On a hit it writes the parsed byte to offset 0x34 through the writer pointer at 0x90D0, then resolves a protocol through the pointer at 0xD790 (member +0xD0) with the GUID at 0x9040, reads the 0xB4 variable block (GUID 0xAB80, attribute 7), stores 1 at buffer offset 0x2F when the parsed byte is 0x22 or 0x24 and 0 when it is 0x21 or 0x23 (BL is cleared first, so any other value also leaves 0), and calls member +0x10 to write the block back; a negative status from either call skips the read-modify-write entirely. The success path appends the record's name (qword at record-8) with the template 0xAF48 and a fifth argument chosen between 0xAEE0 and 0xAEE9 by the writer's status; a miss stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at [RCX+0x18], appends 0xAF08 and lists the four records with 0xAE68. What the records or offset 0x2F mean is not decoded here.

name: refresh_icc_setup_from_sa_setup
comment: Zeroes an 8-byte buffer, and unless the interface pointer at 0x29288 is already set reads the variable whose name is at 0x26018 (decompiler label IccAdvancedSetupDataVar, GUID 0x23580) into that buffer through [0x29488+0x48] with a size of 8; if the lookup for 0x29288 fails it skips straight to the write-back with the result bytes left zero. When the byte at 0x29278 is zero it clears 0x30 bytes at 0x29750, sets the byte at 0x29764 to 1, calls 0x20A08 on that block and records success in 0x29278. It allocates 0x300 bytes, calls 0x20790 with three output slots and that buffer, copies the 0x30 bytes from 0x29750 into a stack record, stores the returned bytes in 0x2927C, 0x2927D and 0x2927E, computes ([0x29768]+5000)/10000 into a 16-bit stack field, and passes the record to 0x2E20. It then reads the variable at 0x26080 (decompiler label SetupVolatileData, GUID 0x23710) with a size of 0x97, calls the method at +0x40 of the interface in 0x29288 on the record, sets two more flag bytes from that result, derives one more from 0x29770 against 0x29774 and another from 0x29778, and writes the 8 bytes back to the first variable with attributes 3.

name: dispatch_notebook_command
comment: Clears the qword at [RCX+0x18] and then compares the command word against five fixed strings in turn with 0x15C4: 0xA6D4 routes to 0x2AC4, 0xAD2C to 0x2C20, 0xAD34 to 0x2D5C, 0xAD3C to 0x2ED4 and 0xAD44 to 0x304C, the first match winning and the function returning 0. If none matches it stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFD at [RCX+0x18], calls 0x2AC4, and returns that same value in RAX.

name: poll_icc_setup_state
comment: Resolves the interface for the GUID at 0x23720 through [0x29478+0x140] and then reads the variables at 0x26070 (SaSetup, GUID 0x238F0) and 0x26018 (IccAdvancedSetupDataVar, GUID 0x23580) into stack buffers, requiring the interface pointer at 0x29288 to be non-zero. It tracks the byte at offset 6 of the second buffer against the byte at 0x2974D (seeding that byte from 0x2927D when 0x29280 is still zero) and on the first change calls 0x20918 with the new value and sets 0x29280 and 0x29290 to 1. When 0x29280 is clear, a byte at offset 7 of the same buffer is non-zero and the byte at 0x29279 is non-zero, it multiplies the 16-bit field at offset 0 by 0x2710 into a stack slot, clears 0x29279, sets bytes in the stack record to 4, 1 and 0, and masks or sets bits 0x08, 0x10 or clears two bits of a 16-bit field according to the bytes at 0x29735 and 0x29736 before calling 0x3020 on the record. It finally calls the method at +0x70 of the table at 0x29478 on the first argument when that argument is non-zero.

name: append_setkbl_help
comment: Sets the 32-bit field at [RCX+0x14] to 2, clears the pending-text buffer with 0x19FC and appends the four fixed strings at 0xB0C8, 0xB0F0, 0xB120 and 0xB160 through 0x1530, the last by tail call. Nothing else is read or written.

name: dispatch_setkbl_command
comment: Compares the command word against three fixed strings with 0x15C4: 0xA6D4 routes to the help emitter 0x350C, 0xAF80 to 0x3340 with EDX=0, and 0xAF88 to 0x3340 with EDX=1. The qword at [RCX+0x18] is cleared before each of the three calls, and the function returns 0 on every path including the no-match one.

name: print_ledkb_status_bytes
comment: Formats and appends three lines, each printing eight consecutive bytes of the 0xFF430000 block one %02X at a time. The first reads the qword at 0xFF430014 (bytes 0x14 to 0x1B) and uses the template at 0xB190, the second reads the qword at 0xFF43001C (bytes 0x1C to 0x23) plus the byte at 0xFF43002C as a further argument and uses 0xB1B8, and the third reads the qword at 0xFF430024 (bytes 0x24 to 0x2B) and uses 0xB190 again. Each line goes through 0x8B40 into a buffer whose size 0x80 is passed in EDX and is appended with 0x1530. The text buffer is not cleared first, so the three lines are appended one after another. What the bytes mean is not decoded here.

name: write_secure_boot_mode_variables
comment: Saves the byte at 0x292CE and sets it to 1. It then reads eight variables in turn through [0x294A0+0x48] with the name pointers at 0x260A8 (decompiler label SecureVarPresent, 6 bytes into 0x292C8), 0x260D0 (SetupMode), 0x260E8 (SecureBoot), 0x26100 (VendorKeys), 0x26118 (VendorKeysNv), 0x26138 (AuditMode), 0x26150 (DeployedMode) and 0x26170 (DeploymentModeNv), each with a size of 1 except the first, and writes six of them back through 0x1EBD4 with the size, the buffer, the GUID and the name pointer in that order. VendorKeysNv and DeploymentModeNv are read but not written back, and the saved byte at 0x292CE is restored before the return.

name: handle_ledkb_set_data
comment: With EDX=1 it finds the argument after the keyword at 0xAF70, splits the string at the first space, and loops up to eight times: each token is tested with 0x192C and parsed with 0x19A8, and the first token additionally has to be at most 0x1A and to have bit (value AND 0x1F) set in the mask 0x04100100. Every byte is stored at [RSP+0x30+index], and depending on the first token (0x08, 0x14 or 0x1A) the byte is also written to offset index+0x14, index+0x1C or index+0x24 of the 0xFF430000 block through 0x2648, with the 0x14 case also setting a flag that is later written to offset 0x2C. The eight collected bytes are then read out of the 0xB4 variable block (protocol from 0x9040, GUID 0xAB80, attribute 7, size 0xB4) and copied by 0x8E40 to buffer offset 0x0F when the first token is 0x1A or to offset 0x17 when it is 0x08, with no copy at all for 0x14. EDX=0 goes straight to 0x35D4, and bad input frees the argument, appends the strings at 0xB1E8, 0xB208 and 0xB228 (or 0xB268) and writes nothing. What the eight-byte block and the three offsets mean is not decoded here.

name: classify_secure_var_certs
comment: Loops over the name-pointer table at 0x25660 and the matching table at 0x25620, writing a per-entry state into the bytes at 0x292C8 plus the index: 0 left alone, 1 when the first read through [0x294A0+0x48] returns 0x8000000000000005 and a retry with an allocated 4-byte-sized buffer succeeds, 2 or 3 when 0x1EDD4 finds a record in the 0x28-byte table produced by 0x22FC0 (3 if the match is not the last entry), and 4 when a record matches one of the 0x10-byte GUIDs at 0x23960 or 0x23760 and the object at 0x292D0 (resolved for 0x23640) produces a 0x20-byte value at 0x29298 matching neither 0x241D8 nor 0x241B8. The record walk reads its stride from the dword at +0x10 and rejects values outside 0x4C to 0x70000. Each entry's state selects a string id from 0x19BC to 0x19C0, which is formatted through 0x5FA4 and 0x1C0F8 into the 0x190-byte buffer at 0x29AD0 and then handed to 0x1E908 with the word at 0x26268 plus twice the index. After the loop it writes the six bytes at 0x292C8 back to the variable at 0x260A8 with attributes 2 and calls 0x3648.

name: append_ledkb_help
comment: Sets the 32-bit field at [RCX+0x14] to 2, clears the pending-text buffer with 0x19FC and appends the four fixed strings at 0xB2A8, 0xB2E0, 0xB320 and 0xB160 through 0x1530, the last by tail call.

name: dispatch_ledkb_command
comment: Compares the command word against three fixed strings with 0x15C4: 0xA6D4 routes to the help emitter 0x3A08, 0xAF60 to 0x35D4, and 0xAF70 to 0x377C with EDX=1. The qword at [RCX+0x18] is cleared before each call and the function returns 0 on every path; the 0xAF60 path also stores a zero byte at [RSP+0x38], which the call to 0x35D4 does not read.

name: append_adaptor_type_help
comment: Clears the text buffer with 0x19FC and appends the three strings at 0xB388, 0xB3B8 and 0xB3E8, then formats and appends eight entries from the 12-byte-stride record array at 0x98A8 (the dword at the record and the qword at record-8, template 0xADE0) through 0x8B40 into a buffer whose size 0x100 is passed in EDX. What the records name is not decoded here.

name: get_adaptor_type_name
comment: Reads one byte at offset 0x33 of the 0xFF430000 block through the reader pointer at 0x90D8 and compares it against the dword at +8 of each of the eight 12-byte records at 0x98A8. On a hit it formats the qword at record-8 with the template at 0xB418 and appends it; if no record matches it stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at [RCX+0x18] and appends the string at 0xB438 instead. The records themselves are not decoded here.

name: set_adaptor_type
comment: Finds the argument after the keyword at 0xAD34, tests it with 0x192C, parses it with 0x19A8, frees it through member +0x58 of the object at 0xD7A0, and scans the eight 12-byte records at 0x98A8 for a dword match. On a hit it writes the parsed byte to offset 0x33 of the 0xFF430000 block through the writer pointer at 0x90D0 and appends the record's name (qword at record-8) formatted with 0xB458, with a fifth format argument chosen between 0xAEE0 and 0xAEE9 according to the writer's status. A missing or non-numeric argument, or a value matching no record, stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at [RCX+0x18], appends 0xAF08 and then formats and appends all eight records with the template 0xADE0. What the records name is not decoded here.

name: append_me_unlock_help
comment: Clears the text buffer with 0x19FC and appends the four fixed strings at 0xB478, 0xB4B0, 0xB500 and 0xB520 through 0x1530, the last by tail call. Unlike the other help emitters in this module it does not set the 32-bit field at [RCX+0x14] to 2 first.

name: set_me_region_lock
comment: Finds the argument after the keyword at 0xAD34, tests it with 0x192C, parses it with 0x19A8, frees it through member +0x58 of the object at 0xD7A0, and rejects any value above 1. Otherwise it reads a byte with 0x82F4 keyed 0x41, and a negative status there appends 0xB578 and stops. For a value of 0 it clears bit 4 of that byte and appends 0xB598, for a value of 1 it sets bit 4 and appends 0xB5B0, and the modified byte is then written back with 0x8294 keyed 0x41, with a negative status there appending 0xB5F0. A missing, non-numeric or out-of-range argument stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at [RCX+0x18] and appends 0xAF08, 0xB618 and 0xB640. The listing shows only the call shape of 0x82F4 and 0x8294 with key 0x41, so what bit 4 of that byte controls is not decoded here.

name: print_usb_light_bar_mode
comment: Formats and appends three lines, each printing eight consecutive bytes of the 0xFF430000 block one %02X at a time under a different leading template: the qword at 0xFF43003A (bytes 0x3A to 0x41) with 0xB6D8, the qword at 0xFF43004A (bytes 0x4A to 0x51) with 0xB708, and the qword at 0xFF430042 (bytes 0x42 to 0x49) with 0xB738. Each line goes through 0x8B40 into a buffer whose size 0x80 is passed in EDX and is appended with 0x1530. The text buffer is not cleared first, so the three lines are appended one after another. What the bytes mean is not decoded here.

name: append_usb_light_bar_help
comment: Sets the 32-bit field at [RCX+0x14] to 2, clears the pending-text buffer with 0x19FC and appends the eight fixed strings at 0xB8D0, 0xB910, 0xB958, 0xB768, 0xB7A0, 0xB7F0, 0xB840 and 0xB160 through 0x1530, the last by tail call.

name: dispatch_usb_light_bar_command
comment: Compares the command word against three fixed strings with 0x15C4: 0xA6D4 routes to the help emitter 0x44EC, 0xB6B8 to 0x40B8 after re-resolving the protocol at 0x9040 into the module global 0xD938, and 0xB6C8 to 0x424C with EDX=1. The qword at [RCX+0x18] is cleared before each call and the function returns 0 on every path.

name: report_flash_write_status
comment: Does nothing when the status in RDX is non-negative. When it is negative it stores that status at [RCX+0x18] and maps it to one of four strings: -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF to the one at 0xA698, -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFC to 0xB9E8, -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFF9 to 0xBA00, and anything else to 0xBA18. The module's own string table labels the first three 'Flash protocol not exist', 'Data size exceed' and 'Flash access failed' and the fourth 'Unknow error'; each is appended with 0x1530 after 0x19FC has cleared the text buffer and after the 32-bit field at [RCX+0x14] has been set to 2. The correspondence is read off the four compared constants, not from anything the callers of this function do.

name: var_read_by_index_forwarder
comment: Takes the variable name from the table at 0x25660 indexed by the low byte of the first argument, selects the GUID at 0x234A0 when that index is 4 or greater and 0x23570 otherwise, and tail-calls 0x22A5C with the name, that GUID, zero, the other of the two GUIDs, the second argument and the third and fourth arguments unchanged.

name: check_named_variables
comment: Stores its first argument in the global at 0x29C60 and returns 0 unless the second argument is 6 or less and the interface at 0x292C0 is non-zero. After a call to 0x6518 it loops over the name table at 0x25660 from the second argument (or from 0 when that argument is 6) to 5, and for each non-null name reads the variable through [0x294A0+0x48] with the GUID at 0x23570, or 0x234A0 for index 4 and above, retrying once with an allocated buffer when the first read returns 0x8000000000000005. It opens the resulting handle for the GUID at 0x237B0 through [0x29498+0x98], calls that interface's methods +0x08 and +0x28, and on failure formats the string id 0x19F1 with the name and hands it to the method at +0x20 of the object at 0x292C0. If every index succeeded it formats 0x19F3 with the success count into 0x29AD0, formats 0x19F2 from that buffer, and sends the result to the same method.

name: write_oem_var_word_and_three_bytes
comment: Resolves a protocol through the pointer at 0xD790 (member +0xD0) with the GUID at 0x9040, then calls its first member with the variable GUID at 0xAB80, an attribute word of 7 at [RSP+0x30], a size of 0xB4 at [RSP+0x38] and a data buffer at [RSP+0x50]. On success it stores the 16-bit value in CX as a word at buffer offset 4 and the three argument bytes (DL, R8B, R9B) at offsets 6, 7 and 8, then calls member +0x10 with the same five arguments to write the block back; either status being negative returns with nothing stored or written. What those five bytes of the 0xB4 structure mean is not decoded here.

name: check_object_supports_label

name: merge_named_object_into_buffer

name: forward_to_00001130

name: empty_stub_return_zero

name: locate_iface_6070_then_query

name: run_table_range_dispatch

name: range_table_contains

name: dispatch_setapctrl_command

name: call_interface_0x50_with_arg_6

It returns that stack qword, or 0 if the call's return value has bit 63 set. The meaning of the 6, and of the interface at 0x6118 itself, is not decoded by this listing.

name: dispatch_on_table_range_test

RCX still holds the array pointer at both jumps, and the callees are reached by jmp rather than call.

name: find_config_entry_by_key

Otherwise the array at [0x6100 + 0x70] is walked, element count from [0x6100 + 0x68] and element size 0x18, comparing each element's first two qwords against the two qwords at 0x6050 and 0x6058; a match caches the element's third qword into 0x6120 and returns it, and exhausting the array returns the cache still zero. name: prime_config_entry_cache
comment: Calls the lookup at 0x58E4, whose side effect is populating the cache at 0x6120, discards the returned pointer and returns 0. No other state is touched.

name: tailcall_cached_interface
comment: Tail-jumps through the first qword of the pointer cached at 0x6138 when that pointer is non-zero, setting no arguments beforehand. With the pointer null it returns 0x800000000000000F, the value UEFI assigns to EFI_NOT_READY.

name: call_interface_0xd0_with_guid_6040

The bytes of the value at 0x6040 are module data and are not decoded by this listing, and the identity of the 0xD0 method is not established here.

name: get_modify_set_oem_var_byte

name: append_color_calibration_help

name: append_rwblock0_help

name: append_rwblock0adv_help

name: append_u16_string

The second argument therefore acts as a byte offset that is compensated for in the destination address.

name: alloc_u16_copy_of_ascii

name: append_display_mode_help

name: append_setmode_help

Otherwise it stores -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE at [RCX+0x18] and appends the strings at 0xAF08, 0xD150 and 0xD188.

name: fill_status_row_from_entry

No caller inside this module is visible in the listings.

name: append_turbo_mode_help

A match formats the template at 0xD400 with that entry's string pointer into a 0x100-byte stack buffer, clears the text buffer and appends it; otherwise -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE is stored at [RCX+0x18], the buffer is cleared and the string at 0xD418 is appended.

comment: Parses the argument after the keyword at 0xAD34 (0x16BC, 0x192C, 0x19A8) and compares the resulting byte against the dword at +8 of each of the two entries at 0x9CD0. A match calls the writer at 0x90D0 with size 1 and offset 0x36 (its return value is not tested), then formats the template at 0xD438 with the matched entry's string pointer into a 0x100-byte stack buffer and appends it. With no match -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE is stored at [RCX+0x18], the string at 0xAF08 is appended, and the two entries at 0x9CD8 and 0x9CE4 are formatted with 0xADE0 and appended in turn; the input is freed on both paths.

name: build_and_submit_opaque_struct
comment: Zeroes three stack structures (0x38, 0x2C and 0x10 bytes at RBP+0x17, RBP-0x19, RBP-0x29) and fills the 0x38 one with 0x4C4B40 at +0, the caller's 4th argument at +8, 0x1000 at +0x10, a zero byte at +0x24 and pointers to the other two at +0x28 and +0x30; the 0x2C one gets (x & 0xFFFFFF06) | 6 at +0, byte 4 at +4, the caller's 2nd argument at +8 and its 3rd at +0x14. What the structure and the callee are is not decoded here, and no caller inside this module is visible in the listings.

name: append_keyboard_light_help
comment: Sets [RCX+0x14] to 2, clears the text buffer and appends the three strings at 0xD478, 0xD4B0 and 0xD500 through 0x1530, the last as a tail call.

comment: Parses the argument after the keyword at 0xAD34 (0x16BC, 0x192C, 0x19A8). A value below 2 is freed, written through the setter pointer at 0x90D0 with size 1 and offset 0x35, and then used to format the template at 0xD5A8 into a 0x100-byte stack buffer that is appended. A value of 2 or more appends only the string at 0xC818, and a missing or non-numeric argument appends the three strings at 0xD530, 0xD558 and 0xD580; nothing is written on either of those paths.

name: append_model_id_help
comment: Clears the text buffer, appends the strings at 0xD630, 0xD660 and 0xD690, then ten times formats the 3-word entry at 0x9D88 (advancing the pointer by 0xC each time) with the template at 0xADE0 into a 0x100-byte stack buffer and appends the result.

name: get_model_id_name
comment: Reads one byte with the reader pointer at 0x90D8 (size 1, offset 0x39) and compares it against the dword at +8 of each of the ten entries at 0x9D80. A match formats the template at 0xD6B0 with that entry's string pointer into a 0x100-byte stack buffer, clears the text buffer and appends it; otherwise -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE is stored at [RCX+0x18], the buffer is cleared and the string at 0xD6C8 is appended.

name: update_ec_82_from_setup_byte_7cd
comment: Allocates 0x7D8 bytes and reads the variable named at RVA 0x262C8 under the GUID {ec87d643-4bb5-eba4-3e3fe5a1-a90db236} through the module's variable wrapper 0x1EA50; on failure it frees the buffer and returns the status. On success it reads EC RAM address 0x82 (0x1BA9C) into a byte, and rewrites it as follows: if the Setup byte at offset 0x7CD is 1 then (value & 0xFD) | 1, if that byte is 0 then value | 3, otherwise unchanged. The modified byte is written back to EC address 0x82 with 0x1BA3C (the 0xA3 07 / 0xA2 lo / 0xA5 sequence) and the 0x7D8-byte variable is written back with 0x1EBD4; the function returns 0. What EC 0x82 holds is not recorded in this repository.

name: set_model_id
comment: Parses the argument after the keyword at 0xAD34 (0x16BC, 0x192C, 0x19A8) and compares the resulting byte against the dword at +8 of each of the ten entries at 0x9D80. A match calls the writer at 0x90D0 with size 1 and offset 0x39 (its return value is not tested), then formats the template at 0xD6E8 with the matched entry's string pointer into a 0x100-byte stack buffer and appends it. With no match -0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFE is stored at [RCX+0x18], the string at 0xAF08 is appended, and the ten entries at 0x9D88 are formatted with 0xADE0 and appended in turn; the input is freed on both paths.

name: hex_char_to_value
comment: Converts one ASCII character in CL to a nibble value: '0'-'9' return c - 0x30, and the branch at 0x7E80 accepts (c - 0x61) <= 0x19, so 'a'-'f' have 0x20 subtracted before c - 0x37 while 'A'-'F' skip that subtraction; both give 10-15. Any other character falls through the same subtraction and yields 16 or more - the range tests are in the callers (0x7F98, 0x8758), not here.

name: strncmp_bounded
comment: Byte-wise comparison of the strings in RCX and RDX with the count in R8 as a limit: it returns 0 immediately when that count is 0, and otherwise stops at the first NUL byte on either side, at a mismatch, or when the remaining count drops to 1, returning (int)*s1 - (int)*s2 sign-extended to 64 bits. With the standard x86-64 argument registers the count is the third argument, so the zero-count case reports equality rather than a mismatch.

name: nop_stub
comment: Three bytes: c2 00 00, a return with an immediate 0. The function reads no memory, no I/O port and no register, leaves no observable state behind, and nothing in its own three bytes says what it was for, so its role is left unresolved.

name: strnlen_cap_1e6
comment: Returns the length of the NUL-terminated string in RCX: 0 when the pointer is NULL or the first byte is 0, otherwise it counts while the counter is below 0xF4240 (1000000), and returns the sentinel 0xF4241 (1000001) if no terminator is found within that bound. The scan tests [RCX + count] with the count already incremented, so the last byte examined is the one at index 0xF4240.

name: insert_keyed_entry_and_resolve_string
comment: Appends one 0x20-byte record to the array held through the caller's first argument, incrementing the count at the caller's second: a fresh count*0x20 buffer is zeroed, the old contents are copied around an insertion point chosen as the length of the leading run of records whose first 8 bytes are equal, the old buffer is freed, and the new record is written at that index with (*(UINT32*)(arg3+0x48) & 0x10) at +0, *(UINT64*)(arg3+8) at +8 and a newly allocated string buffer at +0x10. That buffer is sized 2*(length of the CHAR16 string at arg3+0x50)+6, formatted with 0x1E3B4 from the format at RVA 0x26250 (or 0x25B68 when the value at +0 is not 0x10), then the formatted text is resolved to a 16-bit index by 0x7D2C and stored at +0x18, and the buffer is cleared and reformatted with 0x25B68 before the caller's array pointer is updated.

name: strtoull_base10
comment: Parses a decimal string into the 64-bit value at the pointer in R8. It returns 0x8000000000000002 unless the string is non-NULL, the out-pointer is non-NULL and the length from 0x7ED0 is below 0xF4241; it then skips spaces and tabs and leading '0's, accumulates value = value*10 + digit, and stops at the first non-digit, returning 0 with the partial value left in the output. Overflow is caught by the standard test value > (UINT64_MAX - digit)/10, computed here as the high half of (~digit * 0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD) shifted right 3; on overflow the output is set to 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF and 0x8000000000000003 is returned.

name: strtoull_base16
comment: Parses a hexadecimal string into the 64-bit value at the pointer in R8, with the same argument and length checks as 0x7EF4 (0x8000000000000002 when they fail). After skipping spaces, tabs and leading '0's it accepts a following 'x'/'X' only when the character before it is '0', converts each digit through 0x7E68, and accumulates value = value*16 + digit until the first non-hex character, returning 0. Overflow is caught by value > (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF - digit) >> 4, which sets the output to 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF and returns 0x8000000000000003.

name: write_port_wait_status_bit1
comment: Waits until bit 1 of a status port reads clear, then writes the byte in DL to that same port. The port is 0x64 when the first argument is 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise; the poll re-reads it up to 0x20000 times, calling the delay at 0x8D58 with 15 between reads, and returns 0x8000000000000007 if that limit is reached. Returns 0 after the write. The listing does not identify what is behind the port.

name: drain_port_data_to_port_80
comment: While bit 0 of the status port (0x64 when the first argument is 0x60, 0x66 otherwise) is set, reads the companion data port (0x60 or 0x62) and writes the byte to I/O port 0x80, calling the delay at 0x8D58 with 5000 and re-reading the status each time. The loop is bounded at 0x20000 iterations and returns 0x8000000000000007 if the bit never clears; otherwise it returns 0, having written nothing when the bit was clear to begin with.

name: wait_status_bit1_clear
comment: Polls bit 1 of the status port (0x64 when the first argument is 0x60, 0x66 otherwise) until it reads clear, delaying 15 via 0x8D58 between reads and giving up after 0x20000 polls. This is the same poll 0x8068 performs before its write, but on its own it writes nothing. Returns 0 on success, 0x8000000000000007 on timeout.

name: write_bytes_a3_a2_a5
comment: Calls 0x81CC three times with a fixed first argument of 0x62: the byte pair (0xA3, 7), then (0xA2, the third argument), then (0xA5, the fourth argument), stopping and returning as soon as one of those calls returns a negative status. Because 0x62 differs from each second argument, the port pair selected inside 0x81CC is the 0x66/0x62 one on all three passes. Returns 0 when all three succeed.

name: read_data_port_after_a4
comment: Calls 0x81CC with (0x62, 0xA3, 7) and then with (0x62, 0xA2, the third argument), writes 0xA4 to port 0x66 through 0x8068, then polls bit 0 of port 0x66 until it is set (delay 15, limit 0x20000) and stores the byte read from port 0x62 through the fourth argument. A negative status from any earlier step is returned immediately, a poll timeout returns 0x8000000000000007, and otherwise it returns 0.

name: locate_9df8_or_call_9e08
comment: Two guarded one-time initialisations selected by the byte at 0xD7A8. When that byte is 0 and the cached pointer at 0xD7C8 is 0 and the byte at 0xD7B8 is 0, it calls the +0x140 entry of the table at 0xD798 (the LocateProtocol slot in the Boot Services layout, by the layout of the other entries this module takes from that table) with the 16 bytes at 0x9DF8, a zero search type, and 0xD7C8 as the output pointer. When 0xD7A8 is nonzero it instead requires 0xD7B0 == 0, 0xD7B8 == 0 and [0xD7A0] != 0, then tail-jumps to [0xD7A0+0xD0] with 0x9E08, 0 and 0xD7B0 as the three arguments, so that callee's status becomes the return value. Guards not met gives 0x8000000000000003; the callee at +0xD0 is not identified by this listing.

name: acquire_9010_or_call_9030
comment: With the byte at 0xD7A8 clear: returns 0 if the handle at 0xD7E0 is already set, returns 0x8000000000000003 if the byte at 0xD7B8 is 1, and otherwise raises and restores the TPL through the +0x18 and +0x20 entries of the table at 0xD798 (RaiseTPL/RestoreTPL in the Boot Services layout) with the new level 0x1F, fails with 0x8000000000000003 if the level returned exceeds 0x10, and then calls the +0x140 entry with the 16 bytes at 0x9010 into 0xD7E0, zeroing the cached handle if that call returns negative. With 0xD7A8 set it instead returns 0 if 0xD7C0 is already set, returns 0x8000000000000003 if [0xD7A0] is 0, and otherwise calls [0xD7A0+0xD0] with 0x9030, 0 and an output pointer to 0xD7C0, zeroing the cache on a negative return. The +0xD0 callee is not identified by this listing.

name: dispatch_image_section_table_to_protocol
comment: Requires the WORD at the input to be 0x5A4D and the WORD at input+*(UINT32*)(input+0x3C) to be 0x5A56, and returns 0 unless both hold. It locates the protocol whose GUID is at RVA 0x23640 (global 0x29360), allocates (WORD at header+6 + 1) * 0x28 bytes, gathers the 0x28-byte records at input+0x18+*(UINT16*)(header+0x14) and insertion-sorts them by the DWORD at +0x14 of each record, then builds two parallel arrays (record+4 added to the base, and the DWORD at +0x10) for at most 0x1C non-zero entries, appends one trailing entry carrying the caller's second argument less the header offsets, and calls vtable entry +0x10 of that protocol with (This, GUID at 0x23510, count, &array1, &array2, address 0x29328). It returns 1 when that call's status is non-negative and 0 otherwise, and frees the array. Which image format the two magic words belong to is not established from this listing alone.

name: find_record_by_16byte_key
comment: Walks the record array whose pointer is at [0xD7A0+0xA0] using the count at [0xD7A0+0x98], stepping 0x18 bytes per entry and comparing each entry's first 16 bytes with the fixed 16 bytes at 0x9E30 through the comparator at 0x8B60. On the first match it returns the entry's third qword (offset 0x10); with an empty or absent array, or with no match, it returns 0. The listing does not establish what the 16-byte key identifies.

name: format_number_radix
comment: Writes the 64-bit value in RCX into the buffer at RDX as digits in the base given by R8, least significant digit first, so the caller at 0x8758 reverses the result. Digits below 10 get 0x30 added and the rest 0x57, which maps 10 to 'a'; a zero value writes a single '0'. The magnitude used is the 32-bit value by default, the full 64-bit value when the fourth argument is nonzero, and the negation when the base is 10 - after which a value with the sign bit set gets a trailing '-' - while any value whose sign bit is clear is used as is. It NUL-terminates and returns a pointer to that terminator.

name: parse_number_saturating
comment: Skips spaces and tabs, accepts an optional '-' and '+', and accumulates decimal digits (and A-F/a-F) into a 32-bit register as value*10 + digit, writing the end pointer through the second argument. On overflow it clamps to 0x7FFFFFFF, or to 0x80000000 when the sign byte is 0xFF, and returns the clamped value multiplied by that sign byte, so a too-large input comes back as INT32_MAX or INT32_MIN. An empty string stores the pointer and returns 0; the accumulation is by ten whatever letters appear.

name: status_code_to_string
comment: Maps an EFI_STATUS-sized value in RCX to a string in the module's tables, returning the string at 0xD700 (labelled EFI_SUCCESS in the module's C) for 0. Values with the sign bit clear go to the table at 0x9E26 with stride 0x1A (only 0-4 accepted) or, when bit 0x2000000000000000 is set, to the table at 0x9EB0 with stride 0x23 (only 0-1); values with the sign bit set go to 0x9F87 (low bits 0-0x1E, bit 63 only), 0x9F00 (low bits 0-2, bits 63 and 61) or 0x9F47 (low bits 0-2, bits 63 and 62), stride 0x19. Anything outside those ranges returns 0. The names the decompiled C attaches to the tables (EFI_WARN_INTERRUPT_SOURCE_PENDING, EFI_INTERRUPT_PENDING, EFI_NOT_AVAILABLE_YET, EFI_DBE_BOF) are labels of the first string in each table, not values the listing assigns.

name: format_string_va_list
comment: The module's formatted-output routine, taking (buffer, size, format, argument list) and returning the number of bytes written, or -1 when either the buffer or the format is null. It copies literal bytes, expands %%, takes a field width from the next argument when '*' follows the '%', takes zero padding from a leading '0', and dispatches on the conversion character: 's' and 'a' copy a char string, 'S' a CHAR16 string two bytes at a time, 'c' one byte, 'g' and 'G' 16 bytes read from the argument as a u32, a u16, a u16 and eight bytes - the EFI_GUID field layout - through a recursive call with the module's own format string at 0xD710 (uppercased afterwards for 'G'), 'r' an EFI_STATUS through 0x8690, and 'd', 'i', 'x', 'X', 'p' (optionally 'l'-prefixed) numbers through 0x85BC and 0x8548 with the base from the conversion. Every write decrements the remaining count, and running out of room terminates the output with a NUL and returns the length so far.

name: resolve_handle_index_from_names
comment: Returns EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER if the fifth argument is NULL. It calls gBS LocateHandleBuffer for the protocol GUID at RVA 0x237B0, allocates count*0x28 bytes and for each handle opens the protocol at GUID 0x23690, converts its contents with 0x1EE4C to an ASCII string, duplicates it as CHAR16 with 0x5F1C, resolves it to a 16-bit index with 0x7D2C and stores that index at record offset 0 with a zero status byte at +0x20; a handle whose protocol cannot be opened gets index 0 and status 2. It then asks entry +0x68 of the service in global 0x29350 for an index with (global 0x2A170, 0x19C5, 0, table, count, &index), writes the handle at that index to the second argument, clears the fifth, and when the first argument is non-zero calls 0x8098 with that handle and the service's success as its second argument. If LocateHandleBuffer failed, the strings 0x19F9 and 0x19FA are loaded into the two module buffers and passed to entry +0x20 of 0x29350 with mode 1 instead.

name: add_string_keyed_entry
comment: Returns immediately if the second argument is 6 or more. It loads the HII string 0x19F4 into the buffer at RVA 0x29CC0 and, for selection 5, string 0x19F6 into 0x29FE0, otherwise zeroes 0x29FE0, loads 0x19F5 into 0x29E50 and formats 0x29FE0 with the format string at table 0x25660[selection] (0x1E3B4), then calls entry +0x20 of the service in global 0x29350 with (0x29CC0, 0x29FE0, mode 1 or 3, &status). If the status byte is still zero after a retry with string 0x19F7 and mode 3, it submits mode 1 with no data; otherwise it looks up the blob for (selection, 0x19DE) through 0x9500, wraps it in a fresh 0x28-byte header initialised by 0x22D6C with type 2 and the blob copied to header+0x28, and passes it to 0x4618 with mode 3, calls 0x95E4 if that succeeded, and reports the returned status by formatting the format at 0x262D4 into 0x29E50 before a final mode-1 call. Any failure path frees both buffers and returns without a status code.

name: format_string_1arg
comment: Stores its fourth argument in a one-element stack slot, points the argument list at that slot and tail-calls the formatter at 0x8758. It is the single-argument form of the same routine, which the caller uses for the %g and %r conversions. Returns whatever the formatter returns.

name: match_key_at_9e30
comment: Compares the 16 bytes at RCX with the fixed 16 bytes at 0x9E30: it first byte-compares 8 - (RCX & 7) bytes when the input and the constant share the same misalignment, then compares qwords while RCX is at or below RCX+8, then the remaining bytes up to RCX+0x10. Returns 0 when all 16 bytes match, otherwise the sign-extended difference of the first mismatching byte.

name: address_in_recorded_range
comment: Returns 1 when the address in RCX lies inside one of the ranges described by the 0x20-byte records at the pointer held in 0xD930, with the entry count in 0xD928; each record is a base qword at +0 and a size qword at +8, and the test is base <= address < base + size. A count of 0 returns 0 immediately. Only bit 0 of the return value is ever set or cleared.

name: create_object_type_6
comment: Calls the +0x50 entry of the table at 0xD790 with the constant 6, the second argument passed through unchanged, and a stack out-pointer, and returns the value written there; when the call returns a negative status the out-pointer is zeroed first, so a failure returns 0. Nothing in this listing identifies what the +0x50 entry is, or what the type 6 argument means.

name: free_range_buffer
comment: Tests the buffer pointer held at 0xD930 with the range check at 0x8BDC and tail-jumps: to the +0x58 entry of the table at 0xD790 with that pointer when it lies inside a recorded range, and otherwise to the +0x48 entry of the table at 0xD788, which is the FreePool slot in the UEFI Boot Services layout. Both paths pass the same pointer in RCX and the callee's return value becomes this function's.

name: get_config_table_by_guid
comment: Walks the count at [0xD780+0x68] and the 0x18-byte records at [0xD780+0x70], comparing each record's first 16 bytes with the 16-byte identifier at 0x9070, and caches the third qword of the matching record (offset 0x10) at 0xD7F0 before returning it. Those two offsets and the 0x18-byte record layout are those of EFI_SYSTEM_TABLE's configuration table, so this is a lookup by 16-byte identifier, but the identifier at 0x9070 is not decoded here. It returns the cached value without searching when 0xD7F0 is already set, and 0 if the count is 0 or nothing matches.

name: wait_port_1808_ticks
comment: Waits on the 24-bit counter read from I/O port 0x1808. The argument is split into a tick target (argument & 0x3FFFFF) and a repeat count of (argument >> 22) + 1; each repetition reads the counter, masks it to 24 bits, adds the target, then re-reads in a loop until bit 23 of (target - counter) is set, calling the spin helper at 0x1260 between reads. Testing that bit is what makes the wait work across the counter's 24-bit wrap. The port is named as the listing gives it; what clocks it is not decoded here.

name: delay_by_units
comment: Converts the count in RCX into counter ticks by multiplying it by 0x369E99 (3579545), taking the high 64 bits of that product times the magic constant 0x431BDE82D7B634DB, and shifting right 18, which yields 3.579545 ticks per input unit, then calls the wait at 0x8CF8 with that value and returns the original count. The unit is not established by the listing; the module's callers pass 15 and 5000.

name: memmove_overlap_safe
comment: Copies the byte count in R8 from the source in RDX to the destination in RCX. When the ranges overlap with the destination above the source (destination - source <= count) it sets the direction flag, biases both pointers by the count and copies backwards from the ends; otherwise it copies forwards. It then byte-aligns the pair with a rep movsb when both share a misalignment, copies count>>3 qwords with rep movsq, and finishes the count&7 bytes with rep movsb. Returns the original destination pointer.

name: walk_table_entries_and_count_responses
comment: Stores its first argument in global 0x2A170 and returns 0 unless the second argument is 6 or less and the service pointer in global 0x29350 is non-NULL. It resolves a handle and a name through 0x8850, then loops over the entries of the pointer table at RVA 0x25660 starting at the second argument (6 is treated as 0, and the loop runs to the end of the table when the first attempt succeeded), asking entry +0x48 of the service in global 0x294A0 for each entry's size with the descriptor table at 0x23570 (entries below 4) or 0x234A0, allocating the buffer and retrying when that returns NOT_FOUND. For each entry it then opens the protocol GUID at RVA 0x237B0 on the handle and walks a four-deep chain of interface getters (+0x8, +0x8, +0x18, +0x8, +0x28) with the table entry and the status 0x8000000000000003, counting the successes in R13B and reporting a failure by loading string 0x19F1 and calling entry +0x20 of 0x29350. When the walk reaches the end of the table with at least one success it loads strings 0x19F3 and 0x19F2, formats the count into 0x29FE0 and calls entry +0x20 with mode 1; the function always returns 0.

name: read_named_blob_for_selection
comment: Returns 0x800000000000000F unless the first argument is below 6, and zeroes the caller's size pointer. It asks entry +0x48 of the service in global 0x294A0 for the entry named by table 0x25660[first argument] with the descriptor table at 0x23570 (index below 4) or 0x234A0, passing NULL for the buffer; on NOT_FOUND it allocates the reported size, retries with that buffer, and on a second failure returns 0x800000000000000F. On success it hands the buffer, its size and the second argument (a string id such as 0x19DE) to 0x9FEC and returns that call's status. The service behind 0x294A0 is not identified from this listing.

name: classify_table_entries_and_register
comment: Walks the pointer table at RVA 0x25660 until an entry is NULL. Per entry it asks entry +0x48 of the service in global 0x294A0 for a blob (allocating on NOT_FOUND and copying it with 0x22FC0), and classifies the result into a state byte in the array at RVA 0x29358: 1 when the variable is absent, 2 or 3 when a 16-byte GUID from the second key table at 0x25620 is found by the 0x1EDD4 search and the containing record's size field is in range, and 4 when a 0x20-byte record searched with 0x1EDD4 matches either of the GUIDs at 0x24298 and 0x24268. It then picks a message string by state (0x19BD, 0x19BE, 0x19BF, 0x19BC or 0x19C0), loads it into 0x29E50, loads the per-entry string id at 0x262F8 + index*2 into 0x29FE0, formats 0x29CC0 with the format at 0x26198 and hands the pair to 0x1E908 with the string id at 0x26268 + index*2. After the last entry it submits the whole state array to entry +0x58 of the 0x294A0 service as (0x260A8, 0x24288, 2, 6, 0x29358) and calls 0x3648.

name: dispatch_menu_command
comment: Returns 0x8000000000000003 unless global 0x29270 is non-NULL and its field at +8 is zero, stores its first argument in global 0x2A170, and returns 0 unless the service in global 0x29350 is present. The fourth argument, a 16-bit command word, selects an index: 0x29FE gives 5, 0x29FF 4, 0x2A00 3, 0x2A01 0, 0x2A02 1 and 0x2A03 2, and anything else returns 0. It then zeroes a 0xC8-byte table of 0x28-byte slots and writes one HII string id into the head of the slots named by four index variables (0x19C9, 0x19CA, 0x19CB, 0x19C8, 0x19C7), defaulting those indices from the state byte at 0x29358 + index and from the command word 0x29FE, and asks entry +0x68 of 0x29350 for a 16-bit answer with (context, 0, 0, table, index, &answer). The answer is compared against the four indices: a match on the first calls 0x8AD0, on the second 0x8D78 with flags 3, on the third 0x8D78 with flags 0x0A (skipped when the command word is 0x29FE), on the fourth 0x91E4, and on the default 0x9500 whose buffer is then freed; the answer is re-read after each call, and a value matching none of them returns 0.

name: dispatch_to_first_accepting_handler
comment: Calls the function pointers in the table at RVA 0x264B0 in order with (first argument, second argument, third argument), stopping at the first entry that returns a non-negative status; if the next table slot is NULL it returns the last (negative) status instead. The decompiled C names 0xBCC4 as the only callee, but this listing shows the callee is selected from the table at run time and 0xBCC4 is not provably the entry used.

name: test_protocol_and_check_byte
comment: Returns EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER if the third argument is NULL, then tests the second argument's handle for the protocol GUID at RVA 0x24348 with gBS OpenProtocol using attributes 4 (BY_TEST_PROTOCOL) and a NULL interface pointer, returning 0x8000000000000003 if the handle does not support it. On success it calls entry +0x30 of the interface passed as the third argument with (This, 0, 0x0B, 1, &byte, 4) and returns 0 only if that call succeeds and leaves 3 in the byte. The protocol and the meaning of the byte are not decoded here.

name: get_string_from_protocol_with_fallback
comment: Opens the protocol GUID at RVA 0x23560 on the first argument (a handle) with gBS OpenProtocol using attributes 2 (BY_GET_PROTOCOL) and calls its first entry with (This, GUID at 0x25C24, &string). If that fails it allocates strlen+1 bytes, copies the NUL-terminated ASCII string at interface offset 0x10, truncates it at the first semicolon (3B) or at the end of the string, and retries the same call. On success it measures the returned CHAR16 string, allocates length*2+2 bytes into the caller's second argument and formats it with the format at 0x25B68 through 0x1DFF0, returning 1. If the first protocol cannot be opened or neither call succeeds, it repeats the whole sequence with the protocol GUID at 0x238E0 and the sub-GUID at 0x26490; returns 0 when that also fails.

name: read_protocol_string_with_semicolon_fallback
comment: Opens the protocol GUID at RVA 0x23560 on the first argument with gBS OpenProtocol (attributes 2) and calls its entry at offset +8 with (This, second argument, third argument, GUID at 0x25C24, &string). On a negative status it copies the ASCII string at interface offset +0x10 into a fresh buffer, truncates it at the first semicolon or at its NUL, frees it after the retry, and gives up if the retry also fails. On success it counts the CHAR16 string, allocates count*2+2 bytes into the fourth argument and formats it with the format at 0x25B68 through 0x1DFF0, returning 1; otherwise it repeats the sequence with the protocol GUID at 0x238E0 and the sub-GUID at 0x26490, returning 0 when that fails too. The protocol is not identified in this listing.

name: collect_child_handles_matching_id
comment: Returns EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER if the first or second argument is NULL, after clearing both out-pointers. It enumerates all handles with gBS LocateHandleBuffer, allocates and zeroes one byte per handle, then for the second argument asks the boot-services entry at +0x130 for a sub-list and, for each of its entries, the entry at +0x128 for 0x18-byte records. A record is kept when its qword at +0 equals the first argument, its byte at +0x10 has bit 3 set, and its qword at +0x8 matches a handle in the all-handles array; each match sets the corresponding flag byte. It then counts the set flags, allocates count*8 bytes, stores the count in the caller's third argument and the matching handles in the caller's fourth, and returns 0. The two boot-services entries are identified here only by their offsets.

name: accumulate_handles_supporting_protocol
comment: Clears two out-pointers and calls 0xC464 with the caller's first two arguments plus those out-pointers; on a negative status it returns it, and otherwise, for each handle 0xC464 produced, tests the handle for the protocol GUID at RVA 0x234E0 with gBS OpenProtocol using attributes 4 and a NULL interface. A handle that fails the test is handed to a recursive call with the same first argument, a handle that passes has 0x1F0D4 called and, on a non-negative result, is appended to the global array at 0x29390 with the count at 0x29388. It returns 0 either way; on a NULL handle pointer it returns 0 immediately.

name: collect_handles_and_copy_out
comment: Clears its third and fourth arguments and calls 0xC67C with the caller's first two arguments (passed through in RCX and RDX). If the global count at 0x29388 is non-zero it copies that count to the third argument, allocates count*8 bytes, stores the pointer in the fourth, and fills it with the first qword of each slot in the global array at 0x29390. It returns the status from 0xC67C, which this function keeps in RSI across the copy, so the copy happens whether or not that status is negative.

name: connect_matching_handles_and_report_values
comment: Enumerates handles supporting the protocol GUID at RVA 0x236A0 (gBS LocateHandleBuffer, buffer type 2) and, for each, opens that protocol and calls its entry +0x70 with (This, &out at RBP+0x0F, &a, &b, &c); when the three outputs are 0, 0x17 and 0 it calls gBS ConnectController for that handle (boot-services entry +0x108) with (handle, 0, 0, 1). It then sets the byte at 0x293A0 to 1, allocates 0x100 and 0x40 byte buffers through 0x1B514, and enumerates handles supporting the protocol GUID at 0x234C0. For each such handle it opens the protocol at GUID 0x23690 and walks the result as a list of records terminated by a 0x7F byte, looking for the record with type 1 whose second byte is also 1 and whose byte at +4 is 0 and byte at +5 is 0x17; a match is followed by another HandleProtocol for 0x234C0, entry +0x28 of that interface, a 0x200-byte zeroed buffer filled by entry +0x18, a 0x2A-byte and then 0x28-byte rearrangement of it, and a printed report built from the record fields at +0x78, +0x9C, +0xA6, +0xC8, +0xD4, +0xEA, +0xEC and +0x98 with the message ids at tables 0x26AC0 and 0x26AD0 and two magic-constant remainder computations. All allocations are freed before returning.

name: write_setup_variable_and_report_status_fields
comment: Reads the DWORD at I/O address 0xE00FD010 and masks it with 0xFFFFF000 to form a base pointer, then calls gRT SetVariable (entry +0x48 of the table in global 0x29488) for the name at RVA 0x262C8, the GUID at 0x23710, attributes 0, size 0x7D8 and the 0x7D8-byte stack buffer at RSP+0x30 as data; in this listing that buffer is not filled before the call. It then writes 0 to base+0xB4 followed by 0x1000 and 4, reads the DWORD at base+0xB8, and decodes it into bit fields, printing one line per field with 0x680: bit 30 and bit 20 as yes/no, the 3-bit fields at 26:24, 20:18 and 17:15 and the 2-bit field at 9:8 each mapped to one of four strings, and the 4-bit fields at 7:4 and 3:0 each mapped to one of eight strings. One branch stores 0 or 1 into the byte at RSP+0x3CF, which lies inside the buffer already written to the variable. The register the base came from is not identified in this repository.

name: fill_slot_state_bytes_from_status
comment: Looks up the object registered under the GUID at RVA 0x23860 with 0x1F90C and returns if it or its field at +0x18 is NULL. It then walks 0x10 or 0x18 slots (depending on 0x1B6E0, which classifies the WORD at I/O address 0xE00F8002), setting one byte per slot in the caller's second argument at offset 0x0F: 1 when bit i is set in the DWORD at record+8, 4 when i equals the count at record+7, 3 when bit i is set in the DWORD at record+0xC, and otherwise 2 or 0 by comparing the low two bits of i against the bytes of the record at +1 grouped four to a byte (and, for the 3 case, the byte at +0x18). After the walk the tail is compacted with a 5-byte move and a count is printed with 0x680 using the string at 0x25C1C or, when the count is zero, 0x26A90.

name: print_status_register_diagnostics
comment: Reads the WORD at I/O address 0xE00F8002, and when its bits 5:11 masked value is 0x280 or 0x480 classifies it with 0x1B6E0 and prints one of the strings at 0x28120, 0x28130 or nothing, otherwise the same classification against 0x28140, 0x28150 or nothing. It then latches the byte at I/O 0xE00F8008 into the byte at RVA 0x24E00 if that byte is still 0xFF, formats it as two hex digits through 0x1C128 with the format at 0x284C4 (high nibble plus 0x41, low nibble plus 0x30) and prints it. Finally it re-reads the status word, compares it against the WORD array at 0x24A60 (terminated by 0xFFFF) and, on a match, takes the message pointer from 0x24A60 + index*16 + 8 and prints it. What the 0xE00F800x block is, this repository does not document.

name: read_msrs_into_cpu_setup
comment: Reads the CpuSetup variable (GUID 0x26AE0, varstore 0x235B0, size 0x2BB) and the SetupCpuFeatures variable (0x26AF8, varstore 0x23710, size 0x33) through [0x29488]+0x48. Only on the first pass, gated on byte 0x2AD87 being 0, does it RDMSR 0xCE and 0x1AD and, when a stack byte at RSP+0x61 is non-zero, also 0x1AE; each 64-bit result is split into bytes stored at 0x2AD88-0x2AD98 and 0x2AEFB-0x2AF0A, and CpuSetup is then written back through [0x29488]+0x58. The meaning of those three MSRs is not decoded further.

name: gather_indexed_msr_values_into_cpu_setup
comment: Reads CpuSetup and SetupCpuFeatures, then calls the local helper 0x1BD6C with (3, 0x80000018, out, &status); on success it loops over an index 0-3, extracts a 4-bit field from the returned dword at a per-index bit offset, and when the enable byte at 0x2ADC6+index is 1 and the extracted field is present calls 0x1BD6C four more times with 0x80000118, 0x80000518, 0x80000718 and (index<<8)|0x80000019, storing the results - the first two scaled by (x*100000+0x80000)>>20, the third by (x*1000+0x1000)>>13, the fourth masked with 0x7FFF - into the word arrays at 0x2ADCB, 0x2ADD5, 0x2AE1B, 0x2AE25 and 0x2AE2F. It writes CpuSetup back at the end. What the 0x80000000-prefixed constants select inside 0x1BD6C is not decoded further.

name: prompt_confirm_before_writing_setup_bytes
comment: A setup-variable callback: it returns 0 when the qword at [arg+8] is 0, and 0x8000000000000003 when that qword is neither 0 nor 1 or when the 16-bit value at [arg+0x10] is not 0x2725; otherwise it allocates 0x2BB and 0x10-byte buffers validated against GUID 0x26AE0 and 0x26FF8 on varstore 0x235B0 and returns 0x800000000000000E if either check fails. It formats the three strings at 0x27030, 0x27070 and 0x27130 into 0x190-byte buffers and calls 0x1F4FC(0x47, ...); a returned key other than 'Y'/'y' makes it copy the byte at 0x2ADA1 into buffer+0xE1 and write CpuSetup back, while 'Y' with byte 0xE1 equal to 1 calls 0x230D4 twice to fill the 0x10-byte buffer and clears 0xE1, and byte 0xE1 equal to 2 zeroes that buffer, sets byte 0xE2 to 1 and shows a second prompt (0x17). It then writes back the 0xE1 and 0xE2 fields and, if that was saved, the 0x10-byte variable under GUID 0x26FF8; what the three prompt strings and 0x230D4 read are not decoded further.

name: copy_setup_vars_to_paired_guids
comment: For each of five (GUID, varstore, size) triples - 0x262C8/0x23710/0x7D8, 0x26070/0x238F0/0x21D, 0x26320/0x238B0/0x2E, 0x26AE0/0x235B0/0x2BB and 0x26308/0x238C0/0x6EC - it reads the variable through [0x29488]+0x48 into a local buffer and immediately writes the same buffer back through [0x29488]+0x58 with attribute 2 under a second, different GUID: 0x27490, 0x274A8, 0x274C0, 0x274D8 and 0x274F8 respectively. That the two GUIDs of each pair differ is visible in the listing; the purpose of the second write is not decoded further, and Ghidra's string recovery happens to give the second set of GUIDs a ColdReset suffix.

name: compare_two_me_vars_and_flag_difference
comment: Reads the 0x2E-byte variables at GUIDs 0x274C0 and 0x26320 from varstore 0x238B0, ignoring the first read's status and returning if the second fails. If byte offset 0x2D of the two buffers differ it sets the module flag byte at 0x29468 and calls 0x20524 with (0x20000000, 0) when the second buffer's byte is 1, or (0, 0x20000000) otherwise. 0x20524 locates the protocol whose GUID is 0x234B0 and calls offset 0x40 of it; what that call does is not decoded further.

name: dup_nul_separated_string_block
comment: When the count byte is 0 it allocates 1 byte through 0x1B544 and stores the pointer in the out argument. Otherwise it walks the NUL-separated strings at the first argument count-1 times, measuring the total length including the terminating NUL, allocates that many bytes with 0x1B514, and copies the block with 0x2E0 - but only when the allocation succeeded, the length is non-zero, and the new pointer differs from the source. Always returns 0.

name: enumerate_protocol_records_into_form_fields
comment: Calls [0x29478]+0x70, locates a protocol by GUID 0x236E0 through [0x29478]+0x140, and loops calling offset 0x18 of that interface with a 0xFFFE handle until the call fails. Records whose first byte is 2 yield two strings duplicated by 0x127DC from record+record[1] with counts record[5] and record[6]; the first is set as form field 0x14D8 and is additionally passed to 0x21180 and compared unit by unit against up to 24 wide strings reached from 0x254A8, on a match rewriting the field with format 0x27520 and a word from 0x254A0, the second is set as field 0x14DB. Records whose first byte is 0 set field 0x1378 from bytes 0x16 and 0x17 and field 0x137B from one of three strings chosen by 0x1B738's table entry 0x8C. Once both a type-2 and a type-0 record have been seen the loop ends and field 0x1378 is rewritten from table entries 0x46 and 0xAD.

name: refresh_me_info_form_and_register_callback
comment: When the second argument is 1 it caches the incoming form handle at 0x293C0, reads the 0x12-byte variable at GUID 0x27598 from varstore 0x23930 and sets field 0x137F with four of its dwords, then calls 0x12864 and 0x12D20. It sets field 0x12F5 to one of the three strings at 0x27568, 0x27578 or 0x27588 according to the byte at 0x2AFE4 (3, 4, anything else), locates a protocol by GUID 0x234B0 and, if 0x206A0 succeeds on it, sets field 0x1382 from four words of the result; it sets field 0x136C to 0x26840 or 0x275B0 depending on whether dword [result+0xA0] & 0x110000 equals 0x110000, and field 0x136F to 0x275C0 or 0x275D0 on the sign of the dword at MMIO 0xFED30200. It ends by registering 0x1335C through 0x1F1EC(0x23520, 8, ...) and calling 0x12508; that registration and the 0x12508 call happen whether or not the second argument was 1.

name: read_mmio_status_word_into_form_0x14de
comment: Reads the 16-bit word at MMIO 0xE00FE000 and returns unless it is not 0xFFFF; reads the word at 0xE00FE0CC and returns unless bits 1:0 are 0; takes the dword at 0xE00FE010 masked with 0xFFFE0000, and saves the byte at 0xE00FE004, writing 7 there first if bit 1 of it was clear. If the masked value is non-zero it calls 0x22898 with it and a 16-bit out-pointer, and a non-zero result is matched against the low byte of seven 16-byte-stride entries at 0x24700, after which form field 0x14DE is set either with the matched entry's pointer (format 0x275E0) or with the bare byte (format 0x275F0). The saved byte at 0xE00FE004 is restored on the way out. What the 0xE00FExxx registers or the entries at 0x24700 denote is not decoded further.

name: notify_reset_type_once
comment: Guarded by a one-shot byte at 0x2974E: it returns immediately if that byte is already 1, otherwise sets it and calls 0x12E54 with the incoming argument. If the verdict equals the argument it returns; otherwise it calls the service at [0x29488]+0x68 with (verdict, 0, 0, NULL), or, when the verdict is 3, first copies the 16 bytes at 0x23850 into a stack buffer, formats the string at 0x27620 into a 10-byte buffer with 0x1CFF0, and calls the same service with (3, 0, 0x24, buffer). What the service at [0x29488]+0x68 does is not decoded further.

name: register_0x132e0_with_protocol_0x23520
comment: Locates the protocol whose GUID is at 0x23520 through [0x29478]+0x140 and, if that succeeds, calls offset 0x00 of the returned interface with 0x132E0 as the argument. If the first argument is non-zero it then calls [0x29478]+0x70 with it. Neither the located interface's first method nor the service at [0x29478]+0x70 is decoded further.

name: index_of_key_in_7byte_records
comment: Loads the 16-bit key at offset 0 of the argument, then steps through the array at 7-byte stride comparing each record's first word against the key, stopping when a zero word is found. Returns the record index, or 0xFFFF when the terminator is reached first.

name: strings_equal_case_insensitive
comment: Returns false if either argument is null, or if 0x1D7B4 reports different lengths for the two. On equal lengths it compares the two with 0x1EDD4 and returns true on a match; otherwise it falls back to 0x136B0 and returns true only when that returned 0.

name: find_list_node_by_string_and_copy_out
comment: Calls [0x29498]+0x98 with the first argument and GUID 0x23690 to obtain an object, then gets the head of a linked list by calling offset 0x58 of the third argument. Each node's qword at +0x10 is compared with that object by 0x1376C; on a match the out buffer is cleared with 0x2337E over 0x100 units, the wide string at node+0 is copied in and NUL-terminated, and 1 is returned. Returns 0 when the locate call fails, the list head is null, or no node matches.

name: find_list_node_by_nth_string
comment: Counts 16-bit units from the first argument's offset 6 until a zero word, then walks a linked list obtained by calling offset 0x58 of the third argument, comparing each node's qword at +0x10 against the string at (first argument + 8 + count*2) with 0x1376C. On a match it stores node+0 through the second argument and returns 1; it returns 0 for an empty list or no match.

name: lookup_name_for_boot_index
comment: Formats its first argument into a 16-unit wide buffer with the string at 0x27668 using 0x1DFF0, then calls 0x1D808 with that buffer as the variable name, varstore 0x24838, a NULL default and two out-pointers, returning the first out-pointer's value when 0x1D808's status is non-negative and 0 otherwise. The contents of the 0x24838 varstore are not decoded further.

name: set_legacy_field_from_offset_array
comment: Reads the 8-byte variable whose GUID is 0x27690 from varstore 0x24858 through [0x294A0]+0x48 to obtain a form handle, then reads the byte array whose GUID is 0x276B0 with 0x1D808 and returns that call's status on failure. On success it calls 0x680 with the handle, the field id byte[first_argument + array], the format string at 0x25B68 and the third argument as the value, then frees the array. The origin of the handle and the contents of the two variables are not decoded further.

name: set_uefi_field_from_offset_array
comment: Identical to 0x140B8 except that the byte array it reads with 0x1D808 is the one whose GUID is 0x276E0 rather than 0x276B0; the handle still comes from the 8-byte variable at GUID 0x27690 on varstore 0x24858, the field id from byte[first_argument + array], and the value is formatted with the string at 0x25B68.

name: patch_dev_order_from_fbo_legacy
comment: Returns immediately if the pointer at 0x293F8 is null. It reads the byte array whose GUID is 0x27710 on varstore 0x24858 with 0x1D808, then walks the first argument's record array: it takes the byte at each record's offset 6 masked to 0xFF, and if the corresponding record in the second array has a non-zero 16-bit count field at offset 4 it searches that record's 16-bit entries from offset 6 for a matching low byte and, on a match, copies the source record's first 4 bytes over the first array's record. Both record arrays advance by 4 plus their own 16-bit length field. The byte array is freed on the way out; the record layout is visible but what the records denote is not decoded further.

name: set_legacy_devorder_hii_string
comment: Finds the HII string field for one device in the 10-byte-entry table at 0x293E8 (matched on the first parameter, the table terminated by a zero first word), then loads the legacy device-order package named 0x27738 or, when the byte at 0x293D8 is non-zero, 0x277E0 filtered through 0x14240, and walks its {u32 id, u16 size} records for one whose id equals the first parameter. It reads a 16-bit index at record+6+second_parameter*2, multiplies it by 0x45 into the 0x45-stride table at 0x293F8, takes (word[+0x1E] << 4) | word[+0x1C] as an index into a string area, scans the next 10 bytes for a colon and continues past it, formats what follows with the template at 0x2672C through 0x1DFF0, looks the field up through 0x137DC and stores the text with 0x13DC8. A second parameter of 0x12 or more stores a null string and returns; the package buffer is freed through the service at offset 0x48 of the interface at 0x29498.

name: build_legacy_boot_group_table
comment: Loads the legacy device-order HII package (0x27710, or 0x277E0 filtered through 0x14240 according to the byte at 0x293D8) and the fixed-data package 0x27768, then walks both record lists in step. Each record's low 16 bits are mapped to an index by 0x13670 and to a second index by 0x13638; a 0xFF id, a 0xFFFF from either map, or a zero word at 0x293E8[index*10+4] skips the record. For the survivors it fills an 18-byte slice per index of the table at 0x2B080, writing the running count or the sentinel 0x12 (when the record word's high byte is set, or when no normal entry was seen), stops once the two counters reach 0x12, and stores the count at 0x2B060[second index]. The decoded C and the listing disagree on the loop bound (the C reads (size-2)>>1 where the listing shifts by one), so the element count per record is stated from the listing.

name: build_uefi_boot_group_table
comment: The UEFI counterpart of 0x14F50: the order package is named 0x27838 when the byte at 0x293D8 is zero and 0x27810 otherwise, the fixed-data package is 0x277B8, records are indexed on a 4-byte field at +6, and the sentinel test is the top byte of that dword rather than the high half of a 16-bit word. The two output tables are 0x2B200 (18 bytes per index) and 0x2B1E0 (the per-index count), and 0x14A50 is called at the end of each record.

name: regenerate_fixed_legacy_devorder
comment: Reads the HII package named 0x27710 (GUID at 0x24858), requires a size above 6, allocates a buffer of exactly that size with 0x1D774 and copies each record whose first dword is not 0xFF into it, rewriting the size field as ((size-2)>>1 + 1)*2.
