Up to 0x12 sixteen-bit values per record are then filled from 0x13C34 (any failure there returns immediately), and the assembled buffer is written back to the package named 0x27768 through the service at offset 0x58 of the interface at 0x294A0 with the last two arguments 2 and the byte count. A null allocation returns 0x8000000000000009.

name: regenerate_fixed_uefi_devorder
comment: As 0x1568C but for the UEFI order package at 0x27838 written back to 0x277B8, with the size field rewritten as ((size-2)>>2 + 1)*2 and the per-record fill loop bounded by (size-2)>>2 with the same 0x12 cap. A leading 0xFF dword is not special-cased here: such a record is copied like any other.

name: set_devorder_hii_strings
comment: Takes a package name, a GUID pointer and a flag byte, loads the package with 0x1D808, and for every record with size above 2 whose 32-bit id matches an entry of the table at 0x293E8 stores one HII string through 0x13DC8. With the flag zero it indexes the 0x45-stride table at 0x293F8, builds a path-like string (skipping past a colon found within 10 bytes) and stores it, but only if the byte at 0x24776 is set and the word at record+6 has a clear high byte; with the flag non-zero it instead requires the byte at 0x24776 and a clear top byte of the dword at record+6, and stores whatever 0x13D6C returns. A null string is stored whenever the gate fails, and the package buffer is freed through the service at offset 0x48.

name: rebuild_devorder_hii_strings
comment: Sets the gate byte at 0x24776 to 1, then calls 0x15C60 twice: with flag 0 on the legacy package name chosen by the byte at 0x293D8 (0x27710 with the GUID at 0x24858, or 0x277E0 with the GUID at 0x24848), and with flag 1 on the UEFI name (0x27838 or 0x27810) with the GUID at 0x24858. The second call is a tail jump, so the first call's status is what the routine returns.

name: get_variable_with_retry
comment: Locates the interface for the GUID at 0x237C0 into 0x29410 if it is not already cached, then calls the service at offset 0x18 with (first argument, 0, &size). If the status is exactly 0x8000000000000005 it allocates the advertised size with 0x1D748 and repeats the call with the new buffer, freeing it and returning 0 if the retry fails; otherwise the buffer pointer is the return value. What the first argument denotes, and what the other services of that interface do, is not shown in this listing.

name: apply_semicolon_separated_strings
comment: Copies the semicolon-separated string in the fourth argument into a pool buffer of strlen+1, then walks it token by token, overwriting each separator with 0 and stepping past it. A token is skipped when it compares equal to the constant at 0x278E4 over the length the code counts from that address starting at 1. Each surviving token is passed to the services at offsets 0x8 and 0x10 of the interface at 0x29410, and the copy is freed through the service at offset 0x48; a null input returns 0x8000000000000002.

name: format_setup_and_package_flags
comment: Reads the 0x7D8-byte Setup variable (the GUID bytes EC87D643, 4BB5EBA4, 3E3FE5A1, A90DB236 inlined at [RSP+0x30], the name the decompiler gives as u_Setup at 0x262C8) with a 0x14-byte structure output, and when both bytes at [RBP+0x701] and [RBP+0x6FD] are zero calls 0x16734 three times, with the id pairs (0x1A0A or 0x1A0B, 0x1A17), (0x1A1C or 0x1A1D, 0x1A18) and (0x1A22 or 0x1A23, 0x1A19) selected by the bytes at [RBP+0x6F7], [RBP+0x6F8] and [RBP+0x6F9]. It then reads the 0x14-byte record of the package named 0x278F0 (GUID 0x23880) and, for each of bits 0 to 4 set in its first dword, appends one of ten UTF-16 constants at 0x27908 to 0x27988 into a 0x80-byte buffer, choosing the second of each pair when a previous constant was already appended (tracked in DIL), and hands the buffer to 0x00680 with the id 0x1A47; the same is repeated for the second dword with 0x1A44. It finishes by passing the high 16 bits of the dword at [RSP+0x4C] to 0x00680 with 0x1A57, writing the low four bytes of the dword at [RSP+0x50] one byte at a time (each masked to 0xFF and appended to a buffer) for 0x1A56, and freeing the string 0x16674 returned.

name: sync_setup_variable_stores
comment: A notification body: it returns 0x8000000000000003 unless the qword at request+8 is below 2, then reads PchSetup (0x6EC bytes, name 0x26308), CpuSetup (0x2BB, 0x26AE0), SaSetup (0x21D, 0x26070) and Setup (0x7D8, 0x262C8) into four stack buffers with 0x213F0. The 16-bit and 8-bit stores at [RBP+0x5E7] and [RBP+0x5E9] and the byte test at [RBP+0x610], which the decompiler's C shows as local_d01, local_cff and local_cd8, address stack locals of this frame that nothing later reads, so the value 0x27C0 compared at request+0x10 only gates dead stores. What does take effect is the pair of question paths built with 0x1B458 from the offsets 0xDD and 0xDE and from 0x6B7, 0x6B8 and 0x6B9: each non-null path causes the corresponding CpuSetup or PchSetup buffer to be written back with 0x214E4 and the path freed.

name: copy_lang_string_from_protocol
comment: Locates the protocol for the GUID at 0x24920 through the service at offset 0x140 of the interface at 0x29498 and calls its service at offset 0x40 with (first argument, 1, &buffer, &size). If the second argument is non-zero it advances past up to that many NUL-terminated entries starting at buffer+1+buffer[1], stopping early when the current byte is already zero, then measures the remaining string, allocates length*2+2 from the pool through the service at offset 0x40, and copies it with 0x1E3B4 using the format at 0x27990. Any failure returns 0.

name: update_cpusetup_from_msr_ce
comment: Reads MSR 0xCE into RAX (EDX shifted left 32 and ORed in), takes bits 31:24 into R8B and bits 15:8 into AL, then dispatches on the 16-bit request id at [RDI+0x10]. For 0x2796 it raises the byte at buffer+0x1B9 to R8B when that byte is non-zero and smaller and also copies it to buffer+0xD1; for 0x2797, 0x2798 and 0x2799 the same raise applies to buffer+0x1C4 (against AL), buffer+0x20A and buffer+0x20C (against R8B). The touched offsets are turned into question paths by 0x1B458 (0x1B9 then 0xD1, or the single offset) and the 0x2BB-byte CpuSetup buffer, read with 0x213F0 from the name at 0x26AE0, is written back with 0x214E4; the buffer is freed through the service at offset 0x48 of the interface at 0x29478 either way.

name: set_sasetup_question_value
comment: Requires the cached request pointer at 0x29270 to be non-null with [ptr+8] at least 2 and exactly 0x1000, else returns 0x8000000000000003 (or 0 for a size that is at least 2 but not 0x1000). It reads the 0x21D-byte SaSetup variable (name 0x26070, GUID 0x238F0) through the service at offset 0x48 of the interface at 0x29488, then switches on the 16-bit id at [ptr+0x10] and stores one 16-bit value into *(UINT16 *)[ptr+0x18], taken from a byte or a word of the returned buffer: 0x27A0 gives buffer+0x3B, 0x279B buffer+0x34, 0x279C buffer+0x3A, 0x279D buffer+0x36, 0x279E buffer+0x35, 0x279F buffer+0x38, 0x27A1 buffer+0x3D, 0x27A2 buffer+0x3F, 0x27A5 buffer+0x44, 0x27A6 buffer+0x42 and 0x27A9 buffer+0x47, the byte-sourced ones zero-extended. Any other id returns 0 without writing.

name: read_device_entry_field
comment: Returns 0 unless the table pointer at 0x29448 is non-null, then indexes it at argument*0x40, loads the descriptor pointer at +0 and the payload pointer at descriptor+0x38, and switches on the dword at descriptor+0x40. A value of 1 yields payload+0x390; a value of 2 yields payload+0x60 when the payload's first dword equals 0x54535224 (bytes 24 52 53 54) and payload+0x148 otherwise; any other value leaves the result 0. The pointer arithmetic is unchecked, so an index past 0x7FF would run off the table.

name: cache_device_table_and_count
comment: Locates the interface for the GUID at 0x249B8 into a stack slot through the service at offset 0x140 of the interface at 0x29498, then caches the qword at interface+0x50 in the global at 0x29448 and the 16-bit value at *(interface+0x48) in the global at 0x29438. A failed locate returns 0 and leaves both globals untouched.

name: join_two_strings_in_fixed_buffer
comment: Allocates 0x42 pool bytes through the service at offset 0x40 of the interface at 0x29498, zeroes them through the service at offset 0x168, copies the first string left-aligned from offset 0 and the second from offset 0x21, each loop stopping after copying the terminating NUL or after 0x21 bytes, and returns the buffer. A failed allocation returns 0.

name: resolve_token_list_to_id
comment: Ensures the interface at 0x29450 is located for the GUID at 0x237C0, then fetches a string list into the global at 0x29418 through the service at offset 0x18, allocating a buffer of the advertised size and retrying on 0x8000000000000005. It walks the list splitting on semicolons: each token pointer (R9) is passed with the first and second arguments to the service at offset 0x00 when the 16-bit result is still zero, or to the service at offset 0x10 when it is not, the separator is restored to ';' and the walk continues; the same pair of calls runs once more on the final unterminated token. The 16-bit result is returned, or 0 on any error.

name: build_string_question_block
comment: Zeroes a 0x11-byte buffer through the service at offset 0x168 of the interface at 0x29498, then fills it as: bytes 0 and 1 hold 0x08 and 0x11, the word at +2 is the fifth argument, +4 the sixth, +6 the second argument, +8 is 0xDDDF, the byte at +0x0A is the fourth argument, the byte at +0x0C is 0x14 and the dword at +0x0D is 0x00200000. The 17 bytes are appended to the package named by the first argument with 0x21748, which writes the length and flag bytes into the first two positions of the block before copying it.

name: build_4byte_question_block
comment: Allocates four pool bytes with 0x1B544, writes the dword 0x0246820A into them, appends them to the package named by the first argument with 0x217A4, frees the temporary through the service at offset 0x48 of the interface at 0x29478, and returns whatever 0x217A4 returned. A null allocation returns 0.

name: build_device_list_form
comment: Obtains two 0x200-byte buffers with 0x21668, clears the byte at +0x12 in both and writes the form ids 0x29E1 and 0x29E2 at +0x13, then adds question 0x1A5C through 0x218E4. For each 0x40-byte entry of the table at 0x29448, up to the count in the word at 0x29438 and capped at 0x800, it takes the 16-bit language id at entry+0x12, used directly when the value at entry+8 equals 0x29440 and otherwise resolved through 0x18B3C and 0x18C7C (whose temporary is freed through the service at offset 0x48 of the interface at 0x29478), and appends a 15-byte question (word +2 = the id, word +4 = 0x1A5D, word +6 = 0x29BF + index, byte +0x0C = 4, word +0x0D = 0x29E7) with 0x21748. The two buffers are then joined by 0x21D24 against the constant 0x271A and freed with 0x216BC.

name: init_storage_device_forms
comment: Calls the service at offset 0x58 of the interface at 0x294A0 with (0x27F38, the GUID bytes 2798F49D, 480BF760, 69915580, 4077C240, 2, 0x4A, buffer) and then 0x18978, storing the returned 16-bit count in the global at 0x29438. If that count is non-zero it runs 0x18F24 and 0x19368, and if the global at 0x29420 is still zero it calls the service at offset 0x170 of the interface at 0x29498 with (0x200, 8, 0x19518, 0, 0x249A0, &0x29420), which registers the neighbouring routine as an event handler. 0x27F38 is the symbol the decompiler names u_TcgStorageDynamicSetupVar; what the 0x4A-byte record read from it contains is not decoded here.

name: narrow_wide_string_into_0x21_byte_buffer
comment: Takes the low byte of each of up to 0x21 consecutive 16-bit characters at RCX into a stack buffer, stopping early at the first zero word. It then calls the vtable entry +0x10 of the object in RDX with (object, 1, buffer) and returns 0x800000000000000F if the result is negative; otherwise it copies 0x21 bytes from the buffer to RDX+0x17 through the function at +0x160 of the pointer cached at 0x29498, writes 0x100 to the word at RDX+0x14, and returns 0. Which of the module's cached service tables 0x29478 and 0x29498 is which is not determined here.

name: fill_status_bytes_from_indexed_vtable
comment: Indexes a 0x40-byte-stride table at 0x29448 by the second argument, takes the first qword of the result as a vtable and calls vtable entry 0 to fetch a 16-bit value whose bits 0, 1, 2 and 3 are stored separately at RDI+1, RDI+2, RDI+3 and RDI+4. Vtable entry +0x30 then yields a dword: bit 4 makes RDI+5 become 2, otherwise bit 17 of it does, and bit 16 goes to RDI+6. It looks up a 16-byte GUID built from the immediates 0x38DC1092/0x4336FF7A/0xB5BF73A2/0x5F8A3619 once through +0x140 of the pointer at 0x29498, caching success in the byte at 0x29458 and setting RDI+7 to 1 when the lookup has never succeeded. It finishes with six calls to 0x18C7C, each passing the pointer at 0x29440, one of the 16-bit words at 0x2B020/0x2B030/0x2B032/0x2B034/0x2B038/0x2B03A, and a string chosen between 0x27F10 and 0x27F70 by whether the corresponding output byte is non-zero - except the fifth, which picks between 0x27F18, 0x27F78 and 0x27F90 from the three-way value at RDI+5. The contents of those string addresses are not in this listing.

name: format_then_append_wide_string
comment: Formats into a stack buffer by calling 0x1C0F8 with the format string at 0x280F8, the size 0x3C, and the caller's second and third arguments, then walks the 16-bit string at RCX counting characters up to its zero terminator. It computes the allocation size as 2 + 2*(the stack pointer saved on entry + that count) - the string's own address never enters the arithmetic, so the size does not depend on where the string lives - allocates that many bytes with 0x1B544, copies the wide string in with 0x1D16C, frees the source pointer through +0x48 of the table at 0x29478 when there was one, and appends half that many wide characters from the formatted buffer with a second 0x1D16C. Returns the new buffer, or NULL if the allocation failed. The contents of the format string at 0x280F8 are not in this listing.

name: allocate_buffer_return_pointer
comment: Calls the entry at +0x40 of the table pointer cached at 0x29478 with (4, the size left in EDX, &stack_out) and returns the pointer that call stores there, or 0 when the returned status is negative. The three-argument (type, size, out-pointer) shape and the constant 4 are those of a pool allocation, but which service sits at +0x40 of this module's table is not determined here.

name: allocate_zeroed_buffer
comment: Calls 0x1B514 for the size in RCX and, when both the returned pointer and the size are non-zero, zeroes that many bytes with the memset at 0x340. The pointer is what the function leaves in RAX - 0x1B514's pointer when either test fails, otherwise 0x340's, which returns its destination - and the two callers in this module take it from there.

name: allocate_and_copy_buffer
comment: Allocates the second argument's byte count with 0x1B514 and, when the allocation succeeded, the count is non-zero and the new pointer differs from the third argument, copies that many bytes from the third argument into the new buffer with the memmove at 0x2E0. RAX is left as the allocator's pointer, or as 0x2E0's return (the new buffer) after a successful copy, and is never explicitly stored anywhere.

name: allocate_zeroed_copy_and_free_source
comment: Allocates the third argument's byte count with 0x1B514, zeroes the buffer with 0x340 when that count is non-zero, and then copies min(second argument, third argument) bytes from the fourth argument into it with the memmove at 0x2E0, skipping the copy when the new buffer and the source are the same pointer. It finally frees the fourth argument through +0x48 of the table at 0x29478 and returns the new buffer, or the allocator's zero when any of the intervening tests fail.

name: copy_from_window_at_0xe0000000
comment: Copies RDX bytes from the address 0xE0000000 + RCX to R8, peeling off one byte and then one word first if bit 0 and bit 1 of CL respectively are set, then running a loop of RDX>>2 dword copies that reduces RDX by 4 per pass, and finishing with a trailing word and a trailing byte. Returns the original length argument (saved in R10) in RAX. What lives at 0xE0000000 is not decoded in this repository.

name: cache_code_from_status_word
comment: Returns immediately if the byte at 0x24E01 is already 0xFF. Otherwise it reads the 16-bit word at 0xE00F8002, masks it with 0xFFE0, stores 2 into 0x24E01 when the result is 0x280 or 0x9D80, 1 when it is 0x680 or 0xA300, and 0xFF for any other value. What the word at 0xE00F8002 means is not documented in this repository, so the three codes are not identified here.

name: locate_cached_protocol
comment: Returns the qword cached at 0x29490, and when that is NULL calls the entry at +0x140 of the table at 0x29478 once with (0x23590, 0, &0x29490) before returning it again. The three-argument shape is that of a protocol lookup, but the offset does not line up with one standard UEFI boot-services layout, so which service this is is not determined here; the GUID bytes at 0x23590 are not in this listing either.

name: wait_for_port_bit1_then_write
comment: Chooses I/O port 0x64 when CL equals 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise, reads that port with IN, and while bit 1 of the result is set calls the microsecond delay 0x1F9B8 with 15 and re-reads, counting each pass and giving up with 0x8000000000000007 once the count reaches 0x20000. When the bit is clear it writes the value in DL to that same port with OUT and returns 0. The only evidence for what these ports belong to in this repository is the numeric constants themselves.

name: drain_status_bit0_to_port_0x80
comment: Chooses status port 0x64 when CL equals 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise, and while bit 0 of that port is set reads a byte from port 0x60 (when CL is 0x60) or 0x62, writes it to port 0x80, waits 5000 microseconds with 0x1F9B8, and counts the iteration, returning 0x8000000000000007 once the count reaches 0x20000. Returns 0 when bit 0 was clear on entry or cleared within the limit; no other status is examined.

name: wait_for_port_bit1_clear
comment: Picks I/O port 0x64 when CL equals 0x60 and 0x66 otherwise, reads it with IN and, while bit 1 is set, calls the 15-microsecond delay 0x1F9B8 and re-reads, incrementing a counter each pass and returning 0x8000000000000007 once it reaches 0x20000. Returns 0 once the bit is clear. Unlike 0x1B774 it performs no OUT.

name: read_byte_from_port_0x62
comment: Calls 0x1B8D8 twice against status port 0x62 - first with value 0xA3 and data 4, then with value 0xA2 and the caller's DL - and then calls 0x1B774 with the same port and value 0xA4, returning immediately on any negative result. It then polls port 0x66 for bit 0, delaying 15 microseconds per pass through 0x1F9B8 and giving up with 0x8000000000000007 at 0x20000 iterations, and finally reads a byte from port 0x62 into the byte the third argument points at and returns 0.

name: read_byte_from_port_0x62_mode_7
comment: The same sequence as 0x1B9A0 - two 0x1B8D8 calls on status port 0x62 with values 0xA3 and 0xA2, a 0x1B774 with value 0xA4, a bit-0 poll of port 0x66 with 0x1F9B8(15) and a 0x20000 limit, then an IN from port 0x62 - except that the first 0x1B8D8 call passes data 7 rather than 4 and the destination byte pointer is the fourth argument (R9) rather than the third.

name: read_cpuid1_eax_low_nibble
comment: Makes the same CPUID leaf-1 call as 0x1BB38 - 0x3D0 with the argument 1 and four stack out-pointers - but returns the first output dword masked with 0xF, i.e. only its low four bits.

name: classify_cpuid_signature_with_word_at_e0000002
comment: Computes the same 0x0FFF0FF0-masked CPUID leaf-1 EAX as 0x1BB38, reads the 16-bit word at the fixed address 0xE0000002 into ECX, and dispatches on the masked value through a chain of subtractions, range compares and one bit test against 0x100010001, setting a result byte that starts at 4 and is set to 0, 1, 2 or 3 on the various branches. Immediates along the way include 0x806E0, 0x10000, 0xFF70, 0x10, 0x9B51, 0x3EC2, 0x3E0F, 0x3E34, 0x3ECC, 0x3ED0 and 0x5904; anything not matched falls through to 4. Neither the CPUID signature nor the word at 0xE0000002 is identified in this repository, so the four result values are not named.

name: gate_on_cpuid_signature_0xa0650
comment: Calls 0x1BB6C and then 0x1BB38, and returns 1 only when the masked CPUID leaf-1 EAX is exactly 0xA0650 and the low nibble is 1, 4 or 5. Returns 0 in every other case, with no other effect on memory or registers beyond what the two callees leave.

name: forward_to_1c184_with_flags_0x140
comment: Stores the fifth argument in a home slot, halves the second argument, sets the third to 0x140, passes the fourth through in R9 and the address of the home slot as the fifth, and calls 0x1C184 with those. Returns 0x1C184's result in RAX unchanged.

name: forward_to_1c184_with_flags_0
comment: Marshals its arguments the same way as 0x1C0F8 - fourth argument saved to a home slot whose address is passed as the fifth - but leaves the second argument undivided and sets the third to 0 rather than 0x140. Calls 0x1C184 and returns its result in RAX unchanged.

name: fill_buffer_with_element_stride
comment: For R8 iterations, provided the destination pointer is still below RDX, writes the low byte of R9 to [RCX] and - when the qword at [RSP+0x28] is not 1 - the next byte from R9>>8 as well, then advances RCX by that same qword. Returns the advanced destination pointer, or the destination unchanged if R8 is not positive or the destination has already reached RDX.

name: forward_to_1c184_with_own_home_slot
comment: Stores the fourth argument at R11+0x20, zeroes the qword at R11-0x10, and passes the address R11+0x28 as the fifth argument while the second, third and fourth go through to 0x1C184 unchanged. Unlike 0x1C0F8 and 0x1C128 it sets no third-argument value of its own, so whatever flags the caller passed reach 0x1C184 as they are. Returns 0x1C184's result in RAX.

name: hex_char_to_value
comment: Converts one 16-bit character to its numeric value: 0x30-0x39 becomes 0-9 by the subtract of 0x30, and 0x61-0x7A is first folded by subtracting 0x20 and then reduced by 0x37 to 10-35. The range tests are unsigned 16-bit comparisons, so any other character falls through to the final subtract of 0x37 and yields a negative value sign-extended into RAX; nothing is validated. It touches no memory, and its only callers in this module are the two calls in the hex decoder at 0x0001D374.

name: strncmp_bytes
comment: Byte-wise strncmp with the count in R8. A zero count returns 0 immediately; otherwise it loads a byte from the string in RCX and, while that byte is non-zero, the byte at RDX is also non-zero and equal, and the count is above one, advances both pointers and decrements the count. It returns the sign-extended difference *RCX - *RDX, so the first differing pair of bytes decides the sign.

name: wcsnlen
comment: Bounded length of a 16-bit string. Returns 0 if either pointer is NULL or the first 16-bit unit is already zero; otherwise it compares word ptr [RCX + index*2] against zero and stops at the first zero unit, returning that index, or returns the RDX limit itself when the limit is reached first. The limit is used as a plain 64-bit count with no upper bound check of its own.

name: wcsncpy_wide
comment: Copies a 16-bit string with the count in RDX measured in units. A NULL destination or source, or a count above 0xF4240, gives 0x8000000000000002; a source at least as long as the count gives 0x8000000000000005; and a source that overlaps the destination range gives 0x800000000000000F. Otherwise it copies 16-bit units from the source until a zero unit, writes a 16-bit zero at the end and returns 0.

name: wcsncpy_sized
comment: Copies a 16-bit string with both a destination capacity in RDX and a count in R9, both in units, and clamps the work to the smaller of the two after taking the source length from 0x0001CFBC. A NULL pointer, a capacity or count above 0xF4240, or a zero capacity gives 0x8000000000000002; a capacity no larger than the clamped count gives 0x8000000000000005; an overlap gives 0x800000000000000F. On success it writes at most that many units plus a 16-bit terminator and returns 0.

name: wcsncat_bounded
comment: Appends the 16-bit string in R8 to the one in RCX, whose capacity RDX is in units. It takes the destination's current length from 0x0001CFBC; a NULL pointer, a capacity above 0xF4240 or a zero capacity gives 0x8000000000000002, a destination that already fills its capacity gives 0x8000000000000004, a source that does not fit in the remainder gives 0x8000000000000005, and an overlap gives 0x800000000000000F. The copy is a 16-bit unit loop from the source's start that stops at the source's zero unit, which is also written at the end.

name: str_to_guid
comment: Parses a hyphenated 16-bit string held in the module global at 0x000292B8 into a 16-byte value written through RDX. It requires a '-' at offsets 0x10, 0x1A, 0x24 and 0x2E, and decodes 8 hex units at +0x00, 4 at +0x12, 4 at +0x1C, 4 at +0x26 and 12 at +0x30 with 0x0001D374, then byte-swaps each 16- and 32-bit field with a rol by 8 before writing two qwords; the resulting field widths are 4-2-2-8. A NULL global or output pointer returns 0x8000000000000002 and any missing separator or failed decode returns 0x8000000000000003. The listing itself never names the parsed value as a GUID.

name: hex_wstr_to_bytes
comment: Converts a 16-bit hex string of RDX units into RDX/2 bytes at the R8 buffer. NULL pointers, a length above 0xF4240 and an odd length give 0x8000000000000002, a buffer smaller than length/2 gives 0x8000000000000005, and any unit outside 0x30-0x39, 0x41-0x46 and 0x61-0x66 gives 0x8000000000000003. Each pair becomes one byte by calling 0x0001CF58 on both units, shifting the first result left four and OR-ing it with the second; a zero length is accepted and writes nothing.

name: strlen_bounded
comment: Length of a NUL-terminated byte string with a cap. NULL or an empty string gives 0; otherwise it scans forward with the counter as the byte index while the counter is below 0xF4240 and returns the index of the terminating zero, or 0xF4241 if the cap is reached with no terminator encountered.

name: get_chain_end_offset
comment: Calls the chain validator at 0x0001D694 and returns 0 for a NULL pointer or a failed validation. It then walks forward from RCX by the 16-bit length field at offset 2 of each record until a record whose first two bytes are 0x7F and 0xFF, and returns that record's address plus its own length field minus the original start pointer; with the 4-byte terminator the validator requires, that is the total byte size of the chain. The walk has no bound of its own, so a chain without the 0x7F/0xFF terminator does not return.

name: concat_two_chains
comment: Concatenates two length-prefixed record chains. With a NULL first argument it substitutes the second, or the 4-byte record at 0x00028980 when that too is NULL, and copies the result with 0x0001B570. With two non-NULL arguments it validates both with 0x0001D694, takes each chain's end from 0x0001D478, asks 0x0001B514 for end1 + end2 - 4 bytes, copies each chain into the new buffer with 0x000002E0 and returns the new pointer; any failed validation, failed allocation or NULL chain end returns 0.

name: append_record_and_concat
comment: Takes the 16-bit length at offset 2 of the record in RDX, asks 0x0001B514 for length + 4 bytes using the first argument, copies the record in with 0x000002E0, and appends the 4 bytes at 0x00028980 unless the copy already ends there. It then concatenates the result onto the chain in RCX with 0x0001D4C8 and releases the temporary through the table pointer at 0x00029478 offset 0x48. With a NULL second argument it takes the single-chain path, copying that chain with 0x0001B570.

name: validate_record_chain
comment: Returns true only for a chain whose terminating record - the first one whose bytes 0 and 1 are 0x7F and 0xFF - has a 16-bit length field of exactly 4 at offset 2. Walking the chain it requires each record's length at offset 2 to be at least 4, to fit the running 64-bit total without exceeding 2^64-5, and, for a record whose first two bytes are both 0x04, a zero 16-bit word at offset length-2. A NULL pointer or any violation returns false.

name: alloc_buffer_via_table_0x40
comment: Zeroes a stack slot and calls the entry at offset 0x40 of the table pointer stored at 0x00029498 with (4, size, &slot), then returns the buffer pointer the call wrote into the slot. The table at 0x00029498 and the meaning of the constant 4 are not identified in this listing.

name: alloc_then_call_table_0x168
comment: Allocates a buffer of the requested size through 0x0001D748 and, if that returned non-NULL, calls the entry at offset 0x168 of the same table at 0x00029498 with (buffer, size, 0) before returning the buffer; a NULL allocation skips the second call. Neither table entry is identified in this listing, so what the 0x168 call does with the buffer is not decoded here.

name: chain_total_length
comment: Returns 0 for a NULL pointer. Otherwise it sums each record's length in a chain, reading the 16-bit big-endian value from bytes 2 and 3, adding it to the running total and using it to advance the cursor; it stops early, returning the partial sum, if a record's first byte is zero or its length field is zero, and on the 0x7F/0xFF terminator it returns the sum plus 4. Unlike 0x0001D478 and 0x0001D694 it does not validate the chain first.

name: utoa_radix
comment: Writes the value in RCX to the byte buffer RDX in the base given by R8D, least significant digit first at the cursor and left for the caller to reverse, adding 0x30 to remainders below 10 and 0x57 to the rest. A zero value writes a single '0'; otherwise it divides and repeats until the quotient is zero. The magnitude is -value when the base is 10, the unsigned 32-bit truncation when the fourth argument is zero, and the raw 64-bit value otherwise, and a '-' is appended after the digits for base 10 only. It returns the address of the terminating NUL.

name: utoa_into_wide_buffer
comment: Formats the value in RCX with 0x0001D920 into a 256-byte stack buffer using the base in R8D and the wide flag in R9D, then copies the resulting bytes backwards out of that buffer, sign-extending each byte into one 16-bit unit at the destination RDX. It writes a 16-bit zero at the end and returns the destination.

name: parse_signed_integer
comment: Parses a signed integer from the string in RCX, whose units are R9D bytes wide, writing the stopping position through the pointer in RDX. It skips spaces and tabs, accepts a leading '-' or '+', and accumulates digits: 0-9 directly, and letters folded with an AND of 0xDF before a subtract of 0x37, with any result of 10 or more ending the scan. On a non-digit or the end of the string it stores the current position and returns 0 for the end of the string, otherwise the sign times 0x7FFFFFFF or 0x80000000 depending on whether the 32-bit accumulator crossed 0x80000000.

name: sprintf
comment: Stores the caller's RDX, R8 and R9 into a 24-byte register save area on the stack, points the va_list at the first stack vararg, and tail-calls 0x0001DBE4 with (buffer, 0, format, va_list). The return value of the core formatter is passed straight back.

name: status_code_to_string
comment: Maps a 64-bit status value to a string address. Zero returns the literal at 0x00028998; a positive value with bit 0x2000000000000000 set and below 2 returns 0x00024E90 + value*0x23, and any other positive value up to 4 returns 0x00024E06 + value*0x1A. A negative value whose top bits are 0xA000000000000000 or 0xC000000000000000 is looked up as 0x00024EE0 + low*0x19 or 0x00024F27 + low*0x19 with low below 3, and any other negative value is looked up as 0x00024F67 + low*0x19 for low up to 0x1E; an out-of-range index returns NULL. None of the strings is read in this listing.

name: format_bytes_core
comment: Core byte formatter: it copies the format string at R8 to the buffer in RCX one byte at a time, and on a '%' handles '%%', an optional '0' flag, a '*' width read from the next 8-byte va_list slot, and otherwise a width parsed by 0x0001D9E4. The letter then selects s or a for a byte string, S for a 16-bit string truncated to low bytes, c for one byte, G or g for a recursive call to 0x0001DFD0 carrying the 16 bytes at the va_list cursor and the format at 0x000287B8, r for a recursive 0x0001DFD0 carrying either a name from 0x0001DB1C or the format at 0x000289A4 with the name at 0x00024F30, and d, i, u, X, x or p, which are converted by 0x0001D920 into a 32-byte stack buffer, upper-cased in place for X and p, then left-padded with the flag character to the width. It stops on a NUL format byte or when the output count reaches one, NUL-terminates and returns the byte count, or returns -1 for a NULL buffer or format.

name: vsprintf
comment: Stores R8 and R9 into the outgoing register save area, points the va_list at the first stack vararg, and tail-calls 0x0001DBE4 with the buffer, count, format and va_list passed through unchanged.

name: swprintf
comment: Stores the caller's RDX, R8 and R9 into a 24-byte register save area on the stack, points the va_list at the first stack vararg, and tail-calls 0x0001E018 with (buffer, 0, format, va_list).

name: format_wide_core
comment: Core 16-bit formatter, the wide counterpart of 0x0001DBE4: it copies 16-bit units from the format at R8 to the buffer in RCX, handling '%%', an optional '0' flag, a '*' width and a width parsed by 0x0001D9E4, and then the conversions s for a 16-bit string, S or a for a byte string widened one unit at a time, c for one unit, G or g for a recursive 0x0001E3B4 carrying the 16 bytes at the va_list cursor and the format at 0x000289B0 with the result upper-cased through 0x0001DAC4 for G, r for a recursive 0x0001E3B4 carrying either a name from 0x0001DB1C or the format at 0x00028A18, and d, i, u, X, x or p, which go through 0x0001D994 into a 32-unit stack buffer. Width padding is emitted with the flag character, the buffer is 16-bit NUL-terminated, and the return is the number of units written shifted right by one, or -1 for a NULL buffer or format.

name: vswprintf
comment: Stores R8 and R9 into the outgoing register save area, points the va_list at the first stack vararg, and tail-calls 0x0001E018 with the buffer, remaining count, format and va_list passed through unchanged.

name: get_cached_platform_lang
comment: Manages a cached string pointer at 0x000294C0. If the cache currently holds the string at 0x00025C24 it is first cleared to NULL, a local handle is zeroed, and 0x0001D808 is called with (0x00025C88, 0x000252C0, 0, &local_handle, &cache); on a non-negative result the cache becomes whatever that call wrote, otherwise it stays at the 0x00025C24 literal, which is written back to 0x000294C0 and returned. None of the strings at 0x00025C88, 0x000252C0 or 0x00025C24 is read in this listing; the decompile's name for the last is s_en_US.

name: copy_string_skipping_ampersand_runs
comment: Asks the entry at offset 0x40 of the table at 0x00029498 for a buffer with the constant 4, the second argument as the size and a local out-pointer, then walks the 16-bit string in RCX copying units into it. When a 0x26 ('&') unit is reached it calls 0x0001EDD4 with the following 12 bytes and the pointer at 0x00028A40; if that call returns 0 the units between that '&' and the next '&' are not copied, while both '&' units are. The buffer is 16-bit NUL-terminated, written back over the original string by 0x000233D0 with the byte count 2*units + 2, and released through offset 0x48 of the same table. What 0x0001EDD4 matches against 0x00028A40 is not decoded here.

name: find_matching_segment_in_name_list
comment: For each candidate string in the NULL-terminated list (the second argument and the following varargs), walks the semicolon-separated segments of the first argument comparing byte by byte, and treats a hyphen 0x2D in the candidate as a prefix-match boundary. On a match it allocates length+1 bytes with 0x1D748, copies the matching segment in with 0x233D0, NUL-terminates it and returns the copy. Returns NULL when nothing matches or either of the first two arguments is null.

name: read_protocol_buffer
comment: Locates a protocol (GUID at 0x252D0) via LocateProtocol at gBS+0x140 through DAT_00029498, then calls the located interface method at +0x18 first with a NULL buffer to obtain a size, expecting the status 0x8000000000000005 (EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL). It then allocates a buffer of that size with 0x1D748, calls the method again, and returns the buffer, or frees it with gBS+0x48 and returns NULL if the second call fails.

name: set_each_name_in_list
comment: Iterates the semicolon-separated tokens of the first argument, temporarily NUL-terminating each token at the semicolon and calling the located protocol method at +0x8 with it. It keeps calling the next token while the result equals 0x8000000000000020 and stops at the first different result, which it returns.

name: set_var_by_resolved_name
comment: Locates the protocol (GUID 0x252D0), fetches the variable-name buffer with 0x1E640, resolves the requested name against it with the segment matcher 0x1E520, and invokes the protocol method at +0x8 to set the value; if that returns 0x8000000000000020 it falls back to the per-name loop 0x1E700. The intermediate buffers are freed with gBS+0x48 and a NULL from the matcher yields 0x800000000000000E.

name: get_each_name_in_list
comment: Two-phase get of the name list through the located protocol method at +0x18 (expecting 0x8000000000000005 then allocating with 0x1D748), then splits the returned buffer on the semicolon character 0x3B and for each token calls the protocol method at +0x10, stopping on the first negative result. The buffer is freed with gBS+0x48.

name: append_wide_component_and_parse
comment: Locates two protocols (GUIDs 0x252F0 and 0x252E0), two-phase-sizes a scratch buffer from the first protocol method at +0x8, appends the wide string at 0x25B68 to it with the helper 0x1E3B4 (using the GUID at 0x25300), refetches the enlarged buffer through the same method, and then hands it to the second protocol method at +0x20. The two protocols and the string at 0x25B68 are not identified further in this listing.

name: resolve_wide_name_and_measure
comment: Repeats the two-protocol setup of 0x1EA50 (GUIDs 0x252F0 and 0x252E0), two-phase-sizing a buffer, appending the wide string at 0x25B68, refetching it, and fixing it up with 0x1E448. It then calls the second protocol method at +0x18 to resolve a name into a returned wide string, measures that string in bytes by walking 16-bit units to the terminator (+2 per unit), passes the measured length back through the first protocol method at +0x8, and frees the buffers with gBS+0x48.

name: memcmp_regions
comment: Compares two memory regions of the length in the third argument, using 8-byte word compares when the two pointers share the same low three address bits and byte compares otherwise. Returns 0 when the regions are equal, otherwise the sign-extended difference of the first differing bytes.

name: render_device_path_to_text
comment: Renders a device path as text: for each node it switches on the Type byte (1 to 4 and the 0x7F end) and the SubType byte, selecting a format string from a table (0x28B08 USB, 0x28B18 PCI, 0x28B20 Pccard Socket, 0x28B28 VenHw, 0x28B30 Acpi, 0x28B38 HD, 0x28B40 CDROM, 0x28B48 VenMedia, 0x28B58 ATA, 0x28B60 SCSI, 0x28B68 VenMsg, and a generic 0x25378) and appending it with the node fields via the helper 0x1DAF4, then advances to the next node by the header 16-bit Length field. On the end node (Type 0x7F, SubType 0xFF) it allocates and returns the assembled string, copying it out of a 512-byte stack buffer; if the append helper returns -1 it returns 0x8000000000000003.

name: grow_global_slot_buffer
comment: Maintains a growable array of 8-byte slots held in a slot count at 0x29380 and a buffer pointer at 0x29390, with 0x29388 tracking slots in use. When growth is needed it allocates max(0x50, count*8+0x50) bytes with 0x1D774, copies the used bytes with CopyMem at gBS+0x160, frees the old buffer with FreePool at gBS+0x48, and stores the new pointer and count; returns 0x8000000000000009 if the allocation fails, 0 otherwise.

name: lookup_form_entry_by_key
comment: Looks up a 16-byte key in the global table at 0x29470: an entry count at +0x68 and an array of 0x18-byte entries at +0x70, each with the key in its first two 8-byte fields and a value at +0x10. On a match it stores the entry value through the second argument and returns 0, or returns 0x800000000000000E when the count is zero or no entry matches.

name: call_service_with_handle
comment: Drives three calls on the service table at 0x29478: method +0x50 (passed 0x200 and an out-pointer) to obtain a handle, method +0xa8 with the first argument, that handle and the third argument to dispatch a callback through it, then method +0x68 to release the handle, which is returned. The identity of the table at 0x29478 is not resolved further in this listing.

name: read_protocol_object
comment: Two-phase get on the interface at 0x29488 method +0x48: first with a size out-pointer (expecting 0x8000000000000005), then allocating a buffer with 0x1B514 and calling the method again with it. On failure it frees the buffer through 0x29478+0x48 and zeroes the out-pointer; on success it stores the size through the fourth argument when non-null and returns the status.

name: find_matching_path_segment
comment: For each candidate name in the NULL-terminated list (the third argument and following), walks the semicolon-separated segments of the first string and, where a segment length fits within the candidate and the prefix-compare helper 0x1CF88 returns equal, allocates length+1 bytes with 0x1B544 and returns a copy of that segment. A hyphen 0x2D in the candidate makes the scan retry with progressively shorter candidate prefixes; returns NULL when nothing matches.

name: measure_ucs2_width
comment: Computes the display width in columns of a UCS-2 string, walking 16-bit units and counting 1 column each, except 0xFFF0 (counted as 1) and 0xFFF1 (counted as 2), stopping at the NUL terminator. When the flag argument is set and the running count exceeds the third argument it stores the unit index through the fourth argument and stops; returns the byte length (columns times 2), or 0 for a null string.

name: render_boxed_console_rows
comment: First tries to locate the protocol {0xf31fcbb5, 0x4215b53d, 0x3361db81, 0x6a98d4e4} via LocateProtocol and, on success, calls the located interface first method and returns. Otherwise it renders each UCS-2 string in the array pointed to by the third argument as a console row framed with box-drawing glyphs (0x250C and 0x2510 top, 0x2502 sides, 0x2514 and 0x2518 bottom, padded with 0x2500), sizing rows with the width measure 0x1F454 and writing them through the console interface at 0x29470+0x40 (method +0x38 sets the cursor, +0x8 writes the string), then frees the scratch buffer with gBS+0x48. If the second argument is non-null it repeatedly calls the interface at 0x29470+0x30 method +0x8, waiting on its event (WaitForEvent at gBS+0x60) while the call returns 0x8000000000000006 (EFI_NOT_READY).

name: get_cached_form_list
comment: Returns the module-global pointer at 0x294D0, calling the table lookup 0x1F18C with the 16-byte key at 0x23820 to populate it on the first call when it is still null. The result is the value field cached by 0x1F18C.

name: poll_timer_port_until_target
comment: Splits its argument into a 22-bit offset (low bits) and a repeat count (high bits shifted right by 22), then for each repeat reads a 24-bit counter from I/O port 0x1808, adds the offset to form a target, and polls the port (calling the short delay at 0x420 between reads) until bit 23 of (target minus current) is set, i.e. the counter has passed the target.

name: delay_scaled_ticks
comment: Multiplies its argument by 0x369E99, divides by 1,000,000 using a 128-bit magic multiply (constant 0x431BDE82D7B634DB, shift 18), and passes the quotient to the port-0x1808 timer wait 0x1F958; returns the original argument unchanged.

name: find_record_by_guid_key
comment: Searches the length-prefixed record array in the first argument (entry count at +0x1E, entries from +0x24, each with a 16-bit length and a 16-byte key at +8) for the entry whose key equals the 16 bytes at 0x236B0 and 0x236B8, storing the entry pointer through the third argument and returning 0, or returning 0x800000000000000E when absent.

name: sw_smi_cmd_203_read_dword
comment: Sends a software-SMI read: locates the communication protocol (GUID at 0x234B0), calls its +0x40 method and requires a zero result, builds a 64-bit command word 0x203 with the first argument in the high 32 bits plus a 13-byte parameter block, and invokes the protocol Communicate method (first vtable entry). On success it validates the response header (port field 0x200, bit 15 set, top byte zero) and returns the response data dword through the second argument, which must be non-null.

name: sw_smi_cmd_303_write
comment: Sends a 13-byte software-SMI write: after the +0x40 readiness check it builds a request with header 0x303, the first argument as the data dword, a 0x04 byte and the third argument, and calls the protocol Communicate method, returning its status. No response data is read back.

name: sw_smi_read_named_string
comment: Sends a software-SMI read of a named string: after the +0x40 readiness check it builds an opcode-0x0A request (header 0x020A) carrying the fixed string at 0x28B78 (labelled s__home_hotham_dbg_dam_req by the decompiler) and a caller-supplied length, calls Communicate, and on a valid response (port field 0x200, bit 15 set, byte 3 zero, length within bounds) copies the returned string out and updates the length, otherwise returning 0x8000000000000007. The scratch buffer is freed with gBS+0x48.

name: sw_smi_write_named_byte
comment: Sends a software-SMI write of a one-byte value to a named string: after the +0x40 readiness check it builds an opcode-0x0A request (header 0x030A) carrying the fixed string at 0x28B78 and the single byte from the fifth argument, calls Communicate, and returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_DEVICE_ERROR) unless the response byte 3 is zero. The scratch buffer is freed with gBS+0x48.

name: sw_smi_cmd_40a_write
comment: Calls the helper 0x20D34 for a word value and, if it equals 0xC, uses 7 rather than 9 as the Communicate argument. After the protocol +0x40 readiness check it sends a 4-byte command word 0x040A via Communicate and returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_DEVICE_ERROR) if the response top byte is set.

name: sw_smi_read_variable_buffer
comment: Sends a software-SMI read of a variable-length buffer: after the +0x40 readiness check it builds an opcode-0x0A request (header 0x0A0A) with a sub-command dword 0x10050000 and the caller-supplied length, calls Communicate, and on a valid response (port field 0xA00, bit 15 set, byte 3 zero, length within bounds) copies the payload out and updates the length, otherwise returning 0x8000000000000007. The scratch buffer is freed with gBS+0x48.

name: sw_smi_write_variable_byte
comment: Sends a software-SMI write of a one-byte value: after the +0x40 readiness check it builds an opcode-0x0A request (header 0x0B0A) with a sub-command dword 0x10050000 and the byte from the fifth argument, calls Communicate, and returns 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_DEVICE_ERROR) unless the response byte 3 is zero. The scratch buffer is freed with gBS+0x48.

name: sw_smi_cmd_1b0a_status
comment: Calls the helper 0x20D34 and uses 7 rather than 9 as the Communicate argument when its word output equals 0xC. After the +0x40 readiness check it zero-fills an 8-byte buffer, sets its header to 0x1B0A, calls Communicate, and validates the returned status word (port field 0x1B00, bit 15 set, top byte zero), returning 0x8000000000000007 (EFI_DEVICE_ERROR) on mismatch.

name: sw_smi_read_dword_array
comment: Reads a dword array over a software SMI: after the +0x40 readiness check it allocates a buffer of 8 plus count*4 bytes (count from the first argument), builds an opcode-0x0A request (header 0x1C0A) whose length field is 8 plus count*4, and calls Communicate. It handles 0x8000000000000005 (EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL) by returning the required count through the first argument; on a valid response (port field 0x1C00, bit 15 set, byte 3 zero) it copies count*4 bytes into the second argument and updates the count. The buffer is freed with gBS+0x48.

name: smi_send_14ff_with_two_dwords
comment: Resolves the interface whose GUID is at 0x000234B0 through the entry at offset 0x140 of the table at 0x00029478, calls its method at offset 0x40 with a status out-pointer and bails out with 0x8000000000000003 unless the status is non-negative and that word is 0. It then builds a 12-byte buffer holding the dword 0x14FF followed by the two dword arguments, sets the out-size to 8 and the last stack byte to 7, and calls the first qword of the interface with (0, buffer, 0xC, out-size, 0, 7). If that call succeeds and the first argument comes back equal to 1, the value returned is replaced with 0x800000000000000F.

name: smi_send_20ff_unless_flag_is_0c
comment: Calls 0x00020d34 for two 16-bit out-values and returns early if the first is 0xC. It resolves the interface whose GUID is at 0x000234B0 through offset 0x140 of the table at 0x00029478, calls its method at offset 0x40 with a status out-pointer, and bails with 0x8000000000000003 unless that succeeds and the word is 0. It then builds an 8-byte buffer of the dword 0x20FF plus the dword argument, sets the out-size to 4 and the last stack byte to 7, and calls the first qword of the interface with (0, buffer, 8, out-size, 0, 7). If that call succeeds, the dword at buffer offset 0 is tested against 0xFF000000 and the return value is replaced with 0x8000000000000007 when any of that mask is set.

name: read_pcmp_header_into_out_buffer
comment: Calls the method at offset 0x40 of the interface whose pointer is the second argument, and returns 0x8000000000000003 unless it succeeds and the status word it wrote is 0. It then calls the first qword of that same interface with (0, buffer, 8, out-size, 0, 7) where the 8-byte buffer holds the dword 0x1CFF and then the dword 0x50434D50, and the out-size is 0x60. The returned dword is accepted only if (dword & 0x7F00) == 0x1C00, bit 15 is set, bits 24-31 are clear, and the dword at buffer+4 still reads 0x50434D50; on that path 0x58 bytes are copied from the 0x60-byte stack buffer to the first argument, the first 4 bytes of which are overwritten with 0x50434D50. Which of the two this selects - header or payload - is not settled by the listing.

name: smi_send_50000_subcommand_11
comment: Returns 0x8000000000000003 unless 0x00020c20 returns 0, the interface whose GUID is at 0x000234B0 is found through offset 0x140 of the table at 0x00029478, its method at offset 0x40 succeeds with a zero status word, and its method at offset 0x38 succeeds leaving a byte whose low nibble is 0 (otherwise 0x800000000000000A). It then sends a 0x18-byte buffer holding the qword 0x50000, the qword 0x11, the qword 4, the byte argument and two zero bytes, with out-size 0x14 and the last stack byte 8, and replaces the result with 0x8000000000000007 if the dword four bytes into the out-size slot is non-zero.

name: smi_send_50000_subcommand_1a_echo
comment: Returns 0x8000000000000003 unless 0x00020c20 returns 0; returns 0x8000000000000002 if the buffer pointer argument is null. It resolves the interface whose GUID is at 0x000234B0 through offset 0x140 of the table at 0x00029478, calls its method at offset 0x40 with a status out-pointer (0x8000000000000003 on failure or a non-zero status) and its method at offset 0x38 (0x800000000000000A on failure or a non-zero low nibble). It then builds a 0x30-byte buffer of the dword 0x50000, the dword 0x1A, the byte argument's buffer offsets 0x14 and 0x15, the dword 0x1C and zero dwords, sends it with out-size 0x30 and the last stack byte 8, replaces the result with 0x8000000000000007 if a non-zero dword comes back, and copies the whole 0x30-byte buffer to the caller's pointer unless that pointer is the same buffer.

name: check_smm_software_smi_available
comment: Tries the entry at offset 0x140 of the table at 0x00029478 with the GUID at 0x00023950 and returns 1 immediately if that succeeds. Otherwise it resolves the interface whose GUID is at 0x000234B0 the same way, calls its method at offset 0x40 with a status out-pointer, and returns 0 unless that succeeds and the status word is 0. It then calls the first qword of that interface with (0, buffer, 4, out-size, 0, 7) where the buffer holds the dword 0x1DFF and the out-size is 8, taking the dword at out-size+4 as a condition; on any failure of the resolve or the method it returns 0. If that call succeeds and the dword is 0, it re-tries the 0x23950 lookup and, only if it comes back as 0x800000000000000E, calls the entry at offset 0x80 of the same table with (out-pointer, the same GUID, 0, 0). Returns 1 on that path. Several callers gate their whole body on the low byte of this return.

name: read_acpi_20_table_creator_words
comment: Calls 0x0001f90c with the address 0x00023530, which searches a table it caches itself for a 16-byte match. If that returns a null pointer the function returns 0x8000000000000003; otherwise it stores the 16-bit words at offset 0x1C and offset 0x1E of the returned structure through the two out-pointers and returns 0. Which table 0x00023530 identifies is not decoded here, so the two words are reported by offset only.

name: read_cmos_index_0x7d_value
comment: Samples RFLAGS through 0x000004a0, takes bit 9 (the interrupt-enable flag) of the result, and issues CLI through 0x00000450. It then sets bit 17 of the dword at absolute address 0xFDC431FC, reads the byte from I/O port 0x70, clears bit 17 of the same dword, and writes (that byte & 0x80) | 0x7D back to port 0x70. It reads the byte from I/O port 0x71, and if the sampled interrupt-enable flag was set issues STI through 0x00000440 before returning that byte. The device behind I/O ports 0x70 and 0x71 is not identified in this module, so no mechanism is assigned to them here.

name: write_cmos_index_0x7c_or_0x7e_value
comment: Samples RFLAGS through 0x000004a0, takes bit 9 (the interrupt-enable flag), and issues CLI through 0x00000450. If the first byte argument is below 0x80 it sets bit 17 of the dword at absolute address 0xFDC431FC, reads I/O port 0x70, clears that bit again, and keeps only bit 7 of the byte read; the port pair used is then (0x70, 0x71). Otherwise the pair is (0x72, 0x73) and no port is read. It writes (first argument & 0x7F) OR the retained bit 7 to the first port and the second byte argument to the second, then issues STI through 0x00000440 if the sampled interrupt-enable flag was set, and returns the second argument. The device behind I/O ports 0x70-0x73 is not identified in this module.

name: get_child_handle_of_type_23480
comment: Calls the entry at offset 0x98 of the table at 0x00029478 with the cached value in 0x00029480, the address 0x00023480, and an out-pointer. Returns 0 if that status is negative; otherwise loads the pointer the call wrote and returns the qword at its offset 0x18.

name: open_child_and_call_offset_18
comment: Returns 0x800000000000000E if the first argument is null. Otherwise it calls the entry at offset 0x98 of the table at 0x00029478 with that argument, the address 0x000236C0 and an out-pointer, returning 0x800000000000000E on a negative status. It takes the two qwords the call wrote from the out area, zeroes both, and calls the method at offset 0x18 of the first qword (the interface) with (interface, second argument, 0x19, 0, both zeroed qwords, a byte from the third argument, and the second zeroed qword again), returning that method's status unchanged.

name: walk_semicolon_list_adding_each_token
comment: Calls 0x00021f60 on its first argument and returns 0 if that yields a null pointer. Otherwise it walks the returned ASCII string splitting at every ';' byte - it replaces the ';' with a NUL and advances - and for each token calls 0x0001cf88 against the NUL-terminated data at 0x000278E4 over a length it measures from 0x000278E5. On a zero compare it calls either the first or the second qword of the interface cached in 0x000294E8 - the second when the 16-bit second argument is non-zero, the first otherwise - passing the first argument and, on the first path, a pointer to that 16-bit value, and breaks the loop on a negative return. The string is passed to the entry at offset 0x48 of the table at 0x00029478 at the end, and the 16-bit argument is the return value if the last status was non-negative.

name: get_string_for_langcopy_retried_on_buffer_too_small
comment: Calls 0x00021f60 on the global at 0x000293C0 and returns 0 if that yields a null pointer. It then calls 0x0001f24c with the 16 bytes at 0x00025C88 and the address 0x000234A0 to get a language string, uses that string in preference to the one at 0x00028B91 when it is non-null, and passes both to 0x0001f320 with a null second argument; a null result returns 0. It calls the method at offset 8 of the interface cached in 0x000294E8 with the resulting string, the global at 0x000293C0, the value 0x14D8, a pointer to the 16-bit second argument, and two cleared out-pointers. If that returns 0x8000000000000005 it allocates a buffer of the size the failed call reported, zeroes it through 0x0001b544, and repeats the same call into that buffer, freeing the buffer and returning 0 if the repeat also fails. On every exit path the intermediate strings are passed to the entry at offset 0x48 of the table at 0x00029478.

name: get_string_from_0x29510_protocol_with_retry
comment: Resolves the interface whose GUID is at 0x00023870 into the global at 0x00029510 the first time it is needed, through the entry at offset 0x140 of the table at 0x00029478, and returns 0 if the lookup fails or leaves the global null. If the third argument is a non-zero buffer it is used directly; otherwise the method at offset 8 of the interface is called with (interface, a cleared qword, an out-pointer, the byte 1, the second argument, the first argument), and a non-negative status returns a fresh 2-byte zeroed allocation from 0x0001b544. A status of 0x8000000000000005 instead leads to a 0x0001b544 allocation of the size reported in the out-pointer, which is then used as the buffer. The method at offset 8 is finally called with (interface, cleared qword, buffer, a byte set from whether the third argument was null, second argument, first argument) and the buffer pointer is zeroed if that call fails.

name: format_string_pair_from_hii_string
comment: Calls 0x000212F0 with a null third argument and returns 0 if it yields a null pointer. It measures the NUL-terminated 16-bit string at 0x00028BE0 and the returned string, adds their two byte lengths plus 4, allocates that many zeroed bytes through 0x0001b544, and formats into it through 0x0001c0f8 with the format at 0x00028B98 and the 16-bit string at 0x00028BE0 as the argument; the returned string is freed through the entry at offset 0x48 of the table at 0x00029478. If the allocation is non-null it calls the method at offset 0x20 of the interface cached in 0x000294F8 with (that interface, the formatted string, the fourth argument, and two out-pointers), frees the string, and returns whether that status was non-negative.

name: format_string_with_optional_suffix
comment: Two paths build a format buffer. With a null fifth argument the buffer size is the byte length of the 16-bit string at 0x00028BE0 plus 0x42, and the format used is the one at 0x00028BA8. With a non-null fifth argument the size is the combined byte lengths of the strings at 0x00028BE0 and at that argument plus 2, and the format used is the one at 0x00026398. Either way the buffer is zeroed through 0x0001b544 and filled through 0x0001c0f8 with the 16-bit string at 0x00028BE0 as the argument, and a null allocation returns 0. It then calls the method at offset 0x18 of the interface cached in 0x000294F8 with (that interface, the formatted string, the fourth argument, the third argument, a pointer to the fifth argument, and an out-pointer), frees the string, and returns 0 if that status was negative or the out-pointer is null. Otherwise it measures the string at 0x00028BE0, calls 0x000212F0 with (first argument, second argument, the out-pointer advanced past that measured length), frees the out-pointer, and returns whether the result was non-null.

name: alloc_byte_buffer_context
comment: Allocates 0x18 bytes through 0x0001b514. If that fails it returns 0. Otherwise it allocates 0x200 bytes the same way, stores the second pointer at offset 0 of the structure, and on failure frees the 0x18-byte block through the entry at offset 0x48 of the table at 0x00029478 and returns 0. On success it zeroes the qword at offset 0x10 and writes 0x200 at offset 8 before returning the structure pointer. The three fields the callers use are the buffer pointer at +0, a limit or capacity at +8 and a running length at +0x10.

name: free_byte_buffer_context
comment: Takes the structure from 0x00021668. If its first qword is non-null it is passed to the entry at offset 0x48 of the table at 0x00029478, and the structure itself is then passed to the same entry by a tail JMP through that offset.

name: reserve_bytes_in_buffer
comment: Reads the running length at offset 0x10 and the field at offset 8 of the structure, adds the requested count, and compares the sum against the field at offset 8. If the sum is not within it, it calls 0x0001b5b0 with the current buffer, the old running length, the requested count plus 0x200, and the old buffer pointer, stores the result as the new buffer, and adds requested-count-plus-0x200 to the field at offset 8. It then returns the new buffer pointer plus the old running length and advances the running length at offset 0x10 by the requested count. 0x0001b5b0 itself allocates through 0x0001b514, zeroes the allocation, copies the smaller of the two lengths from the old pointer, and frees the old pointer, so this realloc preserves the existing contents.

name: append_typed_frame_to_buffer
comment: Writes the byte third argument to the caller's buffer and computes a second byte as (fifth argument + fourth argument) & 0x7F, ORed with (sixth argument << 7), storing it at buffer+1. It then calls 0x000216EC on the structure with that second byte's low 7 bits as the count, and when the fourth argument is non-zero and the reserved address differs from the caller's buffer it copies the fourth argument's bytes there through 0x000002e0. So the second byte carries both a length and a flag in its two bit fields, but what either selects is not decoded further here.

name: append_raw_bytes_to_buffer
comment: Calls 0x000216EC on the structure with the third argument as the count, and when that count is non-zero and the reserved address differs from the second argument copies the third argument's bytes there through 0x000002e0. Unlike 0x00021748 this writes no type byte and no length byte of its own.

name: append_type_9_frame_with_arg
comment: Zeroes a 0x1C-byte local buffer, stores the 16-bit second argument at its offset 2, the third argument masked with 0x30 at its offset 4, a zero byte at offset 5, and one byte copied from the caller's own stack at offset 6, then calls 0x00021748 with (structure, that buffer, 9, 7, 0, 0).

name: append_type_5f_frame_from_globals
comment: Zeroes a 0x12-byte local buffer, copies the qword at 0x000234D0 to its offset 2 and the qword at 0x000234D8 to its offset 0xA, then calls 0x00021748 with (structure, that buffer, 0x5F, 0x12, 3, 0). The fifth argument of 3 is added into the length byte, so the length field is 0x15 with bit 7 clear.

name: append_type3_record
comment: Zeroes 8 bytes of stack with the fill routine at 0x340, writes the 16-bit DX argument into the record at +2, the constant 2 at +4 and the 16-bit fourth argument at +6, then calls 0x21748 with the first argument, the record, the type byte 3, the length 8, a zero and a zero. What the writer does with those six arguments, and what the record or the type value 3 denotes, is not decoded here.

name: filter_records_by_type_and_id
comment: Walks a record array whose first dword is a length masked to 24 bits, copying each record (the length in the byte at +5 masked with 0x7f) into the output buffer through the copy at 0x2E0. A record whose type byte at +4 is 0x0E sets one flag when the qwords at +6 and +0xE both match the 16 bytes at 0x249C8, and a record whose type byte is 0x01 or 0x5D sets a second flag when the 2 bytes at +6 match the DX argument; when both are set the record is also compared, through the bounded compare at 0x2C0, against the entry reached through the fourth argument. On a match the bytes that follow the matched entry are appended, and a dword whose top byte is the old one's and whose low 24 bits are the new length is written back through the sixth argument. Returns 0, or 0x800000000000000E when the 24-bit count reaches the running offset. The record format is not decoded further here.

name: rewrite_records_in_stored_buffer
comment: Reads a buffer through the service table at 0x29508, entry +0x20, keyed by the value at 0x29440; on 0x8000000000000005 it maps the status to a name string with 0x1B514 and retries with that string, and fails with 0x8000000000000009 if the name is not found. It lays out two zeroed buffers with 0x1B544, copies the 0x14-byte header from the fetched buffer, takes the total size from the dword at +0x10, and walks the records that follow at +0x14, each with a dword length masked to 24 bits; a record whose byte at +3 is 0x02 is passed to 0x21A60 with the second, third, fourth and fifth arguments and a destination buffer, and a non-negative result switches the source to that destination and sets a flag. If any record was rewritten, the new total is stored in the header's dword at +0x10 and the buffer is written back through the same table's +0x10 entry; the three buffers are then freed through the entry at 0x29478+0x48. The 0x14-byte header and the record format are not decoded further here.

name: get_or_allocate_service_buffer
comment: Calls the entry at 0x294E8+0x18 with the handle in RCX, a zeroed 8-byte local as the output pointer and its address as the size pointer. If that returns 0x8000000000000005 it allocates a buffer of the reported size with 0x1B544, calls the same entry again with that buffer, returns it, and frees it through 0x29478+0x48 if the second call fails; any other status from the first call returns 0 with no buffer allocated. The service and the buffer's contents are not decoded here.

name: open_interfaces_on_all_matching_handles
comment: Returns 0 unless the qword at +8 of the structure the global at 0x29270 points to equals 1; it then asks the entry at 0x29498+0x40 for a 0x7D8-byte buffer (called as (4, 0x7D8, &buffer)) and reads two values into it through 0x1EA50 with the strings at 0x262C8 and 0x28C50. The entry at 0x29498+0x138 is called as (2, &0x236A0, 0, &count, &array) to collect handles, and each handle is put through 0xC2BC, 0xBC4C and 0xC464 to produce a child list whose entries are opened with the entry at 0x29498+0x118 against the 16 bytes at 0x23790. The fourth argument selects the protocol: 0x27F5 opens the 16 bytes at 0x253B8, calls the interface method at +8, stores a smaller dword at +0x730 of the 0x7D8-byte buffer, commits it through 0x1EBD4 with the string at 0x262C8, and calls the methods at +0x10 and +0x18 when the interface's own +0x10 result differs from +0x730; 0x27F6 opens the 16 bytes at 0x253C8 and calls the method at +8 or the one at +0x10 according to the byte at +0x734. The two flag bytes are committed at the end through 0x1EBD4 with the string at 0x28C50, and the function returns the last status it saw. It is the multi-handle form of 0x222B8, whose per-handle work it repeats.

name: poll_reg20_bit1c
comment: Reads the dword at +0x20 of the structure in RCX and tests bit 0x1C. While the bit is clear it delays 50 through 0x1F9B8 and reads the dword again, up to 4000 times, then returns 0x8000000000000012; it returns 0 as soon as the bit is set. The dword and the bit are named here only by their offset and position; what the structure is and why 0x1C is the bit of interest are not decoded here.

name: build_16byte_template_and_fields
comment: Builds a 16-byte value on the stack, the dword 0x120307E5 followed by the qword 0x14380A, and when the global at 0x294A0 is non-null passes its address and a zero to the entry at 0x294A0+0x18, then clears byte 7 and bytes 8 to 15 of it. The 16 bytes are copied into the caller's buffer by 0x233D0, after which the buffer is given the word 0x7D0 at +0 when bit 3 of the second argument is set, the dword 0x18 at +0x10, the dword 0x0EF10200 at +0x14, and the two qwords read from 0x23600 and 0x23608 at +0x18 and +0x20. What the structure denotes is not decoded here.

name: count_blocks_matching_guid_table
comment: Rejects a size above 0x70000 or a null buffer with 0x800000000000001A, then walks blocks whose length is the dword at +0x10: each is compared byte for byte against the nine 16-byte values at 0x256E0 by 0x1EDD4, and a block counts only if it matched one of them, its length is between 0x2D and 0x70000, and the dword at +0x14 is zero; otherwise 0x800000000000001A is returned. Each accepted block adds one to the block count and, when its length exceeds 0x1C, one more for every dword at +0x18 added in from offset 0x1C, and the two counts are written through the fourth and third arguments when they are non-null. The GUID table and the block layout are not decoded further here.

name: fill_random_u64_retry10
comment: Calls 0x483 with the caller's pointer as RCX, up to ten times, and returns 1 as soon as a call leaves AL non-zero; if all ten calls report failure it returns 0, which is what 0x483 leaves in EAX on that path. 0x483 is a single rdrand that stores the 64-bit result through RCX and returns 1 only when the carry flag came back set, so the loop around it is the RDRAND-retry idiom. What the caller does with the value is not decoded here.

name: append_8byte_record_to_list
comment: Builds an 8-byte record on the stack — 0x19, the frame byte at +1 masked with 0x82, 0x12, the frame byte at +3 masked with 0x06, then the 16-bit second and third arguments — reserves 8 bytes in the caller's list through 0x216EC and copies the record in with 0x2E0 unless the reservation returned the stack address itself. The decompile shows the two masked bytes as the constants 0x82 and 0x06; the listing ORs them with two bytes of the local frame whose values are not decoded here, and the record's meaning is not decoded either.

name: append_2byte_record_to_list
comment: Stores the word 0x229 on the stack, reserves 2 bytes in the caller's list through 0x216EC and copies that word in with 0x2E0 unless the reservation returned the stack address itself. The value 0x229 and the list are not decoded here.

name: select_table_by_flag_2
comment: Calls 0x1B6E0 and, when it returns 2, writes the dword 0x0F to the caller's out-pointer and returns the address 0x25970; otherwise it writes 0x11 and returns 0x25770. What 0x1B6E0 tests to produce that 2, and what either table holds, is not decoded here.

name: validate_packed_value_against_table
comment: Calls 0x1B6E0 and computes 4 minus whether the result is 2, then requires the top byte of the argument to equal that value (3 or 4). On a match it takes the table and count from 0x231A0, checks the argument's second byte against that count, and checks the argument's low 16 bits against the word at table + 0x1C + second_byte * 0x1E, returning 1 only when both checks pass and 0 otherwise. The argument's layout and the table's contents are not decoded here.

name: read_table_entry_dword
comment: Calls 0x231A0 for the table, forms the row address as table + (the argument's second byte) * 0x1E, adds 16 * (the argument's low 16 bits) to the word at row + 0x1A, ORs the byte at row + 0 with 0xFD00, shifts that left by 16 and reads the dword at the resulting 16-bit-aligned address, which it returns. The table's layout is not decoded further here.

name: extract_two_bit_field_from_table
comment: Validates the argument with 0x231D4 and returns 0x8000000000000002 when that fails. Otherwise it takes the table from 0x231A0, forms the row as table + (the argument's second byte) * 0x1E, builds a 16-bit address from (row byte 0 OR 0xFD00) shifted left by 16 combined with the word at row + 2 plus 4 * (the argument shifted right by 3), reads the dword there, and writes ((3 << ((argument & 7) * 4)) AND that dword) shifted right by ((argument & 7) * 4) through the second argument, returning 0. The table's layout is not decoded further here.

name: fill_memory_byte
comment: Destination in RCX, fill byte in RDX, count in R8 — the opposite order from the 0x2337E entry that shares this body, which the decompile does not distinguish. This listing stops after that shuffle and a jump to 0x2338A, so the rest of the body is visible only in 0x2337E's listing: the fill byte is broadcast into AX/BX, the destination is brought up to a 4-byte boundary with a stosb.rep, the bulk is written with stosd.rep, and the final count & 3 bytes go out with stosb.rep.

name: set_memory_bytes
comment: Destination in RCX, count in RDX, fill byte in R8. The fill byte is broadcast into AX and BX and duplicated into the upper half of RAX, the destination is brought up to a 4-byte boundary with stosb.rep, count>>2 dwords go out with stosd.rep, and the remaining count & 3 bytes with stosb.rep.

name: memmove_bytes_33d0
comment: memmove: destination in RCX, source in RDX, length in R8. It computes source - destination and, only when the destination lies at or below source + length (so the ranges overlap), moves both pointers to their last byte, sets DF and copies backwards with movsb.rep; otherwise it copies forwards, first with movsb.rep over the difference between the two pointers' remainders modulo 8 when those match, then length>>3 qwords with movsq.rep, then the remainder with movsb.rep. Returns the original destination in RAX.

name: entry_clamp_status
comment: Calls FFCFBB55 and tests the EAX result: a negative return is passed through unchanged, any non-negative return is zeroed before the ret. The module entry therefore yields either 0 or the callee's negative error code to the PEI dispatcher.

name: read_pad_config_word
comment: Selects a 16-bit offset from a pad's 0x1E-byte record with the jump table at 0xFFF81290 indexed by ECX 0..7, reading the word at record offset 0x04, 0x0C, 0x0A, 0x10, 0x0E, 0x14, 0x16 or 0x18 respectively; if that word is 0xFFFF, or ECX exceeds 7, it stores 0 through the pointer at [EBP+0x0C]. Otherwise it adds the stack argument times 4 (times 8 for ECX 6 and 7) to the selected word, ORs the 16-bit sum with (the record's first byte OR 0xFFFFFD00) shifted left 16, and stores the dword read at the resulting 32-bit address through that same pointer.

name: set_pad_index6_or_7_word
comment: Accepts only ECX 6 or 7 and otherwise returns 0x80000003. For 6 it reads the word at offset 0x16 of the pad's 0x1E-byte record and calls 0xFFF813F1, for 7 the word at offset 0x18 and 0xFFF8146C, and returns 0x80000003 again if that word is 0xFFFF. Otherwise it ANDs the value the callee wrote with [EBP+0x0C], ORs in [EBP+0x10], takes the record's first byte as the low byte of ECX, and calls 0xFFF81B00 with the sum of the record word and [EBP+0x8] times 8, a zero, a pointer to a byte at [EBP-0x01] and 0x13, returning its status.

name: set_composite_pad_value
comment: Runs two checks in order: 0xFFF819A6 must accept the composite pad number in ECX or it returns 0x80000002, then 0xFFF8198F, which calls 0xFFF81387 and tests the result for zero, must report zero or it returns 0x80000003. On success it calls 0xFFF819FE with the same ECX and EDX and returns 0.

name: read_pad_bit_field
comment: After 0xFFF819A6 accepts the composite pad number in ECX, or 0x80000002 is returned, it takes byte 2 of ECX as the pad index and bytes 0-1 as the field index. It reads the word at offset 0x02 of the pad's 0x1E-byte record plus (field index >> 3) * 4, ORs that with (the record's first byte OR 0xFFFFFD00) shifted left 16, reads the dword at the resulting address, and stores the 3 bits at shift (field index & 7) * 4 through the pointer that was in EDX.

name: read_index6_word
comment: Calls 0xFFF8117F with the pad number in ECX and the index in EDX and returns 0x80000002 if that rejects them; otherwise it calls 0xFFF811CC with ECX forced to 6, the same EDX and the two stack arguments, so the value comes from the record word at offset 0x16, and returns 0.

name: read_index7_word
comment: Calls 0xFFF8117F with the pad number in ECX and the index in EDX and returns 0x80000002 if that rejects them; otherwise it calls 0xFFF811CC with ECX forced to 7, the same EDX and the two stack arguments, so the value comes from the record word at offset 0x18, and returns 0.

name: clear_index6_bits
comment: Calls 0xFFF8117F and returns 0x80000002 if it rejects the pad number and index, otherwise calls 0xFFF812B0 with ECX = 6, the pointer that was in EDX, the bitwise complement of its stack argument and 0, and returns that status.

name: write_index6_mask
comment: Calls 0xFFF8117F and returns 0x80000002 if it rejects the pad number and index, otherwise calls 0xFFF812B0 with ECX = 6, the pointer that was in EDX, its stack argument unchanged and 0xFFFFFFFF, and returns that status.

name: write_index6_bit
comment: Splits its argument into a pad index (bits 16 and above), a bit number (bits 0-4) and a field index (bits 5-15), forms the mask 1 << (bits 0-4), and calls 0xFFF81517 with ECX = the pad index, EDX = the field index and the mask pushed on the stack, discarding the status that comes back.

name: clear_index7_bits
comment: Calls 0xFFF8117F and returns 0x80000002 if it rejects the pad number and index, otherwise calls 0xFFF812B0 with ECX = 7, the pointer that was in EDX, the bitwise complement of its stack argument and 0, and returns that status.

name: write_index7_mask
comment: Calls 0xFFF8117F and returns 0x80000002 if it rejects the pad number and index, otherwise calls 0xFFF812B0 with ECX = 7, the pointer that was in EDX, its stack argument unchanged and 0xFFFFFFFF, and returns that status.

name: compute_max_entry_bound
comment: Calls 0xFFF81ADD to get the record table's base in EAX and its entry count through the pointer in ECX, subtracts one from that count and passes the result to 0xFFF815DD, returning ((0xFFF81640() != 0) + 3) << 8 ORed with the decremented count. The count is 0x0F or 0x11 depending on what 0xFFF81640 returns.

name: compute_min_entry_bound
comment: Returns ((0xFFF81640() != 0) + 3) << 8 ORed with its ECX argument, i.e. 0x300 or 0x400 with the low eight bits supplied by the caller. The two possible values differ by the single bit 0x0400 that 0xFFF81640 contributes.

name: classify_device_id
comment: Reads the 16-bit value at 0xE00F8002, masks it with 0xFFE0 and maps 0x0280 and 0x9D80 to 2, 0x0680 and 0xA300 to 1, and everything else to 0xFF. The result is cached in the byte at 0xFFF81D2C, and any cached value other than 0xFF is returned in AL without re-reading 0xE00F8002.

name: is_device_class_2
comment: Calls 0xFFF815F6 and returns 1 in AL if the classification is 2, 0 otherwise.
