name: is_device_class_1
comment: Calls 0xFFF815F6 and returns 1 in AL if the classification is 1, 0 otherwise.

name: swap_dword_halves
comment: Returns the 64-bit value whose high half is (second argument >> 16) and whose low half is (first argument >> 16) | (second argument << 16), built with SHRD and a shared shift of 0x10. The shift count comes from a stack local set to 0x10 and tested against 0x20, which is never set, so the swap always runs.

name: write_cfg_magic_word
comment: Calls 0xFFF81C08; if that is set and the top 16 bits of the dword at 0xE00F80A8 are 0xFE41 it skips 0xFFF81C26, otherwise it calls 0xFFF81C26 and returns 0x80000003 when that reports non-zero. It then stores 0xFE410001 at 0xFD882740, reads the dword at 0xE00F8098, clears bit 0 and writes it straight back, and immediately overwrites the same location with 0xFE410001 before returning 0, so the cleared value is never observed by anything in this module.

name: write_port_0x66
comment: Waits for bit 1 of the byte in port 0x66 to clear, delaying with 0xFFF81948 called with 0x0F between reads and giving up with 0x80000007 after 0x20000 iterations. Otherwise it writes the byte it was given in DL to port 0x66 and returns 0.

name: write_port_0x62
comment: Waits for bit 1 of the byte in port 0x66 to clear, delaying with 0xFFF81948 called with 0x0F between reads and giving up with 0x80000007 after 0x20000 iterations. Otherwise it writes the byte it was given in DL to port 0x62 and returns 0.

name: drain_port_0x62_to_0x80
comment: While bit 0 of the byte in port 0x66 is set, reads a byte from port 0x62, writes it to port 0x80, delays with 0xFFF81948 called with 0x1388 and re-reads port 0x66, up to 0x20000 times. Returns 0 once the bit is clear, or 0x80000007 if it is still set after that many iterations.

name: wait_for_port_0x66_bit1
comment: Polls bit 1 of the byte in port 0x66, calling 0xFFF81948 with 0x0F between reads, and returns 0 as soon as the bit is clear or 0x80000007 after 0x20000 iterations with it still set.

name: write_two_bytes_via_0x66_0x62
comment: Calls 0xFFF8185E and, only if that returns non-negative, runs 0xFFF81814, 0xFFF81783 with the byte it was given in DL, 0xFFF8185E, 0xFFF817CA with the byte from its first stack argument, and 0xFFF81814 again, that is, it drains port 0x62 into port 0x80, writes the first byte to port 0x66, then the second to port 0x62, draining after each. It returns the first call's status and ignores the four that follow.

name: write_three_bytes_via_0x66_0x62
comment: Calls 0xFFF81899 three times, with the second byte 0x07 every time and the first byte 0xA3, then 0xA2, then 0xA5; the second and third calls take their second byte from the two stack arguments. It stops at the first negative status and returns it, or 0 if all three succeed, so the two bytes reaching ports 0x66 and 0x62 are 0xA3/0x07, then 0xA2 with the first argument, then 0xA5 with the second.

name: delay_1808_counter
comment: Runs (ECX >> 0x16) + 1 passes, each reading the 32-bit counter at port 0x1808, adding (ECX & 0x3FFFFF) to its low 24 bits and then spinning on port 0x1808 until the difference from that target has bit 0x800000 set. The inner spin has no iteration limit, and the value left in EAX is not meaningful on return.

name: scale_count_then_busy_wait
comment: It takes the incoming ECX count, forms a 64-bit intermediate of it times the constant 0x369e99, divides the high and low dwords of that product by 0xf4240 (one million) and passes the low quotient to 0xfff818ff in ECX; the high quotient is computed and discarded. The unscaled count is returned unchanged in EAX. The unit the incoming count is expressed in is not determined by these instructions.

name: is_callee_out_value_zero
comment: It calls 0xfff81387 with EDX pointing at a stack local, discards the status that call returns in EAX, and returns 1 if the dword left in that local is zero and 0 if it is not. The local is never initialised here, so on any path where the callee does not write it the comparison is against whatever the stack held.

name: check_selector_within_table_range
comment: It validates a packed selector passed in ECX against a table obtained from 0xfff81add. The selector's top byte must equal 3 plus the nonzero-ness of the call to 0xfff81640; the byte at bits 23:16 must be below the entry count that call writes through the local; and the low 16 bits must be below the 16-bit word at (base + index*0x1e + 0x1c) from the base the second call returns. It returns 1 only when all three tests pass and 0 otherwise. What the table describes is not decoded here.

name: set_bitfield_in_mapped_register
comment: Given a packed selector in ECX and a 32-bit value in the second argument, it derives the address of a 32-bit word from the table 0xfff81add returns: index (selector >> 16 & 0xff) selects a 0x1e-byte record whose byte 0 is OR'd with 0xfffffd00 (0xfd00 in the low half) for the top 16 bits while the signed 16-bit at +0x1a is added to (selector << 4) for the low 16; the dword there is read, cleared of bit 0, OR'd with the whole value argument, and written back. A 1 << (selector & 0x1f) mask is additionally passed to 0xfff814e7 and 0xfff81565 with selector >> 16 in ECX, and after the store 0xfff81544 is called with the selector in ECX and 0xfff81595 with the same mask, each of the four gated on a dword left in a local by the preceding call to 0xfff8141d or 0xfff81498. What those five routines do with the mask, and the contents and meaning of the table and of the 0xfd00xxxx range it points into, are not decoded in this listing.

name: select_table_by_platform_predicate
comment: It moves the caller's pointer into EDX, calls 0xfff81640, and on a nonzero result writes 0x0f through that pointer and returns the base 0xfff81f34 in EAX; on a zero result it writes 0x11 and returns 0xfff81d34. It is a pure choice between two constant bases and their matching counts; neither table's contents are decoded here.

name: check_flag_bit12_after_predicate
comment: It returns 1 only when the call to 0xfff8164f returned nonzero and bit 12 of the dword at 0xfd72c210 is set, and 0 when either test fails. Nothing is written, and that dword's meaning is not documented in this repository.

name: read_flag_bit_from_selected_dword
comment: Which of two memory-mapped dwords it reads is chosen by the call to 0xfff8164f: on a nonzero return it extracts bit 23 of the dword at 0xfd8820d8, and otherwise bit 31 of the dword at 0xfd882234. The return is 0 or 1 in both cases. Neither dword's meaning is documented in this repository.

name: read_config_word_via_cf8_cfc
comment: It reads 16 bits through the 0xcf8/0xcfc port pair: it saves EFLAGS, executes CLI, saves the dword at port 0xcf8, writes 0x80000000 | ((ECX >> 4) & 0xffff00) | (ECX & 0xfc) to port 0xcf8 to select, then reads 16 bits from port 0xcfc or 0xcfe (0xcfc + (ECX & 2)), and restores the saved dword to port 0xcf8. STI follows only if the saved flags had IF set, so the sequence leaves interrupts as it found them. The value comes back in AX while the upper half of EAX still holds the saved 0xcf8 read; what packing the caller's ECX uses is not determined by these instructions.

name: write_config_word_via_cf8_cfc
comment: It writes the 16-bit value in DX to port 0xcfc or 0xcfe (0xcfc + (ECX & 2)), after selecting the register with 0x80000000 | ((ECX >> 4) & 0xffff00) | (ECX & 0xfc) written to port 0xcf8, and then restores the dword it had saved from 0xcf8 before that selection. It saves EFLAGS, executes CLI for the sequence, and executes STI only if the saved flags had IF set. The value written is returned in AX, with the upper half of EAX still holding the saved 0xcf8 read; what packing the caller's ECX uses is not determined by these instructions.

name: module_entry_dispatch_services
comment: Module entry. It ignores its first argument, takes a service table pointer as its second, and makes two two-argument calls through offset 0x24 of that pointer's first dword, passing the constants at 0xFFF82AFC and 0xFFF82B08. It then calls 0xFFF8254F, makes a five-argument call at offset 0x20 with 0xFFF82ACC, 0, 0 and the address of its own second argument slot, and passes the dword that call leaves there, together with the constant 1000000, to a three-argument call at offset 0x04. Returns 0. Which service table these three offsets belong to is not established here, and this listing does not decode the three constants.

name: set_config_and_mmio_bit11
comment: Two 16-bit PCI configuration-space read-modify-writes through 0xCF8/0xCFC, plus two 16-bit word accesses. It reads the word at encoded config address 0xF8080 and writes the identical value back, and reads the word at 0xFD882770 and rewrites it unchanged, so neither of those two changes a value. It then reads the word at encoded config address 0xF8082, ORs 0x800 into it and writes it back, and separately ORs 0x800 into the 16-bit word at 0xFD882774 and stores that. A ten-entry constant table (0x02F803F8 first) is built on the stack and never read in this function; what device the two config addresses select, and what 0xFD882774 is, are not established in this repository.

name: ec_drain_obf
comment: While bit 0 of the port chosen by CL (0x64 when CL is 0x60, otherwise 0x66) is set, reads the companion port (0x60 or 0x62) and writes each byte read to port 0x80, then calls the counter delay at 0xFFF828BD with 0x1388 before re-polling; at most 0x20000 iterations. Returns 0, or 0x80000007 if the loop runs out of iterations. The writes to port 0x80 are the only observable side effect of the drain; nothing in this listing says what port 0x80 is for.

name: ec_wait_ibf_clear
comment: Waits for bit 1 of the port chosen by CL (0x64 when CL is 0x60, otherwise 0x66) to clear, up to 0x20000 polls with a 0xF delay at 0xFFF828BD between them. Returns 0, or 0x80000007 if the bit is still set at the limit. This is the wait 0xFFF825FC, 0xFFF82657 and 0xFFF8277F use before touching the same port pair, and the only difference from 0xFFF825FC is that this one writes nothing when the bit clears.

name: ec_write_command_data
comment: One write transaction on the port pair selected by CL, in order: 0xFFF8272D waits for bit 1, 0xFFF826C0 drains, 0xFFF825FC writes the command byte from DL to the 0x64/0x66 port, 0xFFF8272D waits for bit 1 again, 0xFFF82657 writes the byte the caller pushed on the stack to the 0x60/0x62 port, and 0xFFF826C0 drains again. Only the first call's result is tested and returned; the other five are called for effect. The command byte is the caller's argument and is not named in this function, so which EC register a given call reaches is not decidable from this listing.

name: ec_read_reg_0741
comment: Reads one byte from the 0x62/0x66 pair into the pointer it is given. It writes command 0xA3 with data 0x07 and command 0xA2 with data 0x41 through 0xFFF8277F, writes 0xA4 to port 0x66 through 0xFFF825FC, then spins on port 0x66 until bit 0 is set (up to 0x20000 polls, a 0xF delay at 0xFFF828BD each) and reads the byte from port 0x62. Returns 0, or the first negative status from the two preceding writes, or 0x80000007 if bit 0 never sets. registers.yaml records the same 0xA3 07 / 0xA2 41 / 0xA4 sequence in OemOcDxe as reading EC register 0x0741, so the 0x0741 in the name is carried over from that sibling rather than observed here.

name: port_1808_counter_delay
comment: Busy-waits on the free-running counter at I/O port 0x1808. It splits ECX into a repeat count (ECX >> 22) and an offset (ECX & 0x3FFFFF), adds the offset to the low 24 bits of the counter as first read, and then re-reads the full 32-bit port until ((target - value) & 0x800000) is non-zero, once per repeat. Callers pass 0xF and 0x1388; what the counter counts, and so what unit the argument is in, is not established here.

name: find_entry_by_16byte_key
comment: Walks a length-prefixed table for an entry whose 16 bytes at entry offset 8 match the 16 bytes at EDX, compared by 0xFFF82A4E. ECX is the table base: the word at +0x1E is the entry count, the word at +0x02 is a length used to reject an entry that would run past the end, and entries start at +0x24 with their own length word at +0x2 advancing the cursor. On a match it stores the entry pointer through its first argument and returns 0; if the count runs out or the bound check fails it returns 0x8000000E. What the 16-byte key identifies is not decoded here.

name: pci_config_read16
comment: Reads the 16-bit PCI configuration word selected by ECX through the 0xCF8/0xCFC pair: it saves the current 0xCF8 value, clears interrupts, computes ((ECX >> 4) & 0xFFFF00) | (ECX & 0xFC) | 0x80000000, writes that to 0xCF8, reads 16 bits from 0xCFC (0xCFE when bit 1 of ECX is set), restores the saved 0xCF8 value, and restores the interrupt-enable flag to what it was on entry. Returns the word in AX. The decompiled C for this address shows the 0xCF8/0xCFC traffic but drops the interrupt save, the enable bit and the restore.

name: pci_config_write16
comment: The write half of 0xFFF82997, with the same save of 0xCF8, interrupt clear, address computation and restores of both. It writes the 16-bit value in DX to 0xCFC, or to 0xCFE when bit 1 of ECX is set, and returns that value in AX. The decompiled C for this address does not show that the value arrives in DX, and its return value is a packed 0xCF8 constant rather than the word written.

name: compare_16bytes
comment: Compares the 16 bytes at ECX against the 16 bytes at EDX as four consecutive dwords, returning AL = 1 if all four match and AL = 0 at the first that does not. Its only caller in this module is 0xFFF82904, which uses it to match a 16-byte key; the shape matches a UEFI GUID comparison, but nothing in this listing names the value being compared.

name: forward_vtable_0x24_call
comment: PEI entry that takes a caller-supplied interface pointer as its second argument, loads the vtable pointer from it and calls the method at vtable offset 0x24 with (interface, 0xFFF82EAC), popping both pushed words and returning 0. The contents of the data at 0xFFF82EAC and the identity of the vtable slot at offset 0x24 are not decoded by this listing.

name: get_variable_and_fill_tables
comment: Takes a vtable pointer in EDX and calls vtable+0x20 with (vtable, 0xFFFAC688, 0, 0, &interface); on a non-negative result it sets a size of 0xB4 and calls the located interface's vtable slot 0 with six arguments (interface, 0xFFFACAE8, 0xFFFAC6B8, 0, &size, buffer at EBP-0xBC), which is the argument layout of a UEFI variable read, though the protocol located by 0xFFFAC688 is not identified here. It then fills 10 dwords at 0xFFFACA50 and 53 dwords at 0xFFFAC6F0 with the first dword of the returned data, calls 0xFFFAC462, stores the dword at 0xFFFACB28 to 0xFFFAC6F0 + 16*byte[0xFFFACB24], calls 0xFFFAC5BA with ECX 0xFFFAC6D0 and again with ECX 0xFFFACA38, and returns 0. A negative return from the vtable+0x20 call is returned unchanged; a negative return from the six-argument call still yields 0.

name: call_vtable_slot_0x18_1_arg
comment: Executes SIDT, reads the 32-bit word stored at (IDT base - 4), dereferences that word once, and calls the function pointer at offset 0x18 of the result with two arguments: the word itself and the value in ECX. It discards the return value. What that word points at, and therefore which service is dispatched, is not decoded in this listing.

name: call_vtable_slot_0x20_5_args
comment: Performs the same SIDT-based pointer fetch as 0xFFFAC5BA but calls the function pointer at offset 0x20 with five arguments: the fetched word, the GUID pointer in ECX, two literal zeros, and its own first stack argument; its second stack argument is never read. It returns EAX unchanged. The callee is reachable only through the word below the IDT, so the service it names cannot be identified here; its callers in this module pass the GUIDs at 0xFFFAC688 and 0xFFFAC698 in ECX and read an interface pointer out of a stack slot after the call.
